location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Enter via the security gate opposite the Queens Hotel. Walk up the pathway to the temple. Not well signed but the automatic cash ticket machine is round the corner to the right, really easy to use. You need to go back to the front entrance to leave your shoes at the booth ( they give you a number for collection). Enjoy at your leisure. We went early to avoid the crowds we were told would be there for an 11.00 ceremony (people seemed to be queueing for this at 9.00).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: One of the best known and prestigious Buddhist Temples in Sri Lanka. If one is interested in the development of human history missing a visit to this temple, the history architecture and annual so called Kandy Perahera  or huge procession with hundreds of fully decorated elephants will certainly be regrettable. An absolute must for both history buffs and the intelligent :-) curious. Best wishes

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Turned away at the gates by the guards for having shorts on. I was going to give the whole thing a miss until i spotted a strategically placed market stall selling wrap/sarongs by the entrance. It’s not your first rodeo sister - 2000rp’s gone just like that - rather proud I got the price down ever so slightly. ‘Fine cotten best in Kandy’ though so I think I’m a winner? Lucky I stumbled on the best market stall. As I was now suitably wrapped up I entered and walked down the lovely path to the front entrance. To my amusement and slightly relief every other tourist male who misjudged the shorts policy was also sporting a sarong - same market as mine? If so it’s best cotton in Kandy so they should be fortunate. We took our shoes off and paid 100rupees to keep them safe in an outhouse. We then tried to enter the temple but alas we had no ticket - there’s no signs or any information on where to find tickets so it was like bambi on ice watching middle aged white men walk barefoot around the grounds to the ticket counter - 1500rupees and a stone in the heel I was in! Really glad I took the pilgrimage to the ticket counter as this was a real thing of beauty, the ceiling, walls and floors were expertly decorated in colour. As we entered the room of the Buddha I was surprised to see around 50 worshipers sharing a prayer on the hallowed ground. A lovely sight and with A LOT of ‘no camera’ signs it was less than pleasant to see the majority of tourists taking photos as if we were witnessing a new phenomenon - classless. The cherry on the cake, however, was a Chinese tour guide decided to take his group and walk through the worshipers and talking over the prayers - it was potentially one of the worst things I’ve ever witnessed in my life and shame on every single person who participated. Overall lovely hour spent wondering around the grounds - shame the ‘no photography’ signs were not obeyed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Quite a few steps to walk up, At times we felt we intruding in the religious ceremonies, A very popular tourist attraction, with coach loads of people arriving, lots of pushing, some people just so very rude.After all I have said it was still worth seeing, try not to go on a bank holiday.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Standard temple except for the ceremonial aspects. An area that leads to the relic storage room is roped off and a couple of guys bang away at drums while a few officials open the door and disappear inside for a fair while. Eventually they come out again and the crowd surges up the stairway to the relic viewing room. There, those in the know, join a long queue to get a view into the relic room. This is where the scuffles start. Some cheeky visitors jump under the rope containing the queue and break in while others just get on the end and hope for the best. The majority, however, congregate in a large scrum trying to see over all the heads at the relic container. Get ready for some rough and tumble. The other suggestion is to set your camera exposure to a bright setting because the darkness around the room is dramatically contrasted with the bright glow from the relic container through the narrow doorway. My shots just showed a very bright blur of the golden container.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were there at a ?good? time as the tooth was going to be revealed that day. There were 1000's of people pushing, shoving to get a place in line. The tooth was revealed as we were shoved past it, small boys on our shoulders. Wow - not sure I would recommend this one.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Having almost completed the Cultural Triangle, Kandy and this temple were to be the finish. So, we knew all about being respectful, the customs and how to conduct yourself. As a tourist you are stung for the tourist rate of entry and are immediately greeted by a throng of guides, who get bulshy if you decline their offer. You do not need a guide for this by the way. Get a good book. Ladies need their knees and shoulders covered and like all temples, you have to remove your shoes. These are stored in a shed with thousands of other pairs, and you keep praying that they'll be there when you get back! We were politely queuing to file past the casket, but all around us the locals were pushing in, pushing us and showing no regard or respect for anyone or thing. It was a dreadful, disgusting experience and shocking to see, so I'm afraid, but two can play that game. And, when in Rome.... and all that. At the allotted time, the throng shove and do anything to be first to get to the casket. Think rugby scrum and you get some idea. Then as you go past the actual casket you are expected to yet again give money to the monk. You are not allowed to take photos as you file past, however, if you stand opposite the casket opening, away from the filing area, you can take as many as you like! The whole event/experience was not worth either my time or my money and I really would advise you to miss this. There really is not a lot else to see there and the place is heaving with people.  No local showed any respectfulness or politeness to me or the place as we were elbowed in the back. It is clearly religious extortion at it's worst, because although they do not want us there, they clearly want our money. A horrid, disrespectful and shocking experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a very interesting place, with much history, not least the rebuilding of part due to a bomb during the "troubles" which used to best this country. You would not know that there was extensive damage and the repairs are in keeping with the age of the buildings - ie you can't see them. This is an active Buddhist place of worship and it was interesting to see this at first hand, but the ubiquitous selfy picture-taker tends to mar such experiences. For "selfy", I should say, quite often, more "selfish" and lacking in respect. There were clear signs against taking selfies with Buddha icons in the background, but this seemed more ignored than respected. After that bleat, I have to say that this place is very much worth seeing, with many relics and paintings and just the "feel" of the place. Quite special.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited here as part of a coach tour and found the architecture and history interesting. We felt uncomfortable, however, as devout local Buddhists were trying to worship with a constant stream of coach trippers walking through them all the time. And don't expect to see a tooth!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Maybe it's #1 sightseeing in Sri Lanka, historical and religious. But traffic jams are killing your endorsement :) and also be aware that you should cover your legs and arms to visit this place, they don't give you any sheets to cope with that. As of beauty, imho, Thailand temples are much more interesting

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We came excited to see this and waited out  the rain just to enter but we were turned away because my friend wears a hijab and was told because of this she’s not allowed inside. This despite the fact that many people had on scarves on their heads to protect from the rain but being Muslim doesn’t pass muster. Wildly bigoted and ridiculous when we’re politely covered paying tourists like everyone else. I may not be Muslim but that’s no way to treat someone. Won’t be on my list next time. Highly disappointed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple compound itself is beautiful with lots of paintings and sculptures, and it is clearly a deeply spiritual place. The only thing I wished is that there was a little bit more information available somewhere about the history and significance of the place. Once you are there, you are not sure what is what and what you are looking at, so a little reading in advance would help.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We came for the evening ceremony and it was nice, but very crowded. There were donation trays everywhere we looked, even at the viewing of the casket of the tooth. You get rushed through and the monks point at the donation trays wherever you go. Also, at the entrance to the temple gates, a man wouldn’t leave us alone saying that he would be our guide. We agreed to 1,000 rupees for a private tour. He was helpful and informative, but not deeply informative. He told us a lot of information on Buddha and Buddhism that is common knowledge. When our visit (the “tour”) was done, our forced guide wouldn’t leave us alone, asking for more money (up to 3,500 rupees). We had to ignore him and walk away, nearly telling him off and to leave us alone. Overall, the temple is worth visiting. However, be wary of all the donation asking and opportunistic “tour guides.” Also note that the temple used to be a palace, but as there is no longer a monarchy, it has been converted to a “temple,” which for better or worse, is more like a tourist trap. There was no holy nor spiritual aspect to the ceremony or crowded experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Extremely rude and aggressive security at the front entrance checking that the clothing is appropriate. Me and my husband wore the same clothes as in the cave temples but won't allowed in. He wore knee length shorts and I wore a long dress with side splits(covers knees). Security just wave you to the clothes stall nearby to but trousers from locals at 5 times the price of a normal stall. That's the first time in Sri Lanka we found that locals take advantage of tourists. Tickets are too expensive.  Watch videos online and skip this place

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was insanely crowded inside the temple as well as on the grounds around it, so be prepared to fight crowds, be pushed the traditional sri lankan way, or bypass the golden casket for the less crowded outdoors. Too loud to hear tour guide and we were on time constraints so did not get to explore on our own but there looked to be a LOT to explore. Wish we had more time here. Definitely go see it once but be prepared to face the crowds as I said.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We are in Kandy for 2 nights before leaving for Heritance tea factory. We went to the temple with our driver, who is a Buddhist but most of the country is , so not a problem. We came to see the culture and the temple is a very Holy and sacred place for sure , but once inside its just manic and you dont really see much apart from get pushed and crushed and pay for the pleasure around 1500 rupees each was ok but had enough temples for one day .If your not religious once you seen one , you seen them all !

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited at about 11am and it wasn't too busy.  We had read that it gets very busy if attending the early or evening puja when the room housing the tooth is open. It's worth noting that you have to buy a ticket to access the complex (1500Rps) the ticket office is round the opposite side to the shoe drop off and entrance so get your ticket before handing in your shoes. As well as the temple there are museums and other parts to visit. We found the paths extremely hot on bare feet so consider taking a pair of socks or flip flops to save burning your feet.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was a pretty good temple to visit to, try to visit around the time of Puja where you can see the ceremony. Just ignore them and tell them you just want to explore the temple by yourself

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Beautiful temple complex. The most famous temple of Sri Lanka. The relic of the tooth is held here. You can enter the premises for free. To visit the actual temple, a 1500 RS fee is charged. The temple is visited frequently by locals, especially in the weekends. The whole complex is in very good condition and maintained on high standards. You can bring your products to the Buddha, bring water to the holy tree or just stroll around.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Being one of Sri Lankas most important tourist attractions, the Temple is a "Must Visit" when in Kandy. Quite a large complex next to the Kandy Lake, with quite a heavy security presence after the terrorist attacks at the end of the 90s. There is a charge to enter, but already included in our tour so no idea of the cost. Open all day, but the most interesting,and busiest times are early morning or 6.30pm, when the shrine containing the  Golden Caskets, which house the Tooth Relic, is opened for a short time only for public veiwing.  Whilst other religious sites were not so particular about dress code, here they were very strict. Knees and shoulders MUST be covered, hats and shoes removed and good behaviour essential. Our guide took us for the 6.30 ceremony, and as he got us there early we were in a good position to see the actual caskets themselves.  There were literally thousands behind us, most of whom would see nothing.  Whether you are Buddhist or not, you cannot fail to be impressed with the ceremonials and the decor and architecture of the place. We finished our tour by visiting the separate annexe which contains the expertly stuffed Raja, who was the Temples Elephant and quite famous in SL. He died in 1988 Highly Recommended

Arooha tours Sri Lanka has arrange this visit for us during our Sri Lanka trip . Really liked this place!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is an interesting place if you are into the Buddhist religion. You will get to learn about the history behind the temple. In terms of architecture and design I would say that the temples in Bhutan were a lot more interesting. This place felt like it was for those who are really pious followers of buddhism.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is said to hold the Buddha's tooth and there is an elaborate ceremony associated with its regular public display. The crowds on such occasions are substantial however with much pushing and jostling to see the relic. It is worth attending but unless you are a buddhist it is not an unforgettable experience..

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: As a background, we spent many good days visiting the religious sites at Anuradhapura and other places which we enjoyed. This place looks nice but it what we experienced inside was more like a rugby scrum that a place of worship. For a religion that espouses respect and consideration, there seemed to be very little being shown (largely, it has to be said from locals). In the main we have found Sri Lankans to be lovely, but not at this site. Maybe it was brought on by the complete lack of organisation, to deal with the high volumes of people but I have to say we did not enjoy our visit. The pushing, queue jumping, and general physical lack of respect was staggering. Avoid this place if it looks busy.

review_text: Firstly i only give honest reveiws. The entry cost for this religious temple is and i quote "foreigners 1500rp local 20rp".  As with most places in Srilanka you always feel you are being ripped off. You are a tourist and therefore can afford it. The temple...you are required to remove shoes and leave with the shoe store to retrieve later for some rupees. You are also required to wear long trousers and light (preferably white) top for ladies. The entrance has flower seller, selling flowers to offer in respect. Unfortunately if you are Spheksophobic (fear of wasps) run passed. Temple inside is very crowded and you are shuffled through amongst the throng of tourist groups. (reminiscent of the Vatican). There is no tooth on show. It is a casket with the tooth inside allegedly. Spilling outside the grounds are pleasant and inviting, you are however barefoot still. The museum is there but poorly signed but worth a visit if only to get your monies worth. Tip when you want to retrieve your shoes hold ticket with 20rp note for instant shoes. To summarise you dont travel that far and not see it but don't build your hopes, its just a semi pleasant day.

review_text: The Temple of the Tooth in Kandy is probably Sri Lanka’s biggest single temple or monument attraction. So it is a pity that the site is so very difficult to navigate. Do visit but aim to stay than do a day trip.

review_text: When we walked through security we were approached by a freelance guide. Usual story you decide how much. The grounds are expansive. Both outside and inside the ticketed zone. Otherwise the door of the room holding the casket with 7 boxes in which the tooth is held. Opens a few times a day.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: My wife and I paid the LKR1500.00 (£7.50) each to tour the temple in Kandy. We paid for a guide to take us around, however it was only when back in the UK we realised we were entitled to a souvenir DVD (shown in small print on the ticket!) No one pointed this out to us and I suppose thousands of other tourists are duped in the same way. The temple was good but the entrance fee extortionate but may have been worth it dependent on the quality of the DVD. Shame on you Sri Lanka tourist board for being so poor and ripping off tourists!!!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is a must go destination in Kandy. The best time to visit this temple is on a weekday during morning hours. There is a small religious ceremony which happens 3 times a day (morning 5:30 and 9:30 ; evening 6:30), it is only during this time that the tooth relic kept in side the main shrine is open for visit to all. It becomes little crowded during that time, all though the crowd is well managed by temple staff and every one gets a glimpse of the tooth relic. The temple has an entry fee as any other place in Sri Lanka, the entry fee is discounted for SAARC nation nationals. When you are going there do visit the Buddhism museum it is with in the temple complex and is included in the temple entry ticket.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had been been told if we wanted to see the casket with the tooth we needed to arrive at the temple at 5.30am/9.30am/6.30pm/7.45pm, when they have a service and the doors are opened. We ended arriving at 4pm and quickly realised that it would be busy at 6.30pm so chose not to wait. It cost LKR 3000 to enter the temple you buy your tickets from machines at the side of the temple. As for the temple I have to say I was rather underwhelmed and although it has a room that describes the story of the tooth in paintings I think we expected more. Still we ticked it off our list and took a walk around Kandy lake but we found the city so busy we didn't stay long.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I am not sure what those in charge are doing but this sacred temple has turned into a tourist spot during prayer and worship time which completely goes against the teachings of Buddhism. Pooja time should only be for the locals or there should be a pre- booked system to ensure crown control allowing those that wish to pray the time and peace and quiet that they are entitled to. Unfortunately the respect for this sacred place has been traded in for more money and coachloads of tourists. Absolutely shambolic and disgraceful.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are visiting kandy then you must go to the temple of the sacred tooth. It is a beautiful temple with a great historical background. Try to go early in the morning so that you can get a chance to see the sacred ceremony and rituals. Reaching there by 9 or 9.15 am is the best time as the ceremony time is 9.30 am. Its a big temple with 2-3 museums and it will take around 2-2.5hrs to visit the whole temple and museums.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our guide ensured that we arrived in time to see the actual Tooth Relic. It can only been seen at set times during the day so best to check the times when planning your visit. Also plan to arrive very early as the place is crowded as it is such a holy place. There is lots to see in the temple, just be prepared for lots of walking in bare feet. It is a short walk from the temple to the British Garrison cemetery which, if you are from the UK, is worth a visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It’s well worth a visit, however be prepared to be pushed through the temple at a fast pace by locals and people working there. It was very chaotic & busy, not for the faint hearted. Remember to wear appropriate clothing & take water as it’s hot inside. Instead of paying for someone to look after our shoes we put them in our rucksack. Always have your tickets to hand, as there are security guards who will randomly check.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited The Temple of the Tooth about 8 a.m.- fewer tourists and with Raj, a registered tourist guide from See Lanka tours. It's far more interesting if you know what you're looking at - can understand the symbolism and the history behind the temple; having a knowledgeable guide aids your knowledge and understanding and made this trip particularly interesting. It's easy to walk past the Bohdi tree and not realise it's significance; or the relevance of the Tooth relic to both Buddhism and, over the centuries, political power; or even the shape and size of the open lattice walls. Well worth a visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the tooth is the most important place of buddhist people in srilanka and allmost all the buddhists in the world. If someone came to kandy this is the place they must go. Temple of the tooth is a place which built with traditional kandyan arts and crafts. It situated @ the middle of the city near the eye catching kandy lake.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are a religious person, do visit the  temple of tooth. It has a history as well. Otherwise, you don't get to see the tooth as they show it only once in 5 years and it is a big festival; do not be surprised or disappointed later on after you visit the temple.

I would strongly recommend that you visit during the august Perahara to see an amazing display of spirituality, richness and arts.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: So many scammers around this area that you would feel it's a business temple, exactly the opposite of what Buddha taught people. There is nothing special there as you are not allowed to see the sacred tooth except in specific months. The rest is just a regular temple.

Going inside you also have access to the museum which was quite interesting, but overall not great value for money. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is worth a visit, even as a non-Buddhist.  It is quite beautiful in its own way. I made the mistake of walking in to the temple with my cap still on.  I also mistakenly did this at a previous temple, and the guard there was polite in requesting I take it off.  However, here, the opposite must be said!  Without any warning, the attendant yanked my hat off, rebuking me saying “Hat off, you’re in temple.”  I acknowledge the offence I would have unwillingly caused (and apologised for), however, I found this to be an appalling treatment of a visitor.  I was furious about this. The security and shoe keepers were quite rude to us, which was regrettable.  This is despite us, as foreigners, injecting so much cash into the venue (Rs. 1500pp, quite a lot TBH). Summary: although a nice place to visit, it seems the venue operators must learn the lesson of “Don’t bite the hand that feeds you.”

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is one of the main attractions to see in Kandy, right on the lake. There is not much parking, our tour guide struggled to get parked and we were there early in the morning. You must also remove your shoes for going into the temple, you have to pay a small fee to get them taken care off.

review_text: We went on Boxing day which was a local holiday and the crowds were massive with people bringing offerings. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went with an excellent guide who explained to us about the tooth relic, but there is also a very good exhibit in a separate room from the temple which tells the story of the sacred tooth relic.  The grounds of the temple are really lovely, and is the inside too.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: On Buddha s death he left his left tooth as a relic . The story of the journey of the tooth and ensuring war over centuries is contained in pictures inside the museum. It’s crowded and foreigners pay more entry fee ( like most attractions ) . Lots of locals and tour groups so very overcrowded in the morning with flowers everywhere and people in prayer or chanting . The drumming is good . No photos allowed in parts of the building  . Museum interesting on top two floors . Need a few hours . Mass hysteria though and pushing to see tooth relic . Not sure the Buddha would be impressed with all the fuss but it’s a must see all the same !

review_text: Based on other reviews we visited in the morning. We arrived at 9.15 & able to walk around before the services began. We found the whole complex very interesting. If you are an independent tourist, I’d suggest the morning to visit as the tour groups go in the evenings & it’s far more crowded.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is probably a must on everyone's list when visiting Kandy. It is not disappointing, although my visit was not spectacular either. The building is beautiful, particularly the entrence hallway into the temple itself. There are plenty of museum buildings around the actual temple, and it is nice just to stroll around on the grounds. I think it was well worth a visit.

review_text: Fantastic temple, large premises with many buildings and small museum that is closed on tuesdays. Many historical items, wooden parts that are well kept and maintained, impressive main gate entering the temple itself.. Take into account that it can be very crowdy at poya moments and 3x a day during the prayer moments. With all that crowd it is hardly possible to pay respect to monks, tooth relic part and praying people without being pushed or stepped on your feet. If you can cope with that, it is really a temple you return to because every time you discover new items.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Definitely worth hiring a guide, they can explain the history, the religion and highlight the key places. It is very large with many things to see so I would think a bit overwhelming if you had no guidance. It is a very spiritual place so keep that in mind when visiting, the locals are very understanding of tourists and make you feel welcome. Be prepared with small change for the staff who watch your shoes. No shoes and they are very strict about shoulders and knees. Semi transparent wraps/clothing over these areas aren't accepted so be prepared with scarfs.

review_text: Maybe it was just the time we visited, but the place was absolutely crammed, almost to an unsafe point of view. Crowds were desperately trying to get to see the location of the relic and a bit of crowd control would have been good, it was quite uncomfortable. However, it is on the 'bucket list' of sites to visit and we are glad we went. There are a few nice things to see once you are inside, but nothing that sets it miles apart from the other cultural sites in Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A beautiful temple with an interesting story and sections that resemble museum exhibitions (go see the tusker area, with a real stuffed elephant). Crowded but not dangerously so, the atmosphere was calm and fun at all times. If you go to see the actual tooth relic on those mornings in which it is opened, expect many many people with no concept of personal space XD We loved it. Great photo ops and again - great atmosphere!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Being the main tourist attraction in Kandy everyone always visits here and with good reason.  The admission is 1500 LKR and try to have exact change as tickets are done by a machine.  We elected to have a guide but if you have Wikipedia you are fine without one. If possible go in the evening and stay for the pooja at 6:30 when they open up the special crystal Buddha upstairs. The temple also houses the palace of the last king of Kandy and a working monastery so spend a little bit of time walking around. You cannot wear shorts into the temple so either wear pants or bring or buy a sarong to be able to go inside.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I’m a student of Buddhism so actually visiting the temple and observing the daily service was not only an educational experience but an emotional one. To see so many people practicing their religion and meditating brings a special atmosphere. The temple complex is quite large and well maintained. Early palm manuscripts containing Buddhist texts are also on display for the visitor. However, be aware, the services get very busy and I believe the number of entrants is limited. We attended the 9.30am service and it was packed. Even so, we managed to get a view of the relic casket and stayed within the procession through the temple. Whether you’re interested in Buddhism or not, this is a glimpse into the magnificent history and culture of Sri Lanka and shouldn’t be missed if in the Kandy area.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the sacred tooth or else known as Sri Dalada Maligawa is the no.1 attraction in kandy among locals and tourists. It is not only a historical place to see, it calms your mind and gives you the energy to keep going the journey you have begun.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple was nice and peaceful. We followed the ritual of bringing water and pouring it to the peepal tree post praying to buddha and gaining a peace of mind. I was advised by a local to resolve the tree 7 times before pouring. Didn't get a chance to go to the tooth relic itself because it was beyond our budget. Just a note that saarc countries like India get half price

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: You need to wear proper clothing , shouldnt expose much of your skin. place is crowded Q is by properly managed by the authorities. you need to leave your footwear in a space managed by authorities just before you enter the temple which is free of cost service. Cost is 1000 LKR per person for Indians and probably for all SAARC nations. Cost if 1500 LKR per person for Non SAARC nations. you are allowed to take photos God , but not posing you and the God. the place should be idealy visited early in the day or during the evening, it is beautiful along with the lake beside.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Good viewing of the general temple but crowded with pilgrims.The tooth is rarely displayed. Worth a visit. Buying tix is quite the process. Dispensing machines were unreliable but attendants helped out. Have exact cash change ready or credit card. Dress code seriously enforced. You can buy sarong or safety pins for ladies to pin up the exposed areas with other garments. Or simply always carry a long sleeves shirt and pants or sarong in your day pack. You are all set to go anywhere. Do not remove your shoes till after you bought your tix or else you will burn your foot soles walking on hot rock slabs. Take water bottles. Respect the sacred space. People are simply terrific everywhere. Take pix later in eve of candles burning and offering. Partake in ceremonies and you will enjoy the experience even more. Finally ...make sure you take your sense of humour and adventure with you. Learn live and rejoice

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is believed that one of Lord Buddhas Teeth is preserved here, saved from his funeral pyre. The temple is mostly still in the original design , with a few later additional buildings. It is a place I respect due to the fact that there is no glaring deco, which contradicts with the Budhdist philosophy of simplicity. The evening puja with Kandyan style drummers and offerings add a bit of culture to the Temple, without deviating too much from the purpose of a temple. For serious visitors who are interested in meditation, the open gallerie type of long building on the side,is quite a peaceful place. All in all its a temple worth visiting even just for the expansion of experience.

review_text: The entrance tickets for foreigners is quite expensive. We did expect to see the tooth relic or an image of it however the inner chamber only opens at certain times and we could not wait 3 hours. We had a quick look around. The museum is good though however we just felt that if they advertised times we could plan better.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: January 1 and also a full moon brought tens of thousands of white-draped  Buddhist pilgrims who welcomed us to join the long, packed-in wait to see the room of the Sacred Tooth.  Almost all ladies and men carried trays of perfumed flowers.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Chances are you will not be able to see the actual tooth relic because they only display it at certain times. Nonetheless, definitely a place worth visiting. The place is not very difficult to reach. About a 20 minute walk from the Kandy railway station and bus terminus. Once you get there, the gardens around the temple are spacious and lush. There is also a beautiful lake adjacent to the site. Expect large crowds since it is a very important place of worship for Buddhists in Sri Lanka and indeed around the world. Once you get into the temple it is very quiet and serene. It is amazing once you get into the sanctum how quiet it is given the number of people in there. You won't be able to linger at the actual sanctum where the tooth relic is kept since you will be pushed away because of the crowds. Photography is technically prohibited but there is no shortage of people taking selfies. All in all, it is worth a visit if you don't mind the crowds, which you can hardly avoid given the importance of the place.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a very big temple right in the centre of the city. Make sure you are properly attired - legs & shoulders covered - otherwise you will be denied entry! There is a lot to explore on the temple grounds & not a lot of written information available. You can get a guide if you wish but I was content to wander the grounds & read what I could.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was the one thing on our trip I kinda regret spending the money on. It was very expensive compared to most other attractions and extremely crowded. It was interesting but other temples are just as good without the significant cost and crowds.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Just an incredible experience at the most important place in Sri Lanka for Buddists. Go when the Buddists chant (twice a day). Don't miss  the little museum to the sacrd elephant who carried the Sacred Tooth around Kandy once a year.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is a must see when visiting Kandy but be very ready for the crowds. The drumming when you enter is very loud and then you have to join the queues to climb the stairs to see the area where the tooth is kept.  You do not see that much as everyone is trying to get close to take photos. It is a beautiful place to visit. You need to cover your shoulders and knees when visiting and there are staff there to check you are dressed appropriately.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of Tooth is the most sacred temples for Sri Lankans and mustn’t be treated as a tourist spot. What I loved was that I could immerse myself in the richness of the architecture, rituals and culture of the local land. The atmosphere was serene. The museum at the back of the temple is fascinating - right from war artefacts to jewellery to paintings chronicling the passage of the tooth through time. For culture-buffs, this place should not be missed! For scenic beauty, the Kandy Lake is right by the side opening up the view to this beautiful city.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were very skeptical of a visit to the Temple of the Tooth and went at our driver's insistence while we were in Kandy.  So glad we did!  The temple is very nice for a walk through and is filled with pilgrims praying.  The best part is the two-floor museum describing the journey of the tooth to Kandy and displaying all the offerings from various countries that have been given to the temple for hundreds of years.  There is so much history here!  There are also many photographs of the damage to the temple from a bombing during the civil war.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Srilanka is one of the few places where you pay to enter a temple.The rates are different for locals , SAARC nationals and other foreigners Buddha s tooth is kept here though it is on display only once a year The premises are huge and they also are home to a museum dedicated to the famous pachyderm Raja , the sacred casket bearer of the royal procession  who is still there thanks to the taxidermist !!

You basically stand in line and get rushed past a window where they take your donation. You won't see the tooth. Otherwise it's a very pretty temple and the archaeology museum on site is cool.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The place appears to be a tourist trap and is more a business than a sacred site. If you’re foreign then you’re charged more, you also cannot wear trousers and therefore need to buy some in a nearby market stall for about 1000 rupees. So entry to the temple site, plus trousers and then entry into the actual shrine all adds up. They also appear to have genuine ivory on display and nearby you can even find elephants chained up for your amusement. In hindsight I probably would have just walked around the grounds, but even that would only be if I had nothing else to do.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I travel around Southeast Asia as much as possible to visit religious sites, and I was honestly underwhelmed by the Temple of the Tooth. It pales in comparison to even Singapore's Buddha Tooth Temple, and is definitely below Bangkok's National Museum. The building containing the Tooth is nice enough, and there are a few interesting parts. But Kandy itself is completely charmless (side note: don't stay at Hotel Thilanka, whatever you do), so I would strongly recommend skipping Kandy altogether.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple, located on the lake, is high on places to visit in Kandy. You need to remove your shoes and leave them at a stall/tent where you pay a marginal fee for them to be looked after while you are in the temple. The entrance to the temple is beautiful. This is a very holy place for Buddhists. If you are in Kandy then it is worth a visit but I would not go out of my way to go to Kandy just to visit the temple.

review_text: Crowded.. The amount of people waiting to pay respects, flowers and prayers was boggling. I would suggest you wear clothes which are long and not revealing.. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is in the Kings Palace Complex in Kandy right in front of the Kandy Lake. We took an offering of pink water lilies, and also lit oil lamps in a space provided for it. The complex is large and has a lot of walking spaces with walkways, and grass and plants growing. There is also a wooden pillared Vihara type of open hall like a Loggia, in the middle of the open space. The temple inside has the place where they keep the relic in a Golden crown which is opened to the public every hour for 15 minutes. There were long queues and one has to go early. We also saw the Golden Buddha statue in a space surrounded by Elephant tusks, and a hall in front for meditation and prayer surrounded by paintings of the Life of Buddha. A memorable visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is very popular with locals and visitors, and definitely worth spending time exploring.  There are several smaller venues within the larger ones that house fascinating artifacts and interesting stories depicted by ancient paintings.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was our first visit to a Buddhist temple. It was interesting and we were looking forward. This temple is a sacred place for the Buddhists and a popular place for tourists. There was a long line to enter the main shrine which holds the tooth relic, but the temple volunteers were swift and made sure everyone inside got a sneak view and closed the doors of the main shrine sharp at 8 PM. This is a calm, peaceful and huge structure. It has a beautiful garden and a lovely moat 😊

review_text: This is a very busy Buddhist temple. If you are NOT a Buddhist you should think about why you are visiting this as it’s an extremely Holy place and I found myself wondering why, when it was not my religion, I had come to somewhere I was totally out of place in.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We first visited the museum which houses excellent exhibits from Kandk's Royal past. We watched the ceremony start at 9.30AM. There was drumming and chanting and people made offerings..called observing pooja. We later joined the queue that files past the casket which holds the tooth. A very special place to visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Definitely a must for history fans as there is an interesting story as to why this is referred to as the "Tooth Temple".  It was very busy and you must be properly dressed to enter the temple. Women must wear a sarong and cover the legs and shoulders and men to wear long pants. I was intrigued with the story.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Kandy in general is crazy. I wasn't expecting that.The Temple itself is amazing and is obviously a very special place for people to come. Me not being a Buddhist I felt as though I was intruding on people genuinely coming to pray and give offerings, I don't want to be in the way of that. It was very sweet that they have a side annex museum that gives tribute to the Tusker Raja who held the relic on his back during ceremonies.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Having read other reviews I wonder if some visitors actually understand what they are visiting; having to cover your legs/shoulders is hardly a difficult thing to do and if you did a minute of research beforehand...... Anyway, yes it's busy, because it's a unique religious site for Buddhists around the world!  It felt a privilege to be allowed to enter and experience the crush of people of whom 99% were there for religious (not tourist) reasons.  Fantastic artefacts inside and a fantastic opportunity to stand and watch others respecting their religious beliefs.

review_text: Pretty sacred place for the larger population of the country. Crowd depends on the occasion and importance of the day. Use a guide or have google tell you all the information about the place beforehand. Beware of the dress code - Specially if you are wearing shorts and sleeveless.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Best to visit the temple close to the end of the thrice daily religious service times .The chamber containing the sacred tooth relic is opened for veneration by the public. Ritualistic drums are beaten and a colourful ceremony is conducted. Modest Clothing to be worn covering knees by both gender. One can see Kandyan kingdom period architecture in the temple and many buddhist writings done on bound ola leaf books. The entrance ticket also entitles one to visit the nearby Buddhist Museum housing Buddhist exhibits from nearby Asian Countries like China, Bhutan Nepal and India.Photos are not permitted inside the Museum

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A beautiful temple on the old palace. We went in the evening so had to wait for the ceremonies to begin. With Buddhist chantings it quietens your mind amidst the crowd of locals and foreigners. Some nice pictures on the walls that explains the travel of good and difficult times in the history of Sri Lanka. Adjoining is the Hindu temple. A cathedral and a mosque shows how people are united. Great place to visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of sacred tooth relic located by the lake side, in the busy road area, so it’s wise to walk to the temple if you’re staying anywhere close to the center. The temple itself is very beautiful, very old but preserved very well. Locals come here to pray, alongside with tourist flow, which make the place can be quite packed with people. Late afternoon to evening time is quite the busy time, better to come earlier and finish by sunset so you enjoy see every part of the temple in your own pace and peace. Visit the shrine room to see the paintings of tooth relics journey, while seeing all the collections of statues, donated by other countries. The temple block itself consist of numerous exhibitions, so you might want to give 2-3 hours to enjoy their collections. Make sure you wear proper clothes (cover legs, thighs and shoulders) before entering the main gate. Also make sure to buy ticket beforehand. New ticket machine is on the right side (after main gate go straight and head right) cost 1,500 LKR for foreigners. Then the temple entrance is on the left side. They provide service to keep you shoes for 100LKR / person.

review_text: This can be any other temple unless you have got a bhuddist relegious bent of mind. Beware , there is no need for you to spend 1k to 3.5k sri lankan rupees per person, unless you are a practicing bhuddist follower. You can very well tell your guude cum driver to take you to another bhuddist temple nearby and it should be just fine. NOM as this temple carries huge significance from a bhuddist religion prospective. Also, the lake views from this temple are breathtaking.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Buddha's tooth was saved when he died and eventually brought from India to Sri Lanka. All kings in Sri lanka since, has taken the tooth with him whereever he was living. After moving several times, the king and the tooth ended up in Kandy and a temple was created. And its still there after a couple of incidents during the British years. We experienced a fully loaded temple, loud and local with many worshippers and an open shrine. An experience of local buddhistic faith in an interesting place. The city of Kandy with the lake is really something special.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We arrived as the Temple complex opened.  It’s absolutely beautiful and there are several areas to see within the complex but the Temple itself was the highlight.  We didn’t know that they only show off the tooth once every five years.  But still it’s a must see place and you can definitely feel the “good vibes” and spirituality of the place.  Really beautiful and moving experience!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Due to the holidays it was extremely crowded and reminded me of a visit to the Vatican and the chapel berry Michelangelo spent some hours on his back to paint a ceiling. Like cattle we were herded down corridor after corridor, here it felt the same. As foreigner you get met by a local guide who offers his service to guide and explain the temple experience for you. “If you happy you pay, if not you go” he said. So we followed our guide. Yes, he was helpful and offered insights into the rituals, the do’s and do not’s around the temple and about Buddhism and told us when to pay this and that and put flowers where and why. When it came the time to leave and we shared with him how happy we were in form of a bank note, he just looked insulted and asked for more. Oh, you can’t take photos of people inside the temple and selfies are not allowed as you then turn your back to the sacred relics.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Maybe I had reached temple overload but for me it was an interesting temple without being spectacular. The architecture is good and I'm sure the history has significant. I went to the ceremony during the evening, which again was interesting with lots of gift and alms giving.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is heavily decorated with its mighty columns and Buddha statues. It truly reflects what a foreigner would want to expect from this wonderful city. Please be advised not to take photos with your back facing the Buddha statues though; it can be an offensive act in the eyes of locals.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Entrance costs 1500 SLR per tourist (1000 SLR if you are from a SAARC country). Guides cost around 1000 SLR, but are optional. They have special Buddhist ceremonies in the morning and evening (6:30pm) and it is worth it to watch. They have traditional Kandyan drum players and Buddhist monks who come to perform the ceremony. You can pray and take blessings from many parts of the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Sacred Relic is a must see in Kandy. It is a busy temple with tourists mingling with local devotees. You need to be patient with the crowds. There are ticket machines for tourists. You don't need the ticket until the last entrance and I saw many tourists trying to get in  without one. They were turned away.  You are required to take off your shoes to enter the Temple proper.  Leave it until the last booth to take off your shoes and wear socks if you have soft feet. The stone tiles get very hot in the sun.

review_text: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is a place that you must visit if you are visiting Kandy. Leave about 30 minutes to an hour to visit the place, depends on if you are a Buddhist or not as Buddhists might spend more than 30 minutes to worship there. Don't forget to pop in at the museum there too.

review_text: The Temple is a beautiful building, filled with colorful decorations, historical artifacts, and of course, worshipers. Unfortunately the process for visitors is a bit messy and it can be very chaotic inside, but we enjoyed nonetheless. I wouldn't suggest going to Kandy just to see the Temple; be sure to have several stops on your itinerary or it's not worth the trip.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had a great time in Sri Lanka. We came for the travels and the nature, and you also get to see lots of temples. I mean, you can't throw a stick without hitting a temple or a monkey. But Kandy wasn't part of that beautiful experience. Being Dutch, we can't help but compare it to Amsterdam. Amsterdam is huge, crowded, has everything, and is absolutely over-stimulating. This is about markets being surrounded by markets, and temples touching other temples. This temple is a beauty and a gem itself. But where the temples felt real and authentic in other places, this felt like a commercial attraction where you have to stand in a row, pay a grumpy monk, only to catch one short glimmer of a golden crown. It was beautiful, but for us this is proof of what tourism can do to culture. You won't hear me tell you to not go. You should go. Kandy is just as important as Amsterdam. It's just not an experience worth paying extra, or worth telling much about. It's ideal to pass through and don't stay long. Don't buy your presents there. Go short, stay short, taste the stimuli, suck in one beautiful temple, and move on to other places that are really Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: For devout Buddhist, this temple is a place of deep veneration. We stood for half an hour to see the tooth, whilst we only caught a glimpse of the relic, the atmosphere and the people’s faces was well worth it. Entry fee is SLK 1500 p.p.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is good to find a good guide to help you trhough and find out the appropriate timings during the opening of the gates inside the temple. People may ask for more money to guide but negotiate at a reasonable price you will need them for 20-30 minutes.It is beautiful temple and a historical one where one of Buddha's tooth is preserved and has a long story behind this tooth. It is a sacred tooth indeed!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Very interesting temple and tooth ceremony.  The ceremony entrance cost $1,500 rpps and starts at 6:30 pm - sharp. Many people bring offers for the blessing from different parts of Sri Lanka and some Buddhist countries.  You don’t need a tour if you are staying in Kandy, just need to show up with pants or sarong (men) long skirt (women) and pay your entrance - the temple is right in downtown. During the ceremony you will visit 3 different chapels within the same area.  It’s usually very crowded so make sure to move quickly and try to watch carefully to the incredible items like the 1,600 year book, etc. Enjoy!

review_text: It is worth coming by at a time of day when they are doing the "puja" or prayer. Lines can be long so be patient. No shorts, tank tops, or ripped pants. You can buy a sarong or pants outside the temple complex though. You will also be barefoot the entire time.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I came here on a group tour in early December and really enjoyed our time there. The interior was beautiful and at 9.30am a ceremonial display began. It was amazing to see the people of Kandy's religious devotion. It is worth being aware that it is a place of worship and, while you have paid to enter, that needs to be respected. review_text: A pleasant setting, beside the Kandy lake. Be aware of locals who start a conversation then want to guide you around and expect payment for their ' guided tour!' location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

I wish that the temple doesnt charge the steep entrance fee that it levies on foreigners. That apart, the place is a must visit for one and all!!!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Sacred place that you feel peaceful as you walk in. You will be able to see on the walk of the journey taken by the tooth relic and how it finally came to rest at its current place. The elephant that carried the tooth relic during the ceremonial occasion was stuffed and preserved there too, as a mark of respect.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is located in the Royal Palace Complex on the edge of Kandy Lake and close to the city centre. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is actually the castle of the last king of Kandy, which has been transformed into a temple. It holds the tooth of Lord Buddha & is the holiest & most sacred place for Buddhists in Sri Lanka. As someone from Kandy, I visit the temple at least twice a year & have been doing so for the past 30 years. For tourists, it is definitely a must see in Kandy. There are however a few points which you should know about before visting the place. You have to remove your footwear & headwear (including hijabs) when you enter. It is the same for all Buddhist temples in Sri Lanka. So anyone who is unwilling to remove their hijabs will not be allowed inside. You have to wear clothes which cover your knees or below & your shoulders. It's a holy place. You can buy scarves or such items at the entrance. I don't know about the prices, so it's better you come prepared. I have seen this temple through the years in different states, but my trip yesterday was very peaceful & pleasing to the eye, because finally no more plastic is allowed inside, & it was very clean. However, there is room for improvement. Foreigners must pay to enter, whereas locals don't. I've seen & heard foreigners complain about this & I'm not writing to justify it or against it, but that's just how it is. It's located in the heard of Kandy, right next to the lake. Definitely something to see if you haven't already.

review_text: This is a very large temple-cum-historic exhibits (mainly paintings) complex. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Very interesting and colourful sacred site. Women should make sure they wear long dresses(below the knee) non-see through, and arms covered. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Nestled close to the Udawattakele Sanctuary, The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is one of the most important shrines of Sri Lanka. Also named as Dalada Maligawa, this temple is based in the royal palace of the Kingdom of Kandy. Housing the legendary Budda tooth, the temple is a World Heritage site though very little are the remnants of the original temple built around 1600. Amazing ornamentation with golden fence and extravagant Canadian architecture makes it a blissful sight for the visitors. Dedicated monks unanimously chant the prayers of Malwatte and Aegirine , three times every day, during dawn, noontime and evening at the inner temple. Every Wednesday a holy symbolic bath of the Relic is done is fragrant water and that water is distributed among the visitors known to have healing powers.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This place is definitely worth a visit if you are in Sri Lanka. As soon as you get to the temple you will find an entrance check with two different entrances: one for man, with man checking the visitors; another one for women, with women doing the inspection. They did no security check, what they were checking was our clothes. We were not allowed to show our legs (ripped jeans are also a problem) and I believe there was also something with the cleavages. They didn't really explain me anything, they just fixed my clothes to cover me up according to their standards. After this you will walk a beautiful path to the temple itself, you will instantly feel the power of that place. You will then get to the ticket office where you will be asked to purchase your ticket. This was one of the most weird experiences for me because I soon realized that not only they were selling us the tickets but there was people EVERYWHERE trying to charge us for this and that. Be extremely careful about this, because the only thing that you need to pay for is your entrance ticket, so don't fall into any trap! You will then be asked to remove your shoes, you will have access to some taps where you can wash your feet and then "dry" them with a piece of carton that they'll give you at the ticket office. Then you get to enter the temple, which is a truly amazing experience. Don't expect fancy but you can certainly hope for an exotic experience. The smell in the air is of incense, you'll see a lot of people praying and some even sleeping on the floor there for some promise they made. The building is special but the experience is what you need to soak in as much as you can. I certainly did and I believe that this is the most exotic experience I've had in my life so far!

review_text: We headed to the temple at 5.30 for the 6pm evening ceremony. It was really nice to be able to watch the sunset over the lake beforehand whilst hearing melodic prayers over the tannoy. Make sure that you are dressed moderately with knees and shoulders covered. We paid 1500  Rupees (£7.50) to enter - fairly expensive but normal by Sri Lankan standards. Shoes are left in an office outside. As we entered, there was a drumming ceremony going on, we didn't see much initially due to the crowds but it was more of an audio than a visual experience. Just before 6PM we headed upstairs and were instructed to wait in front of the offering table to get a glimpse on the tooth. Otherwise, there was a long queue to actually be able to walk past the tooth. I can't imagine this is particularly exciting unless it has religious significance to you so wouldn't recommend queuing to walk past it unless you really want to. From the offering table we were able to see the tooth unveiling from afar. Though once the monks came in to reveal the tooth, there was a massive crush as tourists tried to take photos and locals pushed forward to make offerings. It was quite a horrible crush and really wasn't worth it as we hardly saw anything. After we escaped the crush, our private guide directed us around the various rooms of the temple. This was one of the times I was very thankful to have a private guide,  the temple was very busy and had I been on my own, I would have just given up in frustration. If you are alone/have young children/don't like crowds you may prefer to visit during the day when it's quieter. Outside there was a pretty glass wall of candles and small museum dedicated to an elephant. Overall I had an interesting time, we spent about 1-2 hours pottering around and soaking up all the mayhem. Wouldn't do it again though!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This holiest of holy Temple that contains the Sacred Tooth relic of the Lord Buddha is of great importance to Buddhists Worldwide. It enjoys a position of pre eminence in the Island. Visiting Ladies should cover shoulders and arms and If men wear shorts they should be longer below the knee if not one has to buy a local sarong. Head gear is not permitted. Wearing socks will help if you visit during sunny times. Daily special Homage services are conducted 5.30 -7.00 AM,9.30-11.00 AM and 6.30 - 8.00 PM towards the end of the service times the relic chamber window is opened for veneration. Local pilgrims line up to walk past the relic chamber. Tourists can walk past the location to look at the casket containing the sacred relic. Sri Lankan traditional Dance forms Drum Beating, musical instruments. Local decor items associated with Buddhism all can be seen at the temple. The temple architecture is typical to Kandy. The entrance ticket is also valid to visit the nearby Buddhist museum housing many exhibits from China, India Nepal, Pakistan,and nearby countries associated with Buddhism.

review_text: You would need at least two hours to walk around the temple, read up a bit on the history that is displayed around and then a brief walk through the Temple museum. Suggest you visit the Temple first around 2pm and once done attend the local Kandyan dance performance which is just outside the temple gate at 5pm. The Temple, according to legend is the holy grail which houses the tooth of  the Buddha that was taken from his funeral pyre. The tooth has a rich history attached to it and has been a treasure sought by Emperors and the likes. Take a walk around and read the history at the sacred hall on the life of Buddha. Also visit the museum which adjoins the temple to see artifacts and other valuable items that were donated by countries and other Kingdoms in honour of the holy relic.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: is one of the most important shrines of Sri Lanka. Also named as Dalada Maligawa, this temple is based in the royal palace of the Kingdom of Kandy. Housing the legendary Buddha tooth, the temple is a World Heritage site though very little are the remnants of the original temple .Amazing ornamentation with golden fence and extravagant Kanadian architecture makes it a blissful sight for the visitors. Dedicated monks unanimously chant the prayers of Malwatte and Aegirine , three times every day, during dawn, noontime and evening at the inner temple. Every Wednesday a holy symbolic bath of the Relic is done is fragrant water and that water is distributed among the visitors known to have healing powers

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you got early when the relic is on show ( 15 minute window) be prepared for crowds. The locals go in droves and you get pushed along. Make sure your shoulders and knees are covered otherwise they will not let you in. cost 1500 rupees ( £7).. Definitely worth a visit if you are in Kandy as it is the most sacred temple in Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is one of the most sacred Buddhist temples, as such, it is always very busy with many people coming to worship and give offerings. You must remove your footwear before entering (which will be minded for a small fee). Wear modest clothing, you will be checked before entering- long pants and a collared shirt for men, legs covered ( long skirt or pants) for a woman, also shoulders covered and no low-cut/sleeveless or tank tops for women. Be prepared to wait whilst you progress through the queue. An interesting part of the experience is watching the diverse crowd of people who line up for a glimpse of the jewel-embedded gold sarcophagus in which the scared tooth resides.Photos are allowed in most parts of the temple.

review_text: Kandy is considered as the second town after Anuradhapura where Buddhism took a root in Srilanka.  This temple is very divine and maintained well. The main hall within which in the second floor is the place where the tooth is kept and can be viewed only on full moon days.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We arrived for the evening ceremony which was luck on our part, although it did mean that the temple was busy and very noisy. Shoes/Socks off to go in (and it was wet)...  we had a private guide which helped us to understand what we were seeing and the things not to miss. This seemed quite commercial, with more tourists than locals, and as for seeing the casket/tooth - be warned even though you join a long queue you cannot stop in front of the window (it's behind glass) and there is an attendant trying to keep the line moving, so little chance for a good photo.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Background: Hosts one of Buddha's canine teeth taken from his funeral pyre and smuggled into Sri Lankan from southern India by the royal family. One of the holiest relics in Buddhism. The relic itself is worshiped like a living God with the devoted providing offerings regular times of the day. One of the best experiences on our trip to Sri Lankan. But I wish I knew the following facts. Tips: - need to remove shoes at the shoe keepers, separate entrance for foreigners. 100rupees per pair - have to have trousers that cover your knees. Bring a sarong otherwise. - You cannot view the tooth itself. Is covered in an ornate gold casket on the First Floor of the tower. - At service times (3-4 times a day), (hotel can tell you when), we went 09am. There will be a ceremony on the Ground floor infront of tower. stand by one of the pillars facing the tower for the best view, they will section it off. - The locals will be lining up around the walls outside the tower to go tothe first floor to see the relic. - If you're keen to see the relic, head up to the first floor during the middle of the ceremony, and make sure you stand in the middle of the basketball court sized room directly facing the door. The relic will be behind this the size of a the mona lisa but it's down a long tunnel, so you wont see it unless you're standing directly facing it. - WARNING: The first floor is very very crowded,packed with people shoulder to shoulder 200-300 people at least. and when the doors onthe first floor open to reveal the casket, people from the entire room will push towards the centre 2-3m narrow band to get a glimpse of the casket situated down a long corridor behind the wall. We were two talls guys, but were literally carried off our feet by people pushing from each side. Do not go upstairs if you have young kids or you're elderly. - Incredible experience seeing the casket in person when the doors open, you can feel the emotion and devotion of the crowd (all praying for a miracle/blessings/paying thanks) - make sure to visit the museum - also can see the large taxidermy elephant which was the designated carrier of the casket around Kandy during the holy Buddhist festival once a year. - not sure if the first floor / unveiling of the casket takes place every day, we visited the week after the once-yearly buddhist festival.

We were amazed with the architecture and ornate decoration of the  Temple and would certainly visit again if we return to Sri Lanka.

review_text: Visited mid-morning to a very busy temple. We timed it perfectly as the casket was open - really quite a magnificent sight to see! Lots of history here and a place where you could feel the passion of local and visiting buddhists alike. Beautiful setting, with impressive views across the lake and surrounding mountains.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: There is a lot of legend around The Buddha's tooth that you can read at the meditation centre in the temple on big boards. You do not get a glimpse of the tooth though, all you see is the casket. Apparently the relic is shown only once in five years or when any important dignitary visits. Lots of folks with young kids - apparently it is a custom to bring three-month olds to get blessings. Lots of stairs to climb though. If folks have a problem climbing steps, this place is best avoided.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Best time to visit is in the evening when all the lamps and lights are lit. The architecture is an interesting mix of Indian and Japanese culture. Apart from the main temple there are many other smaller temples and also a Buddhist museum. We were lucky to be there at 6:30 in the evening when they open the inner temple for viewing. At other times the inner temple is closed. Also there was some military ceremony happening when we were there so it was a bit crowded. But despite all the crowd, the temple has a serene soothing effect on the soul. You feel at peace with yourself. Definitely the highlight of Kandy.

review_text: If your in Kandy then of course you should visit this old relic. Tickets were 1500 rupees each and shoes must be taken off upon arrival and either placed in your bags or at the kiosk. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Walk around the temple complex to absorb the positive vibes and feel at peace. The best time to visit would be at sunset when they light the lamps and  incense. White clothing is preferred.  The temple has a number of paintings depicting the history of the sacred tooth relic.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A must visit temple. The evening ritual offered an amazing insight into the buddhist religion. We were even allowed to see the chamber of the 'tooth relic'. Buddhist worshippers flock to the temple with gifts for the monks as well as cash donations.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is incredibly ornate, with beautiful paintings and brass work inside. It is a major site of pilgrimage for many Sri Lankans, so be aware that the temple does get very busy and crowded, particularly outside the room where the Tooth Relic is kept. Important to remember that this is also sacred place and not just a tourist attraction, so don't get annoyed if the crowds make it difficult to get loads of prefect pictures. It's a special place, well worth the visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visit the temple in the evening as it has an entry ticket costing you around 1500lkr and the doors to the tooth relic on the first floor of the temple is open only in the evening around 6pm. Huge crowds so plan accordingly. The main building of the temple has a offering place in the ground floor with the tooth relic which is placed in a golden dagoba like thing on the first floor.One can spend sometime in the surrounding area of the temple, before queuing up to view the tooth relic.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This place was very popular so very crowded. A beautiful, colourful building.We were able to watch part of the traditional blessing with the participants dressed in colourful robes.. The history of the tooth is a fascinating story. Well worth a visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Didn't have long to have a properly visit this temple but i wish i did! Compared to other temples i have seen this seemed to be the most well kept of them all, i was shocked when i was told the age of the buildings. Unfortunately didn't have enough time but would love to visit again!

review_text: If you've never visited a temple then you may be impressed with this one.  If you have visited the Buddhist temples in Bangkok or even Borneo, I doubt you'll be impressed.  It is a small temple and not all that clean.  I was not happy having to walk bare foot through dried bird poop, nor through small amounts of tiny, sharp gravel.  The temple itself is OK, and I'm always impressed with believers of whatever religion for 'living' their beliefs and I respect their endeavors.  The flowers offered are beautiful, the actual shrines, statues, etc. are not overly beautiful nor large nor stunning in any unique way.  I did enjoy the surrounding area.  We went on a nice stroll along the waterway and even enjoyed an ice cream treat from a street vendor before returning to our car.  Saw a really cool rather large monitor lizard along the water which looked very round and full and may have just eaten a duck.... there were quite a few little feathers scattered around the lizard.  It was a gorgeous day and the people seemed quite happy and everyone was well behaved.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited the temple at around 9am to see the grounds, different rooms, and outer areas of the temple. Shortly before 9:30am we joined the queue the filed along the inside of the building, starting on the second floor where the window of the room containing the tooth relic container will open to worshippers and viewers passing by. The people following the line were quiet and orderly, many carrying flowers to offer onto the table in front of the opening of the temple. As the line shuffled and it was nearing our turn to pass in front and peer into the opening of the room container the tooth relic and its many containers, I opted to not use my camera but rather just take in the moment as I knew it would pass very quickly. (You will literally just walk past the opening and glance inside, spending about 1-2 seconds looking into the room) Also note you will not see the actual tooth relic itself, as it is stored in what I believe are multiple containers, the most visible one being solid gold. It is a fascinating and powerful moment, and I recommend it to anyone visiting Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The lady guard at the gate basically tried to pull my clothes up and down and shook her head when the took off my shoulder scarf and i had a bit of cleavage underneath.
