location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was a beautiful place to explore and it is worth the time. Book a local guide equip with thorough knowledge and stories about this temple. More important, he must be patient to answer all your questions. It was very crowded when we were there so check it out on the timing with your local guide. Dress decently to respect and be prepared to remove your footwear before entering the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had an overwhelming experience of the ancient temple of relic The guided tour was fantastic, special consideration were given to senior citizens where they may access elevators directly and skip the long endless queue I literally developed goosebumps just to even realise that I was standing near the ancient casket preserving the tooth of Lord Buddha A must visit holy shrine in Kandy

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A truly amazing experience and must see site in Kandy. This site attracts more tourists and locals than some other sites, however it is absolutely worth navigating your way through the crowds to experience this temple. To maximise your experience, I would suggest visiting with a local guide who can share this history of this magical and peaceful place and ensure you get the most from your visit here. An absolute highlight of my trip to Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited this beautiful place and it was worth the time. Great tour guide but he could've slowed down a little as it felt a bit rushed but having said that we could have asked him to slow down. BEWARE you need to take a sarong or wear long trousers and t shirts otherwise you get ripped off by the guys offering scraps of material to cover you at extortionate prices then demand them back!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Buildings are pretty. Overcrowded with lots of pushing. Expensive. 1500 rupees per person for entry and 100 rupees per person to store your shoes. Only foreigners have to pay. Never actually got to see the tooth as it's behind closed doors which only open when the next worshippers are in position and by that time, we had been pushed along. Wouldn't recommend going.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had the chance to visit the temple during the ceremonial of the teeth. This was overwhelmed. Of course it was very busy but this is part of the experience. Having the tourists and the believers all together is a bit challenging. A very important notion to keep in mind is that as a tourist you really need to pay a lot of attention to not bother the people that are here to pray, to respect them and the place. The temple is just beautiful and the atmosphere amazing. While leaving your shoes at the entrance (you can never enter a temple with your shoes, knees and shoulders need to be covered), you will have a lot of guides coming to you. I would say that the guide can be useful to learn about the history and story but he will make you go all around very very quickly. They normally request around 10€ tip at the end. I would suggest that if you have the guide that you make the visit by yourself again  after the guide leaves to take more time to look at everything in details For sure a place that cannot be missed !!!!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a really impressive temple, but to make it a memorable experience, go around 6 pm when they open up the room where the Sacred Tomb is kept. The Monks enter the room to a drum procession, and the buzz around the temple is unlike any of the other temples we visited in Sri Lanka (and if you came from the Cultural Triangle, that's a lot!).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a very religious place steeped in history.  To get the most out of it, you really need to do some homework or get a knowledgeable guide to take you round. You can't wear shoes inside the temple grounds so make sure that you have some socks or, please,  that your feet are at least clean and not smelly.  You leave your shoes at the shoe place just at the entrance so make sure you some smaller currency to pay when you collect them or, have a bag and carry them for yourself. Photography is allowed in most of the areas, but obviously without flash.  People are praying and it's an active place of worship.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We decided to go for the 915 Sunday service which involved walking around to see the golden casket as well as the thai temple and the other temples. Some of which were built 2000 years ago. It was very busy and crowded as everyone was trying to see the golden casket or offer flowers or money to the gods. It was a great experiance especially with the drummers playing. If you want to experiance some of Sri Lankas culture and religion it is the best way to see how they live. You can take photos inside the temple but not everything. Out of respect you must wear long trousers and tshirts. However it does get quite hot and sweaty. Great experience for anyone.

review_text: We visited this temple on a Saturday in the Summer holidays which was probably a poor decision on the part of our tour operator but I can handle crowds, what I can't handle is rude, people pushing me out their way, pushing their small children in between me, risking them getting crushed, basically behaving like barbarians. It was very dangerous and people could easily have been crushed. I don't know if the people doing this were locals or tourists but it painted a pretty dim view picture of whoever they were.The irony is they were visiting a Buddhist temple and I'm pretty sure Buddism does not promote treating fellow human beings like objects to be barged out of the way. Put a really sour taste in my mouth and did not enjoy the rest of the morning, was glad to leave. From an objective point of view you could barely see anything anyway and what you could see was very underwhelming. Go to the Dambulla Cave temples instead, they are stunning and visited by people who know how to behave like civilised human beings!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: what a lovely and huge compound with many shrines and individual Temples along the way to the min Temple which house the tooth relic. Entrance fee to the main temple is USD 10 per pax. We had an unsolicited guide on our entry to the temple. He is an old man and smelt of alcohol. We didn't want to make a scene so we let him string along. It was evening and there was a celemony going on as we went in. There was a large crowd mostly locals. The mood was solemn and the last I witness such religious fervent was in a Catholic Church in Cebu. As we processed along the interior from one section to another, I felt like I was on a pilgrimage . The room that housed volumes of manuscripts was very moving. I think it is called Palle Malle Viharay. Likewise the tooth relic section where chanting was going on throughout. Our unsolicited guide zoomed us through the varies section and at the end of it he said" my job is done now pay me $20" . Again I do not wish to make a scene and paid him. To me it was like making a offering to the Temple and he did make our tour easier. On our exit we saw him gave money to the entry guard. I felt sad that even in a holy place people will engage in deceits and dishonesty. Then again, when pay is Low and people are poor this is bound to happen. So if you don't want to pay make sure you stood your ground and reject his guidance. On the whole it was one of the better spot to visit and somehow we felt enlightened and happy. Do visit.

review_text: Maybe Temples just aren't my thing or maybe I'm just a bit Templed Out but . . Getting to the Temple from almost anywhere in Kandy is a bit of a mission. It is situated on the water and parking is almost impossible. Our driver found somewhere close-ish to drop us and we walked the rest if the way. To get in it is necessary to go through 'his' and 'hers' security which takes ages for women as all of their handbags, shopping bags etc are checked whilst the guys flash through. Once through it is not immediately apparent where to go next. As the 'tooth' was not being displayed during our trip we opted for the old temple instead which was interesting and comprises a number of places of worship which are all in use. The main temple is huge and genuinely is worth a visit if you are in Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is really the reason why foreigners visit Kandy and if you like to visit religious sights and soak up the atmosphere that surrounds such sights than this is excellent place to go. Expect a lot of people as this is also frequented by locals especially for evening service. We  went in during morning and there was already a lot of people, specially on the first floor where offerings are presented so i can only imagine what the crowds are for the evening service. In the temple there are other things to see and I found the room with the explanations and paintings on how Buddhism and Buddha's tooth came to SL  great (it is behind the temple where the tooth is). As in other religious buildings no shoes allowed and make sure you are not wearing tight clothes as you first have to go through a "check point" before you even reach the temple and if they think you are inappropriately dressed you could be denied entrance (tickets are bought after this check point so no  worries on lost money).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This must be the most sacred Buddhist temple in Kandy. I think it was my very first visit to a Sri Lankan temple and one that holds the Sacred Tooth Relic of Buddha. It was an interesting visit for me and my friend even though we are both not Buddhists ourselves. It was an eye-opening experience to observe the artwork and the religious ceremonies held inside the temple. I would recommend anyone who visits Kandy to visit this significant temple because it is such an important religious and cultural site of the Sri Lankan people.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic during my short visit to Kandy, Sri Lanka. My experience can be summarized below: What's impressive: - The site is a UNESCO World Heritage site and is very well maintained. - You can witness the wonderful scenes during prayer time (3x a day). What to expect: - Pack of local devotees who will visit the temple to offer prayers during prayer time. - You need to remove your shoes, but you can keep your socks on as you enter the temple compound. There's a storage area for tourists but you may need to tip the person a little for keeping watch of your shoes. - Like many other sacred places that you visit, be prepared to cover up your shoulders and knees. Preferably in long pants. - You may want to get a guide to explain to you the history of the tooth relic and the temple to make it more interesting. What can be improved: - Entrance fee for foreigners. It's too expensive, considering most of the temples in Asia offer free entrance. Final verdict: - Attractions: Few good artifacts to see within the temple compound (the old relics used as part of the worship procession). - Structures: Well maintained. - Cleanliness: Clean. - Food: Nil. But there are nearby restaurants outside. - Staff: Friendly. - Value: Pricey ticket (LKR1500 per pax. 50% for children) - Time: Recommended to spend between 2 - 3 hours. - Likelihood to revisit: Probably if I go with someone who hasn't been here before.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a great temple but it was really busy so we felt pushed along with a crowd. Personally, I don't like walking around in bare feet with hundreds of others so my advice is take a pair of socks to put on which is allowed. You need to wear long trousers too. There is lots to see but we felt we couldn't really stop and take it all in, especially upstairs. It was a holiday so it would probably be better to go on a normal working day, but not prayer time. There is a nice walk around the lake which you can do afterwards!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Most Popular Town in Sri Lanka with Lord Buddha Relics Kandy is the second capital of Sri Lanka. Kandy is world famous for the Temple of the Tooth, which safe keeps the Lord Buddha’s Tooth Relic venerated by the Buddhists all over the world. There are also many sites with Kandyan Architecture prominently displayed, specially at the Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth Relic) , Lankatilaka Temple and Embekke Temple, to name a very few. The traditional Kandyan Architecture consist of Temple Structures, Murals done on walls and on stone in many temples, Carvings and reliefs done on Stone and decorated Wooden Carvings on timber columns and brackets.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It would be difficult to imagine visiting Sri Lanka without visiting the beautiful historic city of Kandy with its temples and lake. It would be impossible to imagine visiting Kandy without visiting The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic. If you're of a spiritual (Buddhist) bent don't expect this to be a place of peaceful and tranquil contemplation. Do expect it to be a fascinating and absolutely rammed cultural experience. We spent a good hour pressed cheek to cheek with locals visiting the shrine just trying to get inside, up the stairs and then past the relic (a molar found in Buddha's ashes).  Don't expect to see the tooth itself. It's hidden away from view. Definitely visit the stuffed elephant Raja in one o the out buildings.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I wasn't sure what to expect, but had been recommended that I must visit.  For tourists, there is an entrance fee (~1500 rupees for single).  As I came to the entrance booth to pay, a nice fellow came up and started to lead me through the whole process of entering, etc.  I guess pretty obvious I was a tourist.  After paying entrance fee, you have to check your shoes, as you must enter the temple bare-footed.  This nice fellow continued to guide me through the temple, stopping at a number of spots and providing some history and background into the temple and Buddism.  He seemed knowledgeable, and interesting, so by now I had figured out he was a "volunteer" tour guide.  I did get quite a bit of info from him through the tour, so was not disappointed; and more info than I would have gotten just walking through on my own.  At the end, he asked for $20 usd, which seemed like alot, and unfortunately I didn't have that much on me.  But he was satisfied with what I did give him.  he gave me back a small tip (~20-30 rupees) to tip the shoe man.  I do think this is a historical site worth visiting. in Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I visited it on Sunday; it was so crowdy with local people. It’s better to choose another day for visit as without a local guide you may spend a lot of time stuck in the crowd. But this somehow also added to the atmosphere. Thanks to our local guide provided by the tour agency with which we booked the Sri Lanka tour we managed to see the Temple a for about 1,5 hour. Without him we would need more than 3 hours, as there were queues with people, and the issue is that they close the passing by the sacred relic and stop the people to pass, and you have to wait a lot in the crowd. Our guide helped us to surpass part of the queue and we managed just 3 minutes before they closed it. The Sacred Relic is not visible you have to believe it is there. The Temple is interesting and worth visit. There is an entrance fee for foreigners – 1500 rupees (10$). NOTE: your body should be covered – no knees or shoulders could be visible. Don’t wear string trousers if you are woman, the guard didn’t permit a lady wearing trousers to enter. Or just have a sarong or scarf with you to cover up. Take socks with you as you will have to leave your shoes before entering the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Had an excellent experience going through the temple and the museum as well.  Was very busy as school holidays but that added to the atmosphere. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is a sacred place for Buddhist so appropriate clothing is a must. Locals normally wear white or light coloured clothing. Revealing necklines, sleeveless or clothes that are short are not permitted. If you wear jeans (non ripped) with a loose and sleeved top you should be fine. As you approach the temple slippers/shoes/hats have to be removed. There is a counter that looks after your shoes and gives a token. Do not pose for photos directly in front of the temple with your back to the temple as it is also considered disrespectful. There are loud music with drums and trumpets at certain times of the day when the pooja is offered. There's a small museum dedicated to Raja, the tusker who carried the Dalada karanduwa in the Asala procession for years from 1960s-80s. Recently they have introduced tickets for visitors (non-locals) which can be purchased at the counters at the entrance to the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Unless you are budhist, my recommendation is to go at the busier times. There is controversy as to the temple's original function and whether the tooth is even there (or kept safely elsewhere), either way you won't get to see it. What is special is seeing throves of believers coming with flower offerings, taking family pictures before entering and then sit there and pray. There are pretty decorations etc as well. Word of advice, if you can come with slippers which can fit into your bag, do so. Not to save the fee but rather to avoid standing in line to hand them in our get them back whilst a big tourist group is doing the same.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is one of many sites in the world that houses the tooth of Buddah, and located in the royal palace complex of the former Kingdom of Kandy. It's the most sacred and biggest Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka. To Buddhists the tooth relic is a symbolic representation of the living Buddha and as such they hold rituals, offerings, and ceremonies. 💐💐 Kandy is one of major cities of Sri Lanka and also the capital of Central Province. It lies in the midst of plush green hills in the Kandy plateau. The greenery comes from tropical plantations, mainly tea. Having read so much about Kandy and the tooth relic, not to mention scores of cricket matches that I watched on TV screens, we decided to pay a visit to Kandy city and the Buddhist holy temple in it. 🌻🌺🌻🌺🌻 The temple turned out to be yet another visitors site where my being a SAARC nation denizen paid dividends (entry fee for visitors is SLR 1500, SAARC nations SLR 750). However, I was sad to see a weird kind of extortion committed by some greedy touts tending the shoe racks in the temple. Since it's a holy place and visitors are supposed to remove shoes, they are asked rather demanded to put at least SLR 100 money in the donation box, in addition to entry fee. To me, donation is a voluntary deed and by insisting upon people for it disgraces the sanctity of the holy temple. Not at all good feelings by any means. A sacred place desecrated by greed of some lousy scavengers!👎😱😡😩 The main shrine has a golden canopy over it, and the golden fence which encircles the main shrine are other notable features. The tooth relic is encased in seven golden caskets engraved with precious gemstones, and kept in a gold casket shaped like a stupa. When we entered the temple there was a big crowd of believers sitting down on the floor in front of the relic with hands raised chanting religious mantras. On Wednesdays a symbolic bathing of the relic is held with a herbal mixture derived from scented water and fragrant flowers. Too many locals and foreigners were visiting the temple and you could easily hear the ongoing commentaries in various languages by guides accompanying the visiting groups. It's a huge complex with many support buildings, a museum, a huge front court & backyard, and a serene lake on the side. Two or 3 hours will be sufficient for a "seen all" tour. 🌺🌺☘️☘️🌹🌹 After visiting the temple, you can walk alongside the Kandy lake all the way to the City Center across the street to rest your tired limbs and settle for a cup of tea, coffee or whatever. The scenery across the lake is breathtaking, and walk seems just as mesmerizing. 👍🌸👍🍁👍🌷

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple during the morning Puja (offerings/prayers), where visitors can catch a glimpse of the relic casket that holds the Buddha's tooth. The temple was heaving with tourists and devout Buddhists alike. On arrival, we were fortunate enough to be approached by the head guide who had been working at the temple for over 40 years. He was a true gentleman and extremely funny, taking about Lord Soulbury "the old codger", as well as personally meeting the Queen and the Prince of Wales during state visits (see uploaded photos). The guide was very informative and well worth the small fee we paid. It made the whole ceremony more meaningful as we understood what was happening and why. The Puja starts with some elaborate ceremonial drumming and various offerings. Once this is complete, there is a mad rush to the first floor where the tooth casket is made visible. We were pushed, shoved and jostled - and this actually made for what was one of the best experiences of all the historical temple visits. You really got a feel for how important this temple is for those making their offerings and receiving blessings. We felt part of something special. Due to the amount of jostling and chaos, I wouldn't recommend those with young children going to the first floor during high season - as it's akin to a mosh pit at a Slipknot gig!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This place facilitates elephant abuse, at least they did during the Kandy Esala Perahera festival. During the festival the elephants stay at the terrain of the temple of tooth. I find it shocking that it is this place that allows the chaining and stick stinging of such wonderful intelligent animals. The elephants can’t move around, because they are being chained. The chains are so tight that we saw the scars on their legs. Also, we saw the scars and wounds on their heads and bodies because of the stinging with the stick to punish/brake them. The Buddha expounded that sentient beings currently living in the animal realm have been our mothers, brothers, sisters, fathers, children, friends in past rebirths. One could not, therefore, make a hard distinction between moral rules applicable to animals and those applicable to humans; ultimately humans and animals were part of a single family. They are all interconnected. I cannot believe that this place facilitates animal abuse. Furthermore there is mistreating of tourist at the entrance. Of course I understand this is a religious sacred place and you have to dress properly/accordingly. But I find it very interesting that they security guards judged the short of my boyfriend to be too short, sending him to a flower stand nearby which charges 500 rupees for a sarong (part of the set-up), and after entering we saw locals in way shorter pants walking by. review_text: I'm not a Buddist or religious person but this place is definitely with a visit. We spent 3 hours walking around and taking in the atmosphere,  information and beauty.  We spent 3 hours here - it was during the Perahera so there were plenty of elephants to see as well. We didn't opt for a guide so the pictures and text around the main hall were good for a brief story of the Buddha. A lot of our time was in the International Museum of Buddism.  It was fascinating to see; how Buddism spread and the same but different images of the Buddha. The museum is laid out by Country and easy to stroll around.  It obviously is busy with tourists and locals but generally didn't feel overcrowded like some places can.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Obviusly as you can deduce fro my title, I am not spiritually inclined. However I found my visit here very insightful. It left me feeling hopeful for Mankind There are a few architectural features that are beautiful ;the arched doorway into the temple for one, but aside from this there is nothing really spetacular. Note - if you are agoraphobic best to reconsider whether you should go .

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Very famous temple in Kandy. We visited on Aug 1 - the week of the annual Perehara festival.  As Indian passport holders, we had to pay a fee but less than other foreign  tourists. You need to show the passports to get the discount in fee. We bought a small plate of flowers to offer at the Shrine.  The whole trip took us about an  hour max. Taking pictures allowed inside the temple. Silence is golden and it is practiced to the max in the temple. We felt peaceful just sitting in the hallway of the shrine. Shoes - Shoes not allowed inside as in most religious worship places. They have a free facility for dropping your shoes & picking them after the visit. A token is issued with a number so your shoes are safe. They have a donation box if you want to donate- no compulsion at all. Dress code - as in any religious place, visitors need to dress formally (no shorts, sleeveless etc).  Men & women to wear long pants/skirt and top with shoulders covered.  We saw a few foreigners with a sarong covered around their waist or shoulder, as they wore shorts or sleeveless and had to cover it before they entered. Beautiful lawns outside the temple as you exit. Do not miss this place in Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is one of the main attractions in Kandy and one you must see - go to the ceremony just after sunset and experience the awe and wonder that the relic creates when it is unveiled. A thoroughly interesting and thought-provoking visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple of the sacred tooth attracts a lot of locals and tourists because of its importance in Buddhism. The shrine itself is crowded and if you go around the time of the opening of the shrine doors to see the casket, be prepared to be pushed and shoved along with the crowd. The temple itself has many other shrines you can visit which may be less crowded. Apart from the temple itself, there are several museums you can visit (most of which are covered in the 2000 LKR entrance fee). There are also areas for you to sit down and take in the energy of the place either within the main temple area or outside. Because of how large the temple and its entities are, prepare to be here for ~2-3 hours depending on the crowd and how much of the temple you want to see. Definitely worth a visit if you're in Kandy!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Hailed as one of must see things in Sri Lanka I had high hopes. However it was a huge disappointment. An incredibly commercial enterprise it seems to have lost anything spiritual about it. Whilst the original temple, which cannot be see from the outside, is impressive that is about the only element that appears to have any soul to it. Everything else seems to be a commercial venture and not something i would recommend to anyone visiting Sri Lanka. There was a cemetery just behind the temple which is managed and tended to by a wonderful man. Not only does he do this for free and not profit (which appears to be the main motivate for the temple) but he knows all of the stories behind each headstone. A fascinating visit which shed some light on how the British survived (or struggled) when they arrived in Kandy. Skip the temple and visit the cemetery to talk with this wonderful man.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Personally I don't like kandy, but this is by far the best thing to do here. The temple is of great significance to the Buddhist religion and you must remove your shoes and respect this. review_text: The Temple of the Tooth, located right beside the lake, is truly beautiful to see. Besides all the obvious things to see, I would give as tip not to forget to look up! location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is located inside the old kingdom of Kandy near an artificial lake in a really beautiful landscape. The temple was named this way for apparent reasons. It is believed that the tooth of Buddha is kept inside this temple. It is considered as one of the most holy places in Sri Lanka. Especially in October they have great celebrations to honor Buddha and also in order the rain period to begin successfully. They have dedicated a room inside this place to a famous elephant, who is kept embalmed in there, who carried on his back the Relic during the celebrations. The day we visited the temple there was also a celebration and people were bringing flowers and food to honor Buddha. Inside the temple there were  Buddhist monks who were praying, participating and also looking after the temple. As in all Buddhist temples you have to leave your shoes out of the temple and also to have covered your shoulders and your feet below the knees. There is a special place where they can keep your shoes paying a small price. It is also really important not to have photos in front of Buddha statues, because it is a clear sign of disrespect! You can photograph Buddha statues alone, with no people in the photo. It is definately recommended to visit this temple in order to know more about the culture and main religion of people in Sri Lanka! A really interesting experience!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: So we heard so much about this place that we had to put it in our itinerary. We arrived and were looking for the ticket booth that someone asked which country we were from. He looked official(with a badge) so we replied. He immediately took us to the ticket booth and told us we what we had to pay. We bought our ticket. He asked to look at it. As soon as we showed it to him, he grabbed them and asked us to follow him. It was so crowded and we had a kid in tow that in the confusion we followed. He had our tickets afterall. He continued to help push us through the crowd. Once inside it was even more crowded with hallways and staircases leading every which way. He started to tell us all about it. I asked him if he worked for the museum. He said yes. It was clear he wanted to be our guide and never asked for permission. The crowd was so off putting that we decided to just go with it. He pushed us past all of the crowd and got us closer to the sights we should like. I was unimpressed. He kept asking us to take a photo or this or that. I didn't. I didn't think it was that impressive. Again I might've been dazzled and confused by the crowd to appreciate what I was seeing. He kept pointing here and there. taking us into corridors. At the end, he said we had to pay him 1000rs. What? My thought was, you never asked us to be our guide and never mentioned your price. We appreciated him pushing us through the crowd so paid him 700rs. He was fine with it. We stayed back and went to the museum that is attached. Free of the crowd and the guide.  We loved it. It has all of the antiquities and history of Buddhism from all around world. All in all, the architecture is lovely. The museum is very informative and beautiful but the temple itself is overrated. Unless you can catch it in a day or time it's not crowded it's so not worth it.

review_text: I visited this temple in Kandy some time ago. It was long before August 2016 but that's as far back as system will take us. Oddly enough at the time I didn't realise we were going to gaze upon the gold reliquary and not the actual tooth. I was shuffled along after my appointed few seconds of viewing had passed thinking I had missed it. Many reliquaries later I'm feeling a bit foolish though it's easier these days to be educated  on just about everything. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited this site with friends.  It is a UNESCO world heritage site believed to hold a tooth of Buddha from 483 BC. We had difficulty understanding everything he was saying and had we not had a basic grasp of the Bhuddist religion we would have struggled to take everything in. We were not at all impressed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went during a ceremony where they open the doors and you can view the tooth relics shrine. Men and women have to enter through separate gates and bags are searched. It's a safety precaution, but everyone moves through the lines quickly. It was so busy, so if you choose to see it, please be patient. Everyone wants to do exactly the same thing and courtesy is important. We hired a guide, who was really helpful. I, unfortunately, didn't bring enough to tip adequately and would have been more than happy to tip more for his knowledge. You can't wear shoes in the temple, which is common, and you can put them away in the shoe storage for a small price. Our driver and guide organised our entry, so we didn't have to wait in line - but most entry prices into ancient sites are around $10-$20, so be prepared to pay around that. You can also buy flowers as offerings, which are available around on the outside of the temple. Photos are allowed throughout the temple except when viewing the tooth relic up close. It's clearly sign posted and you'll be told by staff and your guide. The overall experience is interesting as there is quite a lot to look at including the story how Buddha's tooth was moved around different kingdoms throughout history. The last King of Kandy's Palace is also on site, but you can't see inside, however, you will walk over the old trap door the King used to travel from his palace to the library. The library is small, but the important room houses the oldest manuscript in Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: There are 3 ceremonies per day (05h30, 09h30 and 18h30) and this is your chance to have a look at the golden relic holder for the sacred tooth of Buddha. Start your visit somewhat 1h30 before the ceromony so that you have time to visit all the other areas before. Be present +/- 15 minutes before the ceremony begins on the ground floor of the main temple. Traditional drums and whistle blowers will announce the beginning of the ceremony. After some time monks will come from the left and go through the main door. This door will be closed straight away. Now is the time to move to the first floor. Here is where it happens.  Take the stairs on your left side. Quickly 2 rows will start to form. Take the row closest to the wall. This row moves slowly but this is the row that gives you a chance to see the relik holder. Wait and have some patience untill the monk opens the viewing door (on the first floor). Prepare to make a donation/offering.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: To be concise, I loved this Temple. It is a fenced compound next to Kandy Lake. The grounds are green and expansive with outdoor sculptures. While the sacred tooth aspect can be seen with little time spent right there, the whole complex can consume much more time just sauntering around. I especially liked the incense burning platform adjacent to the glass-enclosed candle/oil burning memorial. Each are outside the temple. The entire setting--inside and outside--does exude a somber and sacred tone. Its dark hues embellish that feel inside. Be sure to dress properly when you attend---long pants for men and no shorts or revealing tops for women. I think sarongs are available from vendors outside the gates if you forget. Also, be prepared to check your shoes at the station adjacent to where you purchase your tickets. By the way, foreigners are charged more to enter the temple (300LKR or 500LKR, I forget)  and 100LKR when you retrieve your shoes with the token provided when you relinquish possession of them.  I spent about two hours there wandering around. Enjoyed every minute too.

review_text: When we arrived at the ticket desk, a man asked how many we were and bought our tickets. He then took us over to the shoes, still holding our tickets, then started leading us into the temple. We then realised we'd accidentally got ourselves a guide! Though we felt a bit ripped off, we had to admit he was somewhat helpful, giving us a brief explanation of what we were looking at. We went during puja, when the doors to see the casket containing the tooth are opened. You don't get much time to linger and look at the box due to the huge numbers of people pushing through the room. Other parts of the temple are equally interesting though, and less crowded, such as the library and the taxidermy elephant. You can't go to Kandy without visiting the temple, but keep your wits about you and don't assume anyone is temple staff!!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I went on a Sunday evening and what an experience of the soul!. Drums, people, prayer and Buddha. So much to take in. I've never been here before, but how lucky to be there when the door to the actual relic chamber was OPEN to public view. This, apparently, is a rare occasion as our tour guide and professional photographer waited YEARS to be there when this occasion took place. I feel so lucky and honored to have seen this with my own eyes. The rooms that also display the story of Buddha and the tooth itself is a must-see. Take time to meditate in front of the 15 or so marble Buddha's all with different yogic hand gestures. Simply beautiful.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We spent a number of hours at the Temple of the Tooth. Men and woman need to have their knees and shoulders covered. There's considerable leniency for 'babies'; this included my nearly 9yo daughter (she's not often referred to as a baby anywhere but SL). There are locals at the entry/check point who you can rent a sarong from if are not adequately dressed (SLR200- rent $ R500- buy). My husband rented/ borrowed a sarong as his shorts weren't quite long enough. We were approached by an unofficial (?) guide near the ticket box. We hesitated in taking his services as we've not quite worked out how to pay all of those who offer their services in Sri Lanka. On prompting, he advised that a payment of SLR2000 was what he'd like to receive although he wasn't meant to talk money.  We arrived at a time when a number of rooms that are only opened once during the day were about to open. He somehow facilitated us in (kind of) queue jumping so we got to see into the room where the relic of Buddha's tooth is said to be kept. We also went into another particularly sacred room. He was also very knowledgable and able to provide insight into the physical surrounds and an insight into the spiritual significance of the temples. I think our money was well spent.

review_text: Having been to lots of Temples in Sri Lanka I can't get to excited about this one although I appreciate how revered and important this sight is. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Fervent Buddhists flock to the Temple because it contains one of Buddha's teeth. We were lucky enough to be there during a small window (0900-0930) when the room is open and you can peek in at the golden stupa housing the Buddha's tooth. If you miss the timing, you won't get to see it. The drawback is that it is incredibly crowded. The locals think nothing of elbowing you out of the way and jumping the queue to get to the front. Take note: a dress code applies (no shorts or bare shoulders) and long pants or a sarong ought to do the trick. You need to go barefoot so wear slippers (unless you don't mind depositing your shoes with a guy for 25 rupees) and bring wet wipes to clean the soles of your feet. There is a museum upstairs and a separate, weird exhibition dedicated to a taxidermied Asian elephant named Raja. Yes, he's been perserved and encased in a humidity-controlled glass room for posterity.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The guided tours of the temple are well worth it - the guides are incredibly knowledgable, with great spoken English. In addition, this was the off peak season which allowed us to walk around freely without too many other tourists and the temperature was perfect (any hotter/ busier and I imagine the experience would not have been as pleasant!)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is located next to the Kandy lake and like most of Buddhist temples, is made beautifully. Big open spaces, a water fence outside, lamp lighting area, Buddha's statues..... all these make it quite a site to be enjoyed. We were lucky to have been there at the time when they open the screen in the central room for visitors and devotees to look at the sacred bell-shaped golden cover which actually has the tooth inside it. One local lady told us that they open this screen for few minutes only at 6am and 6:30pm everyday. The actual tooth is displayed only once every five years! The disappointment was that only a select few were allowed to enter the actual deeper situated room which actually held the relic. On one side were some monks and other VIP people and on the other side were those who had bought some particular kind of expansive offerings.... The commoners were just allowed to look at it from a small window whose screen is what is opened twice in a day...... Go here to appreciate the Buddhist religion and witness a site which is ranked high amongst places to visit IN Sri Lanka. Kandy lake is just adjacent and many good eateries are located close by.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I'm sure I'm just another ignorant tourist parading around a highly spiritual place with camera in hand however the entire 'feel' of this place seems wrong. Firstly the 'welcome' by security is what I'd expect checking into a jail. Stern faces, dismissive pointing and not so much as a nod of the head. Ok - they've probably had 1000 other western tourists turn up with shorts or singlets but cheer up guys. (check the dress code requirements as security simply won't let you in). Once inside the temple grounds, it is pleasant enough but the surrounding architecture is not breathtaking. Inside is not much better and far more crowded. The tooth is somewhere in a vault behind many doors so you don't even see that. For the tourist - underwhelming at best. For the Buddhist - clearly a seriously important place and us tourists should let them enjoy it in peace. We did however catch a rickety old train from Colombo which rocked and rolled like a raft in high seas but the surrounding villages and countryside was well worth the trip to Kandy and the Botanical Gardens was a much better place to visit than this temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Be warned you will be harassed by men offering tours if you go for one of the ceremonies. If you don't want one let them know straight away when they approach you don't want a tour or if you do agree on a price before you start. We didn't have one and still enjoyed our experience but many people around us did so it's completely up to you. I'd recommend going as you get an insight into Buddhism and there is a really big museum of Buddhism from around the world which is included in the entrance fee- definitely worth a look. The grounds themselves are also very pretty and many people stay after the ceremony to relax and take in the views

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We walked down from our hotel to this temple and our walk from hotel to this temple was amazing! This white-colored temple is soothing! Each and every part of this temple has an amazing view! While entering there is small water body on both sides of entry. The inside part of temple is so serene you would want to sit there for a long long time. Lush green garden on one side with lots of wish candles light is a breathtaking view! Must visit!

review_text: we were lucky to be there just after nine a.m., so we could watch the ceremony and see all the rooms. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Interesting place and a must visit while in Kandy. We went there on Poson Poya festival day, there were beautiful processions with dancers and elephants. As a foreigner you have to pay rs. 1500. Next to the ticket office there is a shoe counter, it is obligatory to leave your shoes there. The people at the counter try to scam you by charging rs.200 to leave your shoes. Don't pay them. You already paid your entrance ticket which includes leaving your shoes at the counter. You can give a donation 'for their good service' if you want though.

review_text: Relatively cheap at 1,500 per person and it's a must see if visiting Kandy. Its lovely to witness the locals preying in their temple. review_text: People-watching is half of the experience. The importance of this site to Buddhists from all around the world is incredible to behold. Come here around 6 pm (check the precise time with your hotel), which is when they open up the inner sanctum that contains the Tooth Stupa.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This Temple is situated in the heart of Kandy and is open to everyone regardless of what faith one has. The Temple was once the Royal Palace but today it is one of the holiest Buddist Temple in the world. I as a Christian, was priviledged to to visit the Temple with my Buddhist, Sinhalese friends. One needs nto have their arms and legs covered. In respect tourists are given sarongs to cover up if one is not appropriately dressed. As arranged by my friends I also had the privilege to view the Tooth up close enclosed in a jeweled, gold casket in a special room. One can view this through a viewing point from a distance in an open area.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is the holy shrine of Lord Buddha's tooth and is the no 1 temple for Buddhists around the world.Make sure they you have a tour guide with you so as to explain the various meanings of the paintings and the statues in the temple.The temple is neatly maintained and shows how Buddhism has evolved over the years. I recommend to visit the temple in the evening since the crowd will be less and the history of the temple can be understood in a better way.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I am not sure this is a must see attraction if you are not Buddhist. You do not see the tooth only the Indiana Jones style crypt that it is encased in. There s a museum at the back and various other exhibitions. Its overpriced for foreigners and to me it was not particularly amazing, but you go and see it just because you are there and there is not a lot else in Kandy

review_text: So colourful and full of bright lights and so much knowledge of its history to learn too. We went during the evening the holly praying time (7.00 - 7.30pm).  The temple was crowded with people wanting to get a glimse of this and offer prayers.  It was an experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have to say that I was extremely disappointed. As a foreigner who is not from a Hindu country I had to pay the premium entry fee to get in which was about USD15. You also have to pay to leave your shoes at the shoe warden. The site itself presents some beautiful architecture and work. I was slightly put back by the condition of the facility and general hygiene. I would have thought that for the amount of money they are taking in for entry fees that the location would be maintained much better than it actually is. All I can say is that the money collected certainly isn't being invested into the site and maintaining to a level commensurate with the fees! If you happen to be in Kandy then you might want to see the Temple, but don't go there just for it unless you are a pilgrim and it is part of your religious journey.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple and the surrounding property are beautiful, and this was a nice place to visit for a few hours and walk around. You don't get to actually see the tooth, a fact my friend and I discovered after a lot of walking around and asking/pointing to our teeth. There are processions twice a day that we would have liked to see, but we had limited time, and other places we wanted to see, so we had to miss it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a must-visit attraction.  Inside the temple there are a range of areas - upstairs where you can see the tooth (covered) and bright flower collections.  The architecture throughout is magnificent.  At the back of the temple is a hall giving the history of the Buddha tooth through time - that's a wonderful hall.  There is also the international Buddhist museum which has a room for most countries in the world where Buddhism is prominent - a must-see too.  The shop is inexpensive and has a wide range of souvenirs.

review_text: A beautiful temple. Once you are done taking your tickets (there are different prices for Sri Lankan citizens and foreigners), which may get a little chaotic at times, and you are inside, you can feel the grandness of the place. In spite of the crowd and occasional shoving and pushing, breathe in the elegance of the old architecture and divinity of the temple. Once you are done seeing the idol, come and stand on the opposite side behind the long wooden desk. The flowers offered by people are arranged here in different shapes by the staff. You can chip in too. You can sit and spend sometime on the lower floor where they keep playing music with traditional instruments.

review_text: We went to the temple before sunset, which was nice to see it during the day and then lit up. Men and women remember to wear long bottoms and covered shoulders(Sri Lankans go for white clothing as respect) as my partner hay shorts and he had to get a pricey sarong outside the temple. As we were purchasing tickets 1500 each, a guide persuaded us to take us around and we agreed on 1000lkr. Then once in, you have to leave your shoes at a kind of cloak, and  they ask for some donation. The guide was a nice guy, and actually explained a couple of interesting stories about the history of the temple, which kind of saves you from having to read your way through. It's a nice temple, though the infrastructure isn't that impressive. Nice gardens. However, I would recommend going if in Kandy!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple during the special festival time. It was lovely atmosphere. Very beautiful on the outside and in. The main thing to say is to beware of some guides. We were waiting to buy tickets when we were accosted by someone who insisted he take us round for 2000 rupees which we refused. He then went on to say he would take us round and we could pay him whatever we wanted. Safe to say he did not explain much, left us to read the information ourselves and left to chat to some friends for 10 mins. We were not happy with his service and gave him less money. He was then hassling us for money and shouting at us. We managed to get away from the situation quickly. What I would say is that there probably isn't much need for a tour guide but if you want one just be careful. Otherwise the temple itself is beautiful.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you're contemplating a tour of Sri Lanka, this is a must see stop in Kandy. There are 3 ceremonies each day, it seems the 6.30pm event is the most popular and spectacular. There are 2 lines inside, one general and a second one to see the relic closer, however you will get "pushed" by quickly. An incredible experience! This temple has strict dress code. It  means no shorts/ no sleeveless  for men or women and removing shoes.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: No 1 place to visit in Kandy, it doesn't looks like much from outside, but the temple and two floors of museum provides an amazing overview of the history of Buddhism, bloody terrorist attacks on the temple and religious customs practiced today.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went to the temple in the early evening to see the ceremony of the tooth. What an incredible experience; the sights, sounds, atmosphere, the devotion and the flowers given as blessing were stunning making a lovely aroma. Certainly a cultural must whatever your faith or belief!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Waste of 4500lkr, 1500lkr each for entry for the 2 of us and a self assigned guide, who even though we agreed on 1000lkr once we realised he wouldn't go away still demanded more at the end, then the show guy would not give our shoes back until we gave him enough money, and kept ignoring us/brushing us away. The temple was unimpressive and crowded, great if you are a bhuddist I'm sure but for the casual tourist i would pass.

review_text: There are certain pooja and offerings done for the sacred tooth relic and you should be aware of the timetable in order to attend/ observe such events. review_text: The temple area on the northern shore of the Kandy lake is a beautifull day and evening time stroll. review_text: I've travelled extensively throughout Asia and I am aware of the importance of dressing appropriately especially when visiting temples. I made sure I wore a boat neck dress which was quite long and which covered my shoulders My husband wore long pants and was immediately told he could go in but I was stopped by the female guard and rudely waved away. I asked what the problem was and she pointed to my sleeves, apparently she felt they were too short. We had a Sri Lankan driver who is a Buddhist himself, who when he came to pick us up was amazed that I was not allowed in and couldn't understand why. He said he would have told me if he thought I would have had a problem with my dress. It was quite disappointing as it was our only chance to go. So just a warning make sure you wear something with longish sleeves as well as an appropriate length.

review_text: Traditionally, one must remove shoes upon entering temples.  As this is a very popular tourist destination, there are so many people going in & out. review_text: Very crowded in the evening, but definitely a must if in Kandy.  There is a long line for a brief look at the tooth, but our guide walked us through the praying area  (stay to the right up the staircase) so you could see the shrine without having to wait in the very long line to avoid a bit of the crowd.  In the back is a pagoda where we were told the independence documents were signed, so there is a bit more history here then just the tooth, hence it may be nice to have a knowledgeable guide or guidebook there with you.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was to be one of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka.  It is indeed a beautiful building and easy to locate by the lake.  This is a very important site for Buddhists and of great historical significance.  On entering the complex you follow the crowds in, there is a counter for "foreign visitors", first to deposit your shoes and then purchase higher priced entrance tickets.  Guides hover.... We took the services of a guide which was helpful in view of our limited understanding of the complex and the history behind the tooth relic's presence.  We visited during the morning and it was very crowded. As people make their way through to where the ceremony takes place it becomes extremely congested, however the crowd is generally good natured, although we did experience pushing and concern that if someone fell, especially given the numbers of young children and babies being carried, it could potentially be dangerous.  Once away from the main hall on the upper level it was much less crowded and there was more opportunity to absorb the atmosphere. Beautiful flowers for devotional offerings abound and the stalls outside were doing a brisk business. Just outside is a great coffee house "Natural Coffee" which has to serve the best coffee in the whole of Sri Lanka.

review_text: The temple has a dress code which is basically to be covered. No open shoulders or legs. The tickets for foreigners are expensive. So do find out the timings and visit accordingly. The area around the main shrine has a lot of people meditating and praying. One can offer lotuses to the God. Once you come out of the temple there are a lot of other things. The scenery is beautiful, there is a pillared hall and an art gallery. There is also a museum which give some the details of the history of th temple. Overall, nice experience of visiting a Buddhist temple of great significance.

review_text: This being a top attraction for both tourists and local pelgrims, the place gets a little bit insane, especially filing by to view the tooth. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Seeing people praying and making offerings of flowers and gifts was moving. And apparently in the evening the temple can be flooded with pilgrims. We visited during the day to avoid Kandy's traffic jams (our driver says after 4.30 it's gridlock). The temple is reasonably interesting from outside but not really spectacular and once inside you can't see the actual gold casket which houses the Buddha's tooth relic. There is one temple area inside which has stunning Buddha statue and ceiling painting plus a good explanation of the tooth relic. The tour guides etc talk of the Temple of the Tooth as a highlight of Sri Lanka's "cultural triangle ".  And if you are a Buddhist then it's a MUST visit. But for western tourists Kandy city itself is not very attractive (very busy, the food market gives a flavor of full on Sri Lanka but is a hassle) And for me the Temple was not as impressive as some of the other  truly stunning  sites like Sigiriya (Lion Rock ) or Dambulla Cave Temples (see me separate reviews). Once inside Photos are allowed - but of course out of respect you should never pose with your back to the Buddha statue. Dress code: the strictest we found in Sri Lanka - with a military guy on the entrance checking everyone and sending away even men in shorts! Like many temples and churches women must cover their shoulders and top, and legs down to ankle (but no need to cover hair). And men the same . A friendly opportunist stall holder outside warned us we would not get in wearing shorts - so when he was proved right, he was happy to sell us both sarongs. Guys - tell yourself if David Beckham can wear a skirt....

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I loved Kandy with its rich culture and history, and if you are there, you cannot miss the Temple of the Tooth. I am sure you can google all about, but I think its worth to mention a few practicalities. There are ceremonies/prayers twice a day, where public can attend. I joined the evening one, which is around 6 PM. Make sure you buy flowers before entering and then you "plant" them one-by-one in front of the altar. As to most sacred places, you are oblidged to take your shoes off (at the entrace for some fee they will keep it for you safely). I always wear thick socks (for hygenic reasons) to these places as you dont have to take them off. When the ceremony begins the monks start the chanting and they open the inner altar which in order to see you have to stand in line for. Beware, its going to be hot and long cuing, so have water with you and a fan if you have.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Cost four hundred Sri Lankan rupees to enter.  Lovely seeing people worship in this special place.  Take a donation of around twenty five rupees per person for the guy who minds the shoes whilst you go into the temple.  It's also a good place to buy prayer strings and small buddhas.  You can also purchase flowers here as an offering in the temple.  Read up in advance.  There is no guide book available and it's not clear what each area relates to without some sort of explanation.  You may wish to wear socks as the ground is so hot.  Be sure to cover your shoulders and knees here and do not wear a hat or head covering when you enter the sacred area.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Great interesting place Need to pay again! 750 rupees which was the cheapest I've paid for anything in Sri Lanka , considering everyone only interested in dollars. Ladies need to take Scarf OFF! All should be covered.  No shorts . Beautiful statues inside and peaceful! Nice tusks and golden statues Contemplative !

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is nice to walk around and interesting to look at. Beware outside there are lots of unregistered tour guides. The temple does not want you to use them and they are just looking for money. You need a long skirt or pants, woman before me had her knees covered but this wasn't enough. Sarongs are ok to wear. Flowers for sale just after the entrance, no price just a donation to be made but they were looking for more after we have them 200 rupees. You need to give some money for them to take care of your shoes while inside also. Def worth a visit anyway

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a must see whilst in Kandy. We visited this as part of a tour of Sr Lanka. Our tour guide made sure that we witnessed the moment the casket was visible to the public. This is a very important place for the people and is very busy. You have to remove your shoes and leave them with a shoe minder who you have to pay a small number of rupees. A tip - take socks as the floor gets very hot in the afternoon sun. The sound of drums and flutes echoes around the temple. A visit to the museum is also interesting and explains the history of the tooth.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: As the City of Kandy was grown around the tooth relic temple, it is must visit if you are visiting Kandy. But if you visit the temple during pooja time, as we did, there will be a huge rush. In fact you can not see the tooth, you will get to see the casket were toot is supposed to be kept. Architecture and the building around the temples are worth a visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a must see place to see the devotion of the Buddhists of Sri Lanka or any other.So much of history behind it. please read and then visit Need to be properly clad covering shoulders and knees. Remove slippers or shoes at entrance and take it in a bag with you. Beautifully decorated,illuminated sorrounding during festivals especially during the Perehera season called the Dalada Maligawa in Sinhala and thousands pay homage to the Buddha, with offerings of flowers and the like.In August it would be very crowded but worth the visit

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is certainly one of the better temples we have seen in Sri Lanka.  After awhile one begins to think, "Not another temple ".  But this temple was worth the visit. We were ripped off by short changing.  (We have come to recognize thus is very common in Sri Lanka). This lowers our tone for the rest of the experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Along side the lake in Kandy, the Temple of the Tooth houses the most important Buddhist relic in Sri Lanka – a tooth of the Buddha. We were lucky enough to visit during the morning when there are more worshipers than tourists. Best to pre-book tickets and you need to be properly dressed, ladies covered shoulders and men in trousers, no shorts. Shoes need to be removed but there is a kiosk by the entrance where they can be stalled for a small fee. It was a incredible visit, but we did feel we were gatecrashing on what is a very important pilgrimage for the many.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I would say this is sort of a must do when in Kandy kind of thing. Its actually a complex of temples, museums, stupas and more or less holy buildings. Its rather crowded and the tooth of Buddha is kept well safe under a little dome of 'gold'. This place is a temple so act accordingly. You need to remove shoes that is handed in for safekeeping. The entrance fee to entire complex incl museum is 1500 LRP.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a remarkable place full of history and interest, and well worth visiting.  If planning a visit I strongly recommend that you time it so that you are present at one of the ceremonies when the casket containing the tooth is paraded - this happens several times each day so that should not be difficult to achieve.  The ceremonial music etc make this much more interesting than just visiting at another time of day.

review_text: We arrived early in the morning and there were thousands of people making their way to the temple. Don't forget that you have to take off your shoes and ladies cover up. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Being a Buddhist myself, a visit to the Temple is always a treasured experience. Having visited the Temple many times in my life, my most recent visit was slightly chaotic. Locals go in free, but foreigners are charged a min LKR 1500 just for entry. The place is really crowded - especially on weekends and public holidays such as Poya in Sri Lanka - so best avoid during this time. Make sure to wear covered clothing from head to foot - ladies in skirts or baggy pants and loose fitting, non transparent clothing - and gents in trousers/jeans and baggy shirts or tee shirts. A certain level of respect needs to be considered when visiting the Temple. Also, you need to remove your shoes, so make sure you wear something you can easily take off and put on again. The inside of the Temple is really crowded, but if you get a chance to see the Tooth Relic itself - please head on the tour!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: the best time to visit is during the morning offering (around 5.30am). We stayed at the hotel nearby only 5 min walk. We visited the place with our local colleague, so we bought flowers and incense for morning offering. It's really a great religious experience.

review_text: I'm sure that if I was a Buddhist I would have had a completely different experience. review_text: The best time to visit is at afternoon around 5:30 PM,spend 45 minutes to walk around and visit the International Buddhist museum at the back of temple. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is well worth visiting this site, in the hustle and bustle of Kandy.  We were with our private guide, and not a group, which was very helpful.  Go when the tooth is being revealed -- there is a ceremony downstairs with traditional music and dress, then proceed upstairs to the viewing area (you will be in dense crowds -- a mix of tourists and pilgrims who are coming to view and make offerings).  As a tourist, I think it is best to stay to the right -- the left side will take you closest to the tooth, but this is the way the pilgrims move, and you can see what you need to without interfering if you keep right.  It is a very unique experience! The Sri Lankan people are very friendly.  One woman gave my son and I a few flowers to place on an alter before the Buddha.  A very nice, spiritual experience.  NOTE: proper dress is required for men and women -- knees  and shoulders must be covered (pants, long skirts, or sarongs). You can buy a sarong for very little money in Sri Lanka and use it for visits to religious sites during your trip.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: What really attracted me to this Buddhist Temple was the interesting story behind it.Unfortunately we didn't get to actually see the Tooth ! Apparently it is only displayed on special days. A short walk from the neatly kept entrance to the stupa like simple  white structure did not prepare me for the ornately done up altars,the glittering Buddha statues and the beautiful paintings depicting the journey of the Tooth and glimpses of Buddhas life. The place tends to get crowded so going on a weekday would be a better idea. Also the sun can be blazing hot so do keep a hat or umbrella handy for the walk to the temple, though once inside you must remove the hat as a mark of respect. Photography of the main idols is prohibited and the caretakers can be very nasty if they see you disobeying orders.  Also being a place of worship,I felt the entrance fees was a bit too high but I guess I would still pay up as its the main attraction here. Fortunately it's located in the heart of the picturesque little town of  Kandy and easily accessible.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Leaving the capitol of Colombo and arriving in Kandy was a beautiful change in terrain and temperature. Though extremely hot during the visit, it was much more temperate, especially in the early morning when we visited this temple. The lines were long, as it was during the puja, but it was exciting to be there with the many devotees who revere this holy place. There were lots of adorable babes in arms, as it is custom to take them to this temple to receive blessings for a prosperous life. After being herded to the main floor and glimpsing the casket containing the tooth relic, it became less rushed but still extremely crowded to finish seeing the rest of this massive complex. Bonus, since you must remove your shoes, it is cooler padding about barefoot inside the various marble-floored sanctuary rooms. This is a wonderful temple in a lovely country.

review_text: Placed beautifully amid the greenery hills beside the historical and breathtaking kandy Lake, Temple of the Tooth stands proudly with distinguished Kandyan Architecture. review_text: We visited Temple of the Tooth and decided to walk around the grounds before we paid to go in to the main temple. I am so glad we did. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went to the evening worship. The energy was very spiritually strong there. Packed with people. There were 3 different lines. 1 to go upstairs in the hall and look at the relic from the furthest view. One line to pass in front of the room with the relic, and one line to go into the room with the relic (which is not open to all peoples). The pooja started downstairs with drummers starting the influx of the priests who would conduct the service. Then you wait online up the stairs to walk in front of the relic or take the other line to stay further back from the relic in the hall itself, still able to see the casement, but not pass in front of it directly. Didn't matter, because the energy of this place was tremendous. Many groups were there, each group awaiting their turn to go into the room with the relic. Long lines of people to pass in front of the room with the relic and the packed hall with all the people meditating, walking, praying, standing in front of the room area. Flowers and gifts as offerings to the relic was everywhere. It was an amazing experience. Foreigners pay quite an amount, but it helps with the upkeep.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the Tooth Relic is a 'must - visit' when in Kandy. It is absolutely beautiful and in the heart and buzz of Kandy. This historic temple has a beautifully sad story and will touch each person that visits. It is a sacred place and it will mean a lot for the locals if you dress in white when you visit the temple. Also, make sure not to take a photo with your back towards the temple - or any temple for that matter.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a temple that is at the heart of locals' commitment to Buddhism so expect crowds whenever you go. It is an interesting and authentic experience - especially if you buy an offering and put up with the queue to present your flowers at the tiny opening to the central room where the tooth resides in a golden casket. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic) is a Buddhist temple in the city of Kandy. Tooth Relic of the Lord Buddha is deposited there. It is located in the royal palace complex of the former Kingdom of Kandy, which was last capital of the Sri Lankan kings. It is a World Heritage Site mainly due to the temple. It is considered an honour by Buddhists to worship it. Buddhists clad in white come there to worship it. Bhikkhus of the two chapters ( Malwatte and Asgiriya) conduct daily worship in the inner chamber of the temple. Rituals are performed three times daily with the drums beating. The timings of the rituals are at dawn; morning Thewawa (5.30 -7 am), at noon; Nineth Hour Poojawa (9.30 – 11am) and in the evenings; Evening Thewawa (6-30 – 8 pm). A symbolic bathing of the relic with an herbal preparation made from scented water and fragrant flowers called Nanumura Mangallaya is done on Wednesdays. This holy water is believed to contain healing powers and it is distributed among those present. The temple sustained damage from bombings by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam in1998 and now it is fully restored. Famousous Kandyan architect Devandra Mulacharin made the plans for the Patthirippuwa in the upper floor facing its garden area. Kings used it to address the public and now it is used by some Presidents Sri Lanka for the same purpose. Mahawahalkada is the main entrance which is over the water tanks and at its foot of its steps, Sandakada pahana (moonstone) is found. The golden canopy was built in 1987 over the main shrine while the golden fence encircles the main shrine. The tooth relic is encased in seven golden caskets with gemstone engraving.  Kandy Esala Perahera (Procession) takes along the procession casket which is also deposited along with tooth Relic of Lord Buddha In July / August. You get an incredible cultural learning experience, on Buddhism and on Sri Lankan traditions in Buddhism. The architecture of the buildings, the statues including the carvings and paintings were very impressive. If you wish to pay respect to the Lord Buddha; you can present your offerings of flowers. You can view tooth relic if you go in the thevawa times and the timing are given above. In another part of the temple can view the story behind the tooth relic and its value to the people of Sri Lanka. There was much pomp and ceremony with many monks, drumming, praying and lots of flower offerings. It was very magical to observe. You would feel pious and holy as there is no noise made by the public and the way that the Buddhists pray and worship Lord Buddha clad in white, covering the whole body. It is a truly calming experience.  It is tranquil and silent and can concentrate in praying and wearing of white clothes by the people adds on to situation. Therefore visiting of the Tooth Relic Temple should not be missed if you visit Sri Lanka. It is an Important Buddhist place of worship where most locals visit even from far-away places. The Kandy Lake is near it where it has a unique design structure on the top of the boundary walls near the lake which is unique to Kandy. Oil lamps; as lighted in side of the Maligawa inside glass house to prevent wind blowing them out and avoid fire risks, could be kept here and lighted up during functions of the Dalada Maligawa. Entry charges for tourist is 1000 LKR for SAARC countries citizen and 1500 LKR for others. You have to go barefoot and you need to keep your shoes at shoe center found just beside the ticket counter and  donation of 100 LKR is expected when you get them back. Good time to visit is in the evenings with the cool atmosphere and also avoids hustle and bustle that you experience during the day. I think it is one of the most ancient places of worship in the world.

I really enjoyed the museum, it is free for foreign visitors and on two floors. There were some fascinating objects, sculptures and Jewellery. The display cases had plastic coating on the glass which distorted viewing them. Some of the background cards looked like they had mold on them. For such beautiful, priceless objects it is a shame that more care is not given to the display of the objects. Overall, an enjoyable and interesting visit and would recommend.

review_text: I've been here twice now on my visits to kandy..each time just as underwhelming. Always crowded, an excessive entrance fee for tourists, I'm a resident in Sri Lanka but both times made to pay the tourist fee. Then got chased and shouted at by a police woman for keeping my shoes in my bag rather than paying ANOTHER amount to keep my shoes behind a desk. And on my way out the guy behind the shoe desk held his hand out for yet more money, which I swiftly told him no. The temple is interesting if you like Buddhist/religious culture however there are a hundred more temples in Sri Lanka which are a much more worthwhile visit than this one. Take socks for your feet, and don't forget to cover up or yet again you'll have to spend more money on a sarong.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is beautiful however many locals come to give their devotion to Buddha so the crowds are crazy - people are aggressive and tend to shove you out of the way. It is extremely hot inside and you don't really get to see anything due to all of the crowds. They tend to just move the hoards of people through a Congo line procession. Don't pay for a guide, it is not necessary and a waste of money. Also, don't allow the guides to tell you that you can't go in the front entrance without them because you can!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Walked from the Galaxy Hotel (see other review) down to the temple. As others have said, beware of people "trying to help" as you go in - they're after your money. You stop on the left and deposit your shoes, then walk into the temple. We got there around 10am and we'd been told that 10:30 was when the Tooth was open. Timing was good. You queue up and then when it opens, everyone files past a window where you can see the very ornate casket containing the tooth. You can't take pictures and the time to view it is very limited. However, this is a site of religious significance. A lot of people had come to worship and that's the whole point of the place. It's worth a quick look round the museum inside and the Buddhist museum opposite.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
