location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple, probably the most sacred place for Sri Lanka citizens, is really worth a visit if you are interested in the buddhist culture and what it means to people living in Sri Lanka. The temple itself with the wooden chamber and the Buddha teeth is a crowded place. It's really fascinating to see all the people living their religion (we're not religious at all, but respect others) Also the museum is worth a visit to get to know some facts about the history and why the teeth came to Kandy. Bring a bag for your shoes. So you don't have to pay money for people watching after your shoes.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went here as part of our kandy trip and it was a nice to see temple. The security is tight and you maybe searched on way in due to the temple being bombed many years ago. We had a good guide who was very knowledgeable and explained everything about the temple. Was def worth a visit. Be warned you need to wear long trousers for both guys and girls and girls need to wear a long sleeved top. Also you leave your footwear outside the temple and the ground is very hot so be prepared to move quick to get into a shaded area !!!!!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The tooth relic ceremony takes place daily at 09-30 its noisy hectic and unmissable.  The local people are trying hard to honour their God, while tourists elbow their way to the front!! please stand back and watch and do not use your camera !!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A great insight into Buddhism. Very educational and I would recommend going outside of the ceremony times. You still get to see everything but will avoid all the devotees that pack into the venue to worship the tooth relic at set ceremony times in the morning and evening

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A very nice place to visit but sadly they are more interested in taking your money than helping you.  We wanted the audio guide, we had been told you collected them inside.  However on entering we were told you collected them outside.  We were not given an option of a tour guide and once we were 10 mins into our visit, we were told that the shrine to the tooth was closed until the evening.  All that said you should visit if you are in Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were looking forward to visiting this temple as we had heard a lot about it. Men cannot wear shorts so we had to buy a covering. We walked around the grounds and discovered entry fee of 1500 rupees for foreigners. Thought this was excessive as locals enter for free. We don't mind paying a fair entry fee but this was excessive for a temple. After all this is a place of worship. Be warned about the entry fee.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Very interesting ad beautiful temple, definitely worth a visit.  Unfortunately a guy tried to scam me out of the entry fee after I had paid it as he evidently thought a) I was a woman by myself and b) I wouldn't stick up for myself..I told him I'd paid the ticket fee and to leave me alone..he promptly disappeared!  Other than that, a really good experience.  Wet weather= slimy feet you have been pre-warned!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple just as the relic of the tooth was about to be displayed to the faithful. I was amazed by the number of people lined up to see it, and overwhelmed by the line up to get into the actual reliquary chamber. Instead we opted to look in from outside the main chamber - still very crowded but at least we got a glance, and telephoto lenses can make up for the rest. But although the reliquary was the most important part, the rest of the building was also amazing. The palace itself is truly beautiful and there are numerous rooms and chambers that you can explore. Don't miss the tribute to the ancient elephant who worked there for many years and is now taxidermised and on display along with many photos and stories of what he did. I'm not exactly sure, but I think the display and movement ceremony starts around 6.30 pm - that's about when we were there, and although that's when it's most crowded, it's also the best time to get a feel for the spirituality and purpose of the building. I strongly recommend that you check the correct times, and also read up on the story behind the relic and the temple before you go so that you can appreciate it even more.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Evenings are good time to go here but are crowded due to the evening prayer. The place needs you to be wearing clothing that covers your legs and won't permit entry otherwise. Has some nice wall architecture to check out and is a holy place for Buddhists.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: You need to visit here but.... Our guide suggested we went early which we did I am afraid I really don't get it, in a nutshell it would appear there was a man who became a Budda, when he died they kept his tooth, them some one attempted to smash the tooth so it went into the sky and became a tooth, someone then got it back to earth and there have been wars over it!  It is now locked away so you don't actually get to see it. But it is an impressive building and I have never seem so may people trying to catch a glimpse of the "urn" it's kept in

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: To be honest, mid-way through our Ceylon trip, we had seen too many temples. And to visit another one, without witnessing any ceremony going on, wasn't in our game plan. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are a tourist leave your shoes in the car! This isn't just an obligation when entering a sacred sight, or common courtesy, it will save you the £5 fee they extract from foreigners only, the locals are charged only 10 rupees for a segregated holding facility. I have been here many times over the past 30 years and this is the first time I have experienced this money making scheme, and much to the embarrassment of my Sri Lankan friends who implored me to make this comment in the hope it may help to bring to the attention of those involved this discriminatory fee. Please don't let this put you off it is a most wonderful temple, buy a garland of flowers outside of the entrance gates and take your time. I hope that they reconsider this charge.

Be warned as you are asked to remove shoes and hat, the paths etc outside are extremely hot, and remember to dress in a "respectful" manner, covering arms, legs and chests.

review_text: I felt a bit of an intruder in the temple since I am only a tourist traveller and not religious at all. Now, it feels a quite strange to witness the ceremonies through a camera lenze while at the same time it is the most  personal and privare moment for many Buddhist visitors. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I was lucky to have been escorted around the temple, the architecture and paintings were impressive. after presenting my offering (flowers) to the monk, and viewing the relic Tooth, I was taken to view another part of the temple to view the story behind the tooth and its value to the people of Sri Lanka. A truly calming experience which I will take to the grave. Not to missed if you are near or in kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Firstly, make sure you wear clothes where your shoulders and knees are covered and you have shoes that you can easily slip on and off. Secondly, if you're claustrophobic or don't like being in crowds( like Xmas sales) then this is not the place for you! Lastly, if you are allergic to bees then don't go- there are lots of bees due to the flowers that people bring. Yes this is an interesting Temple but the mixture of heat and thousands of people pushing and shoving makes the experience less than enjoyable.

review_text: The majority of people there when we went were actually pilgrims. You have to show great respect and not wear uncovered shoulders or shorts as it is a religious place. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was the first temple we've visited at Sri Lanka. Of course it has his own style and differs a lot from temples in China or other buddist countries. We were there on Saturday and the place were full with locals. The entrance for tourists is not free of charge as it is for locals. And from my own point of view it doesn't worth the price. We have walked around all premises and territory - yes, it's interesting, but not that special as I've expected.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is an exciting active Buddhist temple, which is an important pilgrimage site.  We timed our visit for one of the times during the day when there is a puja and the shrine is opened for viewing.  Chanting and drumming announce the beginning of the puja.  You enter the first floor where the drumming occurs, then go upstairs to the meditation room, and finally to view the casket containing the tooth.  The tooth is not actually shown, only the casket.  Naturally, dress must be modest, and shoes removed in order to enter.  There is a security checkpoint as well.  This was a great experience, and I highly recommend it.

review_text: I loved this place. I went there in the evening to see the temple with the sun going down. There were not so many tourists. The atmosphere was peaceful. I spent one hour to see the place. Entrance fee was 1500 rupees if I am not mistaken.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: That will be my lasting memory of this attraction. Everywhere one looked there were people carrying flowers as offerings to the Buddha. Inside the temple the flowers were piled high and although cash offerings were also being made the flowers seemed to be the favourite. Due to timing constraints we were not able to see the actual ceremony at the temple so missed the pageantry but at least we were able to appreciate the beauty of the buildings and to learn something of the history. We also visited a small archaeological museum at the site which was quite interesting and saw the previous "tusker", Rajah, who had been preserved by taxidermy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth was a very interesting place to visit, however it gets quite crowded. Don't forget to cover your knees and shoulders, and be aware that you'll have to remove your shoes at the entrance (they ask for a small donation when you get your shoes back).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I visited the temple in the evening about 6 pm. It was cooler and everything looked beautiful in the glow of the late day sun. I was very lucky to chance upon the opening of the golden casket holding the relic of buddhas tooth! There was much pomp and ceremony with many monks, drumming, praying and lots of flower offerings! It was very magical!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went on our tour with our private guide. He was a Buddhist himself so was very passionate about it all and informed us ok everything. It was absolute madness but all very organised and well laid out. Everyone was there to worship or appreciate it as a foreigner. Nothing like madness at a drunken festival with rude and violent people. So even if you aren't good with large crowds you may be able to handle this as everyone is lovely and respectful. I highly recommend this as it would be a shame to miss out if you are in or near the area.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a large temple complex -formerly the Governor's residence and very impressive it is. The centrepiece of this Buddhist temple is a remnant of the Buddha's tooth and every day after sundown the casket is partially opened for witness by the faithful- as well as a huge majority of tourists from around the world. So, at the time of my visit, we all stand outside awaiting the appointed hour. Standing in front I was protected by a rail in front as well as a crowd some 10 thick both behind and in front. All had cameras, selfie sticks etc at the ready. Not comfy when those around you are slow heavily armed and see the unusual British phenomenon of queuing with contempt. The crush. Gets worse as action starts - it is then that Ai note the queue. Moves from the side and those behind the barrier don't have a hope. I never got an inch closer to the hallowed object and left this very unpleasant and shambolically disorganised event before any damage was done. As for my wife who struggles with knee arthritis, the score for disabled access is a round 0. I would love to be more positive as the building is magnificent . Buddhism is a religion I find very interesting and would have loved to have had a better view from that perspective as well. Issues of safety ( mini Hillsbrough?), let alone access, need to be urgently addressed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Last time my wife and I visited Kandy we wanted to go see the "Temple of the Tooth" (as they, according to local lore, keep one of Buddha's teeth in a shrine in this temple). I've visited the temple once before about 10 years ago, and my experience then was exactly the same as it was this time around. The temple itself is beautiful and an impressive construction. What does ruin the experience to some extent is the fact that this has also been the gathering point for everyone trying to earn a few rupees from all the tourists passing by, wether it be someone offering to take your shoes before you enter, someone offering to take your picture on front of the temple, someone selling you flowers for offering in the temple, someone helping you get into the small piece of garment that both men and women must wear in the temple, someone else getting you out of said garment when you get out, etc. etc. And even though it's good for tourism and Sri Lankan economy the place is crowded with tourists and some of the sacred atmosphere that should be in a place like this is somewhat ruined and I ended up felling sad for the munks to whom this is actually their plkace of worship, and you could see that they were sometime less than pleased with all the tourist's screaming kids, laughing people, and other people lacking a sense of their surroundings. And I ended up feeling part of the crowd that actually undermined the purpose that was the original intention of this magnificent building. What I don't know is if this is only the case on certain times of the day and if there may actually be calmer hours of the day where you could visit to get a more genuine feel of the temple and the atmosphere and where you are not just getting pushed forward like cattle in a row. Nevertheless, I'd still recommend the Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth), as it is an impressive building and definitely worth at least one visit. Sri Dalada Maligawa should definitely be on your "bucket-list".

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is both a temple and a royal palace. We walked along the long promenade leading to the complex. The Kandyan kings built the complex in the 15th century. It is not at all large or grand the way many other royal palaces are. The Temple of the Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa) is one of the holiest sites for Buddhists. After the cremation of the Lord Buddha the tooth relic was preserved and brought to Sri Lanka. Since ancient times Singhalese believed that whoever holds the tooth relic holds the governance of the country. Sri Vikrama Rajasinha was the last king, along with Queen Rangammal Devi. Interestingly, he spoke Tamil and practiced Hinduism. Nonetheless he was the guardian of the precious Buddhist relic of Sri Lanka, the tooth of the Lord Buddha. He surrendered to the British in 1815 at the Kandyan Convention.

review_text: We arrived for the evening ceremony (that starts 18.30) around 17:30 hoping to walk around on the grounds of the temple. The problem is that we thought that we could do this tour by ourselves by reading some guidelines and signs, etc. but there is absolutely no signs there at all. It makes the whole visit very confusing, cause firstly you don't know really where to go, you just basically follow the crowd, and secondly you don't know exactly what to expect of it. I believe that a board with some explanation of the importance of the place and a map near the entrance would be very helpful. I understand that this is a place of cult and people come there to pray, but since they also allow tourist there - and charge them 1500 rps! - they should inform what to expect and how to behave. Since I don't understand much of this ceremony I cannot really tell you if I managed to whole of it: basically people praying before the tiny room where the Tooth is kept, they are being let inside in small groups and these are the only moments when you can catch a glimpse of the silver case where the tooth is kept. That was it for me. There are drummers and trumpet player downstairs, so you hear the music all the time. After that you can mix yourself in with a totally disoriented crowd that is trying to see parts of the temple. But there is no explanation at all what are you looking at and why. People just move, there is some sense of queuing but in general it is very chaotic. Everybody comes there early to be there at the start but I think there is absolutely no point. Actually we stayed till the end 19:45 and I must say when most of people is gone you finally start to feel you are a part of something spiritual. So my advice - come there even around 19, it is enough time to see quickly the silver casket and then walk around the temple grounds - without crowds. But be aware that the smaller temples and shrines will be already closed. Do it only if you have nothing else to do in kandy or if Buddha is important for you.

Overall it was nice to look at and probably would have been better with a guide. However after paying both admission and for a guide I'm not sure if the cost would be worth it.

review_text: Okay it seemed that some had the best guide ever but for me my guide seemed to "push me" (not literally) through the temple. It all went over so fast! First of al be prepared as a tourist (unless you are from Myanmar or Thailand) you will have to pay 1500LKR entry; save the paper as you will have to give it when entering the actual temple. When leaving the temple I had to pay a extra 100LKR to get my shoes back, it did not say anywhere that it cost that and I fee that I was the only one that paid to get my shoes back... While buying my ticket a guide (with official badge!) offered me a tour for 1000LKR, I thought i was going to learn sooo much about the place but ended up disappointed as the little I already had read was being retold. It seemed to me like he was bored and him speaking to me made me actually feel uncomfortable at times. Most importantly the temple had a spiritual meaning for me and by him rushing me I felt that I did not get to go in my own tempo and this ruined my experience at such a holy place. Tips; 1)If you have closed shoes on KEEP your socks on! The floor is rock and the sun is hot which means that the floor is hot too. 2)Please wear appropriate clothes; cover knees and shoulders. 3)if you like to take your time ether tell your guide priori tour start or go by yourself. 4)by reading a little bit about the history before going I believe the experience will be more enjoyable. 5)If you have trouble with stairs not that you will be walking up and down at least 1 floor. 6)Enjoy!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you've never been to a Buddhist temple then this will be a nice place for you. People from SAARC pay less than people from other continents and countries.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were there for the evening ceremony which gives access to the capsule that holds the tooth (can't see the tooth). It was a terrific experience with the drumming adding to the atmosphere. The temple building is very beautiful. Not to be missed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The building is beautiful, but we felt like we were intruding on the people praying. You can't see the sacred tooth as it's housed behind doors. There were lots of people dressed in white congregating outside to hear a guru speak. Interesting to see but you don't need a guide.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Having said that, given the entrance charge, it is place tourists are expected. The experience is amazing, sights, sounds, smells. The rest of the temple is fascinating as well, but unless you are in the know you do need someone to tell you what you are looking at.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: To start, as a Westerner I have to be sensitive and respectful of cultures and religions other than my own. My comments come from an informative perspective, instead of a critical one. I was first tuned away at one of the entrances because my shorts did not cover my knees. After walking around a bit I realized that I could cover my knees with my wife's scarf, and wear it as a skirt. Although the entrance security guard was not too happy with me, he did help me put it on properly. In addition to the dress code, the security screening was really extensive.  More so than any other temple I have visited in SEA. The grounds are beautiful and the buildings magnificent. The entrance fee into the temple however seemed a bit unreasonable. I understand that prices for locals should be made accessible, to allow them opportunity to pray, however the foreign price of 1500 rps is simply relatively too high for me to justify. I have never and will not pay this amount to enter a house of worship and prayer, regardless of tje country or economy. I am sure it is beautiful, but you will have to find out for yourself. It is worth a visit for the grounds alone.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We have visited many temples and mosques, Hindu. Buddhist, Moslem. The Temple of the Tooth is the most important Buddhist shrine in Sri Lanka and we visited on a particularly holy day. Its very pleasant and you do not feel pressured. You buy a little platter of flowers  and dedicate them and give a small donation which is a happy experience . There is a route through the temple, just follow those who know where they are going.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Close to the centre  and next to the lake, a very sacred site. Tooth relic in the main building. No visible sight since contained in a visible area well protected and only brought out on special occasions. Photographs allowed. Next part of the site was the museum which was quite good and interesting.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our driver was good enough to guide us through the mayhem that was the evening ceremony where the doors are opened revealing the holy relic. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have to temper this a little as we have visited many many Buddist temples all over Asia. This is a very grand place in size, but somewhat underwhelming in terms of the site itself. Also a total lack of monks, which seemed strange. . Also, the tooth itself, or the stupa it is housed in, cannot be viewed. However, just for history alone is worth visiting.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: You must visit this place, even if you are just hopping for a night. Best time to visit this place will be post sunset. It's brilliantly done, the carvings on the wood are a masterpiece of its own. It's a bliss to connect amazing history to this temple, we had Nuwan (our tour guide with us throughout the trip). He is reachable at travelwithme48@gmail.com or whatsapp him at +94-72325-9091 Visiting this temple during a hot day can be a bit harsh - kindly plan your visits post 6 pm. Don't forget incase you are in your shorts- you are expected to cover your legs with a lungi (they sell at the entrance), even for women it is  important to cover your legs and shoulders (be a little cautious if you are wearing spaghetti or tank tops) The management of the temple is extremely humble and approachable if anything needed. The sculptures/photos have headers well written in english- so language should be a problem.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: An important part of the Buddhist faith in Sri Lanka, the temple is visited by hundreds of locals and visitors every day. Yes, there is so much to see, it's a huge complex and you could spend hours here. Very interesting even for the non Buddhists. A sight that you shouldn't miss if you're in Kandy

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Having visited many places of worship in India and rest of the world this is one of a few places where visitors are asked to pay an entrance fee. In my opinion all places of worship must be accessable free of charge to any one interested. Charging a fee to reduce the waiting time (especially for those with limited time) is a practice I have come across elsewhere. Also charging disproportionate surcharge for foreigners too is in my opinion deplorable. Why not include a small surcharge in the visa fee or at the port of entry instead? The place itself is crowded as you can expect in a religious place of such fame! Do avoid public holidays and weekends if you are looking for a quick experience. Those who are interested in religion, history and culture this place is definetly worth a visit.

review_text: Clearly your experience may be completely different....on a different day and at a different time.  Nonetheless we went to the evening ceremony at the Temple of the Tooth.  Beforehand we walked around he grounds plus visited the museum on world Buddhism.  We then entered the temple 45-60 minutes before the ceremony was to begin.  We sat on the floor along with many worshippers. Everything up to this point was truly enjoyable, informative, relaxing and inspiring.  However as the ceremony began there was such a crush of people, it became unbearable and frightening.   So many people  jostled for a place in the line to witness the tooth casket that we could barely breath.  Pushing and shoving. Picture takers blocked views and elbowed others.  We escaped as quickly as we could. If you plan on going, pick your time and be prepared.  IMHO, a bit unfortunate that such a significant and inspiring place is being overrun.

review_text: My partner and I visited the temple around 6.00 after the Kandyian dancing next door (which was fantastic btw). Entry is very expensive at Rs1500 for tourists (love the discrimination!) and the experience for us was horrible. There was no information on what we were seeing or where to go inside the temple, so we just sort of followed the crowd to where the door opens and you can see the tooth (apparently). A virtual rugby scrum ensued (and I played rugby...), with people pushing, kicking, screaming and any short people left gasping for air. There was no chance to see the tooth, but even if there was, we just wanted to get out of there. I understand this place holds great significance for Buddhist people, but if you're not, it's a truly horrible experience. We try to be respectful of other cultures and religions when we travel, but in this case it was impossible. If you aren't Buddhist, DONT GO!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Kandy symbolises this temple and vice versa. This is a must visit temple in Kandy. Close to the lake, the prayers start at 9:30 am and goes on for 1 hour. The ceremonies including the drums and trumpeting is a treat to watch. Very well maintained temple and neat. Be sure to be in early around 9-9:15 am so that you can have a good look inside.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I feel like I'm going to be a bit harsh here but hopefully you'll understand why after reading... We visited Temple of the Tooth seeing as it was the No1 attraction in Kandy. I'll be honest, once we left Kandy we realised that really, it was the ONLY attraction in Kandy. We arrived at the the temple and my husband was wearing long shorts, below the knee. He was told that he couldn't enter so we were about to leave when I noticed one of the security guards gesture to a roadside seller. A few seconds later, we were accosted by the same man selling sarongs. He pushed and pushed for us to buy a sarong for £30!! and in the end we gave in. He would've followed us otherwise!! When we went back through 'security', the guard smiled at us knowing that he'd just got his commission! We entered the grounds of the temple and took off our shoes. We put our shoes in our bags and went through another set of security checks to be told that we had to take our shoes out of our bags and check them in. Whilst the check in fee was only about 50p, we again felt a bit cheated. We were then ushered to enter through the 'foreigner' entrance - why there's a difference, I don't know. We paid to enter (which in my honest opinion, is massively overpriced) and we then walked around the working buddhist temple. This is NOT a tourist attraction - there are monks working and praying and there are normal members of the public praying to Buddha. I have a lost of respect for these people as tourists are ushered in and out, taking photos and completely disrespecting their place of worship.  I felt uncomfortable and just wanted to leave. The temple is really beautiful and should be respected. I felt that the tourist industry takes advantage of the place, knowing that 'foreigners' will pay a lot of money to enter it. I respected it for what it is but I certainly won't go back if I visit again.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: costs 1500 rupees for entry and if you leave your shoes in the holdall a tip is expected so we put ours in our bag, this price does include entrance to the buddhism museum at the back of the grounds which was very interesting. Beautful temple and lovely to walk around - be careful of the unoffical guides at the front offering to show you around. The tooth is kept in a casket and the casket is only visable a few times a day so try to go when it is open (usually during the prayers) otherwise you pay a lot just to walk around the temple and grounds. The experience was tainted by seeing the beautiful 40year old male elephant chained up around the side of the temple who is brought out for the celebrations and parades - the conditions are terrible and large sores are visable on his hind legs - Not happy to have helped fund the mistreatment of such an incredible animal. wouldnt reccommend

review_text: I visited this temple as part of a tour. We arrived close to dusk, and could hear the drumming outside. Once inside, the drumming was very loud. I wear hearing aides and I wish I had taken them out! The experience was almost overwhelming: the crowds, the drumming, the scented oil burning, walking barefoot over the different textures, the moon rising. I am very glad we visited when we did, but I would recommend a visit at any time of day.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Yes this is a truly iconic place and the (understandable) reverence with which the tooth is held in grabs you, especially as you get swept along as hordes gush past the casket. Make sure you see the lovely library and get there on time for the ceremony they hold prior to opening the tooth casket for viewing. Whilst you can queue to see the tooth casket, far better to bypass the queue and just go to the centre of the room opposite the viewing window - you can take photos from there whereas there is no chance as you are whisked past the casket. Take time to see all the grounds and other places in the precinct. We went early evening after the cultural show nearby, but check opening times carefully.

review_text: The temple complex is nice, containing several hindu & buddhist temples, entrance check is quite strict so bring a sarong. Only a fee for the actual tooth-temple. If you want to catch a glimpse of the little highly devorated stupa containing the tooth, come during one of 3 daily ceremonies. We went for the 18:30-19:00 one. Keep left on the stairs to get close and catch a glimpse, even if people tell you to go via the right side. Expect some pushing, queueing and hurry-up-behavior though, but that's all part of the experience. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: An opulent display of elephant tusks, golden roof lotus tiles and assorted ornaments indicate just how important this temple is to Kandy's collective psyche. The temple itself is relatively straightforward to navigate, but the tooth remains behind closed doors on the upper floor until once a day (at 5pm?) when the shutters open and people can catch a glimpse of the tooth. If you're there outside these hours, not to worry. Plenty to see, and calmer too (lots of people pray to the tooth along the mezzanine). The whole temple is beautifully appointed and has a serious, almost holy air. Well worth a visit. Surrounding the temple itself is a collection of museums that range from bland (archaeological) to niche (tusker) to enlightening (upstairs cultural museum behind tooth relic). Watch out for 'tour guides' out front who charge 1000Rs for a brief five minute tour of the temple constituting somewhat relevant information and a rushed attitude. Ignore them and take your time going through the temple, or pay, take their tour and then redo the whole thing at your own pace.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The tooth relic temple at Kandy is a must visit. The place is of religious and cultural importance in Sri Lanka. review_text: Feeling on entering temple is holy and spiritual! Very neat and tidy. Location besides d lake and temple has great historic value in Buddhism. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth Relic is an important religious site for Buddhists. As such it is visited by many worshipping Buddhists as well as visitors ... and therefore very crowded, seemingly at all times. I am not Buddhist but found it very interesting to see such an important temple active with worshippers. As with many places in Sri Lanka there is a fee for foreigners of USD10 while it is free for locals. Our guide traveling with us went in with us and gave English explanations of what we saw and guided us through the crowds so that we saw all the main rooms. There are many local guides available if you are not travelling with a guide. While you can go in without a guide I don't think you would have a meaningful visit without one. Since this is an active worshipping site there are not museum explanatory signs on everything. I found it very interesting to see the inside of the Temple and hear of the importance of the Tooth Relic. Like other visitors have mentioned I felt somewhat self-conscious with the worshippers there but found it to be a very cultural experience. Modest clothing is required for both men and women. Men need long pants and women need modest dress which covers shoulders and knees.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I visited this temple as part of my first trip to Sri Lanka and a journey to bury my fathers ashes in his home country.  While this temple is certainly busy it is easy to become lost in the beautiful artwork and profound respect the Buddhist community shows for this site.  I found it to be a place of great soul searching and was certainly in awe of the grandeur of the site. My advice to visitors is to approach this site with an open mind.  You will be asked to remove your shoes but I suggest embracing and getting used to this is customary throughout most Hindu and Buddhist sites in Sri Lanka as well as many homes.  Also understand that this site is an active place of worship and show respect for the local population.  Oh and remember to never take a picture with yourself or other people standing in front of Buddha.  I witnessed several tourists doing this and then receiving a stern scolding.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple during the evening procession. The loud drums gave an extra vibe but because there were so many tourists the vibe was quickly lost. To look at the location of the tooth you had to push yourself true the hordes of people.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I accepted an offer from a local inside the temple to act as my guide. Normally I wouldn't, but I was glad I did in this case. You can tip them whatever amount you deem appropriate at the end. It was insightful into the history of the temple and general information on Buddhism. The temple is quite impressive and beautiful. Take your time and enjoy the peacefulness. There is a lot to see besides just the main temple. If you have a guide, they are helpful at explaining the different areas of the main temple. Be sure to ask them (if you decide to engage one) if they will only be guiding you through the main temple or if they will accompany you to the other smaller spots. You will need to take off your shoes and leave them out front. Be sure to visit the smaller temples before collecting them. Also be sure to have your legs covered (men & women) out of respect. I brought a long dress just for this but I did see ladies selling sarongs outside just for this purpose in case you don't have anything appropriate. I also happened upon a few large elephants that live there. Be careful not to get too close on your own. There is an opportunity to feed them if you would like to pay for the experience. You also may wish to purchase some flowers outside the temple as an offering.

review_text: This is a beautiful temple with peaceful gardens and in a lovely location by Kandy Lake. It has allegedly been moved so many times that it is frankly difficult to believe that it is still there (if it ever was) - but for the Buddhists, this is the holiest place on the island and everyone should make a pilgrimage there at least once in their lifetime.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were looking forward to seeing the temple as we'd read so much about it. We went for the 6.30pm ritual where tourists and pilgrims walk past the tooth in its dagoba. Firstly, when we went to pay we found it was 1500 R per person which considering it cost 1000R in April seems an awful lot. This cost appeared to be just for foreigners. We dodged past the guides and also took our shoes off a way before the entrance to avoid the trap of paying to store and collect them - we snuck them in our bags. Once up inside the temple we were caught up in the procession of pilgrims with offerings. The whole experience was interesting, but not particularly peaceful or spiritual for us as we found we were jostled along and got barely a glimpse of the dagoba before we were pushed along. The rest of the temple and buildings were quite interesting - we liked the story of the tooth and where it had come from but the story was cut short by construction work in the new shrine. Be aware whilst you are wandering around there are lots of pilgrims trying to pray and present offerings. The World Buddhist museum sounded interesting but closes at 6pm so we missed that which was a shame, as was the taxidermized elephant in the tusker hall. Overall, it felt a bit profiteering and exploitative of both tourists and pilgrims. Not the zen and calm energy one has come to expect from other Buddhist temples. That being said, the temple itself is in good condition, the best we have ever seen....Although that is likely due to the high number of visitors and thus donations & entrance costs. We wouldn't recommend based on our experience here.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is the holiest temple in Sri Lanka, and justly so as it boasts holding the tooth of  Buddha, a holy relic and sign of power and governance. Kings fought and people died quarreling over the right to acquire it, and it had to be hidden in so many places across the country to be preserved across the years. There is an entrance fee for foreigners of 1500 rupee. It includes entry to the main temple, and two floors of museums annexed to it, a room that has the famous stuffed elephant that served the tooth ceremony for 50 years, as well as entrance to the international museum of Buddhism. The tooth is hidden in a golden container and locked up. It is usually brought out at 6 pm on Wednesdays, washed with flowery water, and then the "holy" water is handed to people to use for benediction. There are also masses at 6 am and 6 pm every day. Might be a good time to be present around that time. I wasn't, but you could watch a movie that explains the basic ceremony within temple quarters. You are allowed to take photos in the majority of temple sites but be careful not to give your back to the temples as it is offensive to them. You should basically take pictures in a profile position while looking towards the temple not giving it your back. There is a place to leave your shoes outside, they will ask you to tip them, but it is by no means obligatory to do so. Definitely worth a visit! Take your time and read a bit about Buddhism and temple before you go, it will help you appreciate the visit more and make the best out of it. Otherwise, hire a guide if you can afford it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Unless you have a religious connection to this tooth, I strongly advise avoiding the time when they open up the one section that is usually closed. Everyone advised us to show up at 6:30p for the ceremony.  What resulted was mass chaos.  We were pushed into a large crowd and unable to escape. A large russian man stood tall to take photos and block exit access for several hundred of us. I nearly fainted as I remained wedged between his large belly and his wife's bosom next to me.  Eventually the crowd pushed us through and we left the temple as quickly as possible in search of a stiff drink to calm our nerves. It's an interesting place, but would be much better and more serene without the shoving crowds.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Ancient Tooth Relic is a must if even passing through Kandy. I must admit that I feel a little awkward viewing a place of worship that means so much to some through the eyes of an ignorant tourist. That said, so long as you are respectful, they could not be more welcoming. Indeed, a troop of monkeys appears to have made the temple their home! (The kind of monkeys that might relieve said ignorant tourist of shiny objects - remain guarded...). The temple is equally stunning as peaceful and contemplative. Do have a look around; the lakes around the grounds also makes for some spectacular photographs of you are so inclined.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: From my very limited understanding of Buddhism I expected a place of peace and tranquility, quiet contemplation and reflection. I was mistaken. There are pockets where this is possible and you will see the Buddhist faithful sitting quietly in them. But the main areas are a crush of people all trekking to Buddha's tooth relic to catch a glimpse of the gorgeous jewelled vessel or more importantly to give an offering or prayer. The buildings are majestic, with beautiful architecture, ornate carvings, frescoes and art work. This capped off with gold lined ceiling and the priceless vessel of Buddha's tooth relic. Every countries primary place of worship is always a must see. It gives you an insight into the people, their culture, their devotion and faith. This is no exception. There are many reasons to visit this wonderful palace/temple. - to pay respects to the heart of Sri Lanka's primary religion - to learn about Buddhism and the story of the tooth relic - to watch the Buddhist faithful paying their respects and giving offerings - to admire the beautiful architecture, ornate carvings, frescos and art work - to enjoy the atmosphere of all the Sri Lankan's enjoying a beautiful night out or - to see the tooth relic or at least it's gorgeous vessel It's worth the visit for any one of the above, but a single trip delivers them all. I recommend going in the evening. Accept their will be lots of people and a slow moving queue, go with it and enjoy the experience. Read the story and get a sense of Sri Lanka's spirit and devotion to their deity.

review_text: Its and interesting place to visit. We went as its recommended as one of the must see sights of Kandy. The temples and buildings are good and there is quite a bit to see. Outside of the main temple in the grounds its a lot calmer. The International Buddhist Museum is in the grounds and that was worth a visit. It costs 500 rupees to get in to the museum, however it is free with your main ticket, but this is not advertised so its easy to end up paying twice. review_text: The temple of the Tooth Relic is magnificent and spiritual. A must for all to visit when in Kandy. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This property exhibits a quote from Albert Einstein prominently in its hallway: "The religion of the future will be a cosmic religion.  It should transcend a personal God and avoid dogmas and theology.  Covering both the natural and the spiritual, it should be based on a religious sense arising from the experience of all things, natural and spiritual, as a meaningful unity.  Buddhism answers this description.” That's all fine and dandy but as a western tourist you are still required to pay an entrance fee, pay to have someone watch over your shoes, cover your knees and shoulders before you can enter and tip the volunteer tour guide that just suddenly appears from nowhere to take you inside. It was hard for me to take to heart the less dogma and theology part of the quote with so many individuals plopped on the floor chanting their mantras in hopes of being heard. The inside was attractive enough, although there was one room where you were told not to take photo's by your guide, after you had already taken them, which was very nice.   Different Buddha representations from different parts of the world. We did not get to see the  Pooja and one can only imagine how crowded that would have been.  Maybe next time. These are the kind of places that make travel worth while.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is the most important Buddhist shrine in Sri Lanka. Built next to a giant tank (artificial lake) built by a king of Kandy to hold a tooth of the Buddha, it is a must see. Full of devotees, interesting architecture and large, but not vast it can pleasantly occupy 45 to 90 minutes of your time before leaving the peace of the surrounding well maintained grounds. Admission. Shoes off. Offering flowers available for purchase outside and in without pressure. A guide is helpfful but not essential, especially if one has read a good guidebook. Kandy itself is a formerly lovely hill town and aristo retreat now hugely damaged by chaotic, ugly development. A tough 3.5 hour long traffic filled drive from Colombo. Much stop and go through highway side sprawl. There are trains which take the same time.but bypass the ugliness and move steadily without sudden stops, blaring horns and road dust. Possibly a bit more awkward, but cheaper and more pleasant than a hired car/driver. You wlll miss passing some attractions (tea factory, elephant orphanage) and road side shops but there are many more shops in Kandy. Look at some photos of the place a century ago and wish you were there then.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Set in pleasant, peaceful grounds. Take off your footwear ate the entrance and pay (donate) for the on collection. The entrance is up a few steps where it's appreciated if you buy some Lotus flowers to use as an offering when you go to the first floor, where the shrine of the 'Tooth' is situated. The tooth can be viewed from a distance three times a day by the public, thus these periods tend to be busier. There's also another shrine on the ground floor surrounded by Elephant tusks. On the 2nd floor, there's a museum (no photos allowed) displaying past donations of jewellry, brass pots, etc.Aso  there is a nice view of the nearby lake. Adjacent to the temple and within the grounds are a Hindu temple, Catholic church and a museum displaying wood carvings and another containing the stuffed remains of the Elephant who used to carry the 'Tooth' during parades. Overall, a must see site.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple of tooth was our first stop for a half a day Kandy sightseeing (we arrived from Colombo on the train). It is a beautiful structure set in a large and green compound which is an oasis of calm amidst all the hustle and bustle of Kandy town. You need to remove your footwear before entering the temple and need to be modestly dressed. Will be a good idea to wear socks, the heat during the day can scorch your feet even if it is just for a couple of minutes. The temple complex is big and has many structures. We visited the main temple which is a collection of many rooms on 2 levels (the upper level holds the sanctum in which what is believed to be Buddha's tooth is placed). This part is frequented by pilgrims and tourists. Once out of this main hall, you will reach a part that holds smaller structures built by many different Kandyan kings and decorated with beautiful motifs all over. One interesting roof holds many medallions of the Sun and Moon. Continuing from main shrine, we entered the rear hall which is filled with Buddha imagery and statues, one small but very interesting piece is a pair of holographic Buddha set in a minute Dagoba whch turns its head as your move around the room, we had a few minutes of fun as we moved around the room much to bewilderment of others around us. We did not visit the other museums and temples inside the complex given it was a hot afternoon and our 5 year old wouldn't cooperate!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I dont know why but this temple still evokes me comparison with the grand palace in Bangkok. I apreciate that they are two different establishments however their importance for the local budhist culture is indisputable. It is definitely one of the main reasons why anyone travelling around Sri lanka should visit Kandy. Unlike the Grand palace the temple of the tooth isnt so massive and golden but it is still a dominant place in the town. It has spacious exteriors with many places for meditation or worshiping. Inside you can feel the history. It is an amazing place and if you are lucky and arrive in Kandy on a right date (the full moon holiday in November) you will get to see the procession with the elephants and men in traditional clothes dancing and acting in the streets in front of the palace. The entry for foreigners cost Rs.1500 but on the full moon it is free for everyone. Just think twice about what you wear when visiting the palace. Long trousers and something covering your shoulders is essential for everyone regardless of gender. Also watch for the self-styled guides who are waiting for the lost looking tourist to offer you a guided tour for a "great price"...

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went there during evening hours and the temple was crowded. Please note you have to pay an entrance fee (how much depends whether you are a local or a foreigner)  to see the temple and you have to leave your shoes before you enter for a small fee. This temple is one of the most sacred in Sri Lanka and has the tooth of Buddha. Of course, you can read the historical significance of the temple on the internet and so, I will not describe it here. Also, please beware you have to stick to dress code visiting the temple. Shorts for men and sleeveless for women are not allowed. You can spend an hour to two in the temple complex.

review_text: We were taken there after the Kandy Dance performance. There were a lot of people and it was getting darker. A guide took us in but he was rushing and talking quite fast. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: As part of our visit to Kandy we went to the Temple for a tour with our guide. The tour was interesting and the temple is certainly a fascinating place. I'd advise that you don't rush too quick through the tour. Our guide had us in and out in less than an hour. Also, be prepared for crowds. Remember that it's an active religious site with a large number of worshippers. As for the price we paid on the door - 1,500Rs each (~£8.50), which is reasonable compared to other attractions in Sri Lanka. You'll need to remove your footwear and can store them outside the temple for a charge of about 100Rs. Alternatively, you can put them in any bag you're carrying.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We spend around 2.5 hours with our guide at the temple.  The site is quite exceptional.  There is mythological, ancient, Sri Lankan royalty, colonial and modern history here.  It's worth making an effort.  There is a taped guide but I didn't see many using it. We arrived in the morning to the sounds of the temple drummers and lined up with the believers to see the casket that contains the tooth relic.  Just watching the passing parade of locals brings offerings is fascinating.  And then shuffled past the open door where the relic (encased in seven caskets with jewels over the top) is exposed for a short time each day. If it's  more recent history that grabs you, there is a memorial in an area where the Tamil Tigers set off a bomb in the 1990s, killing many.  A sobering spot, given the apparent safety of the country now.

You must have shoulders and knees covered to enter. The temple itself is beautifully preserved inside and out. Around 1810 drummers started to play and at 1830 everyone is huddled together to parade upstairs to see the tooth. Queues can be long with some pushing and shoving. You are hurried past the tooth in the crowd don't blink or you will miss it completely. If there is anywhere that the taking of selfies will annoy you it is here! review_text: We visited on a full moon 'poya' day which was not intentional. This means the temple is exceptionally busy to the point of being very unpleasantly overcrowded. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went in the morning for the ceremony at 9:30 and it was beautiful! Men in traditional dress playing drums and many people visiting to worship and pray so it was nice to see that it's still a functioning temple. One thing I will say that at this time is was absolutely packed! I decided to go in the morning as a read that it gets a lot of tourists during the day - I don't see how it can get much busier! Also we were swept away by a man outside who gave us a full tour of the temple and explained everything in detail. I knew we would have to pay him but when I gave him 1000 rupees at the end of the tour he said "sorry it's usually 2000". Don't get caught out and ask price before you begin but be quick! You'll be inside with the guide before you know it!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I loved visiting this temple as once inside it is tranquil and very interesting.  However getting inside is a little more taxing. review_text: While the Temple of the Tooth Sacred Relic Temple is nice, the real highlight is to attend one of 3 Daily Thevava Services. The Tooth Relic Door is opened at 5:30am, 9:30am, and 6:30pm. review_text: The entrance fee is 1500 lkr + 50 lkr for shoe handling. The staff was rude and we practically had to fight our way through guides offering us 1000 lkr guided tours through the temple. review_text: Of course, rating the Temple of the Tooth would only sound too shameful for me, because this is a place of worship and I simply love visiting the temple, any time of the year. I can't really opine here a brief on the history but knowing about the relic is interesting as there is a great story behind it, as history should be. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Be prepared for a hard climb to the top of the " tooth", if possible go early morning when the sun isn't too hot. The views are stunning but it does get crowded and if you have a fear of heights this probably isn't the place to go, especially as some of the climb is via a metal spiral staircase up the mountain.

review_text: One of the main attractions in Kandy town and holds one of the Buddha's relics (a tooth hence the name). Entrance fee + guide was a little pricy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were advised by several locals to go at just after 6pm straight from the Cultural Centre dance to witness the tooth being opened.  Unfortunately this is so popular the whole visit was chaotic, confusing and a little uncomfortable.  We ended up queuing for a long time (with many people pushing in ahead of you which if this irritates you then beware), not entirely sure what for.  We did eventually get to file pass the tooth which is a very brief experience.  Generally the crowds are so big it is hard to enjoy this properly.  We wish we'd gone at a different time to appreciate the beauty of the place better. We were told by a couple of people that foreigners did not need to pay to enter, but I have no idea how this would be possible as there is a ticket office for foreigners and people checking tickets on the door, so we assumed that false info.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: On our 18 day tour of Sri Lanka we had a pre arranged two day stop over in Kandy to visit the Temple of the Tooth which is considered one of the most historic and important sites to the Buddhist religion in the world. Although you can't actually see the Tooth relict it self because of its historic importance you can see the temple were its kept locked safely away behind various doors etc. Our great tour guide Raja who was with us for 12 days of our stay told us of the history surrounding the Temple of the Tooth, we saw a video of the annual ceremony were 100 elephants, 10,000 Kandyian dancers& drummers parade through the streets every August with a replica of the Tooth. The video looked fantastic to see it in real life would be even greater!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This should be on everyone's list. It was an inspiring tour (again with our personalised guide) and you get unrivalled access. Really interesting to understand the history and present day Buddhist religion/culture and again in a lovely location. Do not take pictures with your back to any statues. You have to be bare feet throughout and need to have trousers on for men. Would highly recommend.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is one of the places which has the relics of Buddha across the globe. It is very rich in history. The tooth was gifted by an Indian king. The temple is huge and the architecture is of typical kandyian one. One should really absorb the whole proceedings by meditating in the temple sanctum. I felt really calm and some kind of energy while meditating there. There is a musuem with stories about Kandy kingdom and the artifacts of those times. The temple has separate musuem for its famous elephant. Must visit while  you are in kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a sacred Buddhist Temple in the City of Kandy and holds Sri Lanka’s most important Buddhist relic. The architecture and carvings within the temple are impressive, however you don't get to see the actual tooth. The history of the tooth and it's journey to Sri Lanka is an interesting story.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a holy place for people in Sri Lanka with an interesting history attached to it.  It is quite an old monument which they have recently resurrected.  The temple is a must-see attraction in Kandy.  It depends on your level of interest how long would you like to spend but may be around 2 hours are sufficient if you do not go into too much of details.  Prefer to visit it during the evening time and then take a walk by the lakeside.  It's quite serene.  Parking is a bit of an issue near the temple so plan accordingly.  You tour guide is not allowed inside the temple as they prefer that you hire a guide inside the temple which will cost you 3X the money.  I would not recommend a guide unless you want to delve in the history to a greater extent.  The temple has every major events written in English which suffice your need.  If you have some surplus time then you may want to visit their museum on the 2nd and the 3rd floor.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went there for the 6:30pm ceremony to make sure that we saw the tooth, since this is what all the fuss is about. "seeing the tooth" means that you get paraded along with a 100 of tourists while the devoted Buddhist sit in the middle, trying to pray. You "see the tooth" for 5secs, which means you see the Stubba it's kept in. The are also increasing the prices heavily! Used to be 1.000Rps, it's now up to 1.500 RPS and will increase to 2.000Rps on 01.01.2017. Compared to the overall price level in Sri Lanka that's insane. Our advice: go to a small temple, that is still used as a temple. You'll see, learn and experience more!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Here in this Temple in Kandy, Buddha's sacred Tooth Relic is being preserve. It was built in the 15th century and one of the major attractions in Sri Lanka and it's a must visit place. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is a must visit place. The temple of tooth relic is purely sacred and significant for Buddhists. The temple building and the areas are beautiful and peaceful. As the temple is a sacred place, both genders are advised to dress modestly in order to enter the temple premises.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Good cultural experience and insight into another religion. We visited as part of a 1 day tour that included Pinniwala Elephant Orphanage. We arrived mid- afternoon and were greeted by a pre-booked local guide who spoke good English. I mistakenly had shorts on, so had to hire a sarong to cover my legs for LKR 200. There's a place to leave your shoes before you can enter the temple. The tour lasted around 1 hour covering all aspects with time to reflect and views the fantastic paintings and architecture. Photo's are permitted of a respectful nature..eg panorama views, no person standing obstructing inside the Temple. Whilst we could'nt see the tooth gasket unless during daily x3 ceromonies, the visit gave great insight into a different religion, culture and way of life. truly thought provoking and well recommended. The journey back to Beruwala was 4 1/2 hours mind you which made for a 16 hour round trip, not helped by single track roads, volumes of traffic and the quirks of Sri Lankan Bus, Truck and Tuk Tuk drivers.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited this temple in the morning when it wasn't too hot. Our driver introduced us to a good English speaking guide. We paid LKR 1000 (which is just over £5). Us tourists, were the minority which I quite liked. It is one of the Kandy checklist sites.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited it on a weekday, in the evening. The place was crowded and had a queue. There are counters to remove your shoes. Do take the token. As you step out, on your right there is a hall with carved pillars. Do visit this structure too. There are more temples in the vicinity. If possible visit in the evening to avoid heat.

review_text: This a very interesting place to visit, it can be very busy with local and foreign visitors, you will have to leave your shoes outside the temple in a store and not allowed to put them in your bag, so wear a cheap pair as I could see them being given to someone else even thought you get a ticket! review_text: Got here at 6.30pm in time for calling of the prayers & prayers/offerings. Was beautiful to see at night (& cooler). Very busy in the main temple with a combination of locals giving offerings & coming to pray & tourists. The smells of the incense & flowers, the tea lights burning, hearing the calling to prayer & the drumming, the intricacy of the carvings & statues & ceilings, and the smaller temples all made it a highlight of our trip!

review_text: We went there late afternoon to see the temple in sunset light which puts all the colours in a warm light. The temple consists of a two-storey building with the inner sacred area on level 2. Evey day at 6.30 pm there is a ceremony with buddhist drummers and singers where the shrine is opened and the tooth of the buddha carried forth and back. The ceremony can get crowded with locals and tourists sharing a rather small room. But it is still worth going, exploring the other temple areas, the candle lights and incense sticks that are lit. There is a small museum attached with the only taxidermist elephant  in the country, a bull which died at the age of 50 and was the leading elephant in the yearly Kandy Buddhist parade. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were inside the Tooth Temple by 09:30 at the Drummer's Courtyard to see the door of the main shrine opening. It is a very interesting ritual which only occurs 3 times a day I believe. The drummers and a horn will play for an hour at each scheduled opening. We took some photos and watched for a few minutes until the Main Shrines' doors opened (open for only 10 minutes) then snaked through a big line up to catch a mere glimpse of the gold stupa through a small opening and far back which houses the supposed Sacred Tooth. It was crowded, pushy and hectic but also nice to see the devoted apart from this scrummage just content to sit, chant and pray in this far-proximity to the sacred relic. We lined up again to enter the Octagonal Tower or library which houses ancient manuscripts (again I believe this is only open for 10 minutes 3 times a day as well). Outside you can find the Audience Hall - a lovely carved wood post & roof pavilion with historical significance, the Royal Palace and the Devales. You must pass through security to enter these sites.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple does not look anything spectacular from the outside like some temples do but inside the place is beautiful with really intricate designs unfortunately our photos do not do the place justice. We queued for about 40 minutes to see the 'tooth' in a non moving queue, once it got moving we literally had not even a second to view the tooth. I found the temple very calming (but hot) we are not Buddhists however found it interesting and an insight to Buddhism which seems a calm and wholesome influence. You can purchase lotus flowers or jasmine outside to gift to the Buddha which we did, inside the temple smells lovely as everyone brings this gift. Entry was pricey, donations for looking after shoes is not advertised as a certain cost and guides push you toward the shoe counter so you cannot put your shoes in your bag, guides will also try and see if you want to hire them to take you around the temple. There are lots of rooms to explore inside, you do not get a map when you purchase your entry ticket, there is a map of the outside areas (where you can see the raja taxidermy in one building) when you exit the temple. I would expect that tourists should be provided with a leaflet that has a map and explanation of what is where inside the temple and in the outside grounds for the inflated price they charge tourists. Allow yourself 2-3 hours with queuing to see the tooth and exploring the other rooms and grounds.

Go in the late afternoon as not too crowded to see the ceremony with the Monks giving thanks,but beware gets very crowded with pilgrims,we were very lucky as our guide knew were and when to go and stand which was very important as we saw everything. It was a very rewarding and brilliant insight to the Buddhist culture and its history,dont know the admission price as pre paid on a tour.

Go if you want to say you've been, but you won't see much other than tourists...

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is what Kandy is all about, so be prepared for lots of tourists and of course scammers. When you purchase your ticket they will attempt to take them from you and pretend that you must have a guide to enter the Temple. Don't be fooled as they will want to push you through as quickly as possible to then pick up their next unsuspecting tourist asking for a "normal tip of 1000LKR per person". Take the time to visit at your own pace allowing for a much more relaxed visit with time for contemplation.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A visit to this sacred site is a must on a full moon poya day or during the kandy perehera time. The temple is majestically illuminated during this period and is a photographers dream to capture the place when thus illuminated. People are required to dress appropriately at all times before entering the premises.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Went here as part of our tour with our guide. Something I'll remember forever - so moving! Filed past the golden casket with worshippers and witnessed puja. Lotus flowers everywhere. Other things include museums with artifacts but the actual temple is amazing. Don't miss it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A cool bit of history. Slightly awkward to walk around taking photos as people are praying, but no one seemed very bothered by tourists. Very beautiful inside! Tickets are around 1500 rupees for foreigners, along with a tip for the guys to watch your shoes. The ticket also has free access to the world Buddhism museum just behind the temple. Well worth it to see inside!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The place itself is interesting but it's the regular tourist rip-of that you face everywhere in Sri Lanka. it's 10 dollars per person to get inside the temple which is interesting in a way but if you're not all about buddhism you might just want to skip it and spend this money on something real memorable. You can walk around the temple which is a really nice area and you can enter free of charge after a security check. When we were there it was really difficult to move around the temple because of the hundreds of locals but this actually made it a 'living' place instead of being just a museum. If you have a spare 10 bucks go inside but expect nothing spectacular. It's simply super-overpriced as everything for tourists in Sri Lanka. It's a shame

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Hundreds of locals with offerings. Very pushy and in a rush to get through. The magic door to see the tooth container was so busy and hidden, then opened for a couple of minutes, with wealthy heads pushing through. Officials did a good job trying to organise the crowd.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A cultural opportunity you don't want to miss!  You enter the grounds that are well maintained and beautiful.  Be aware that you must be covered and no shoes on when you enter the temple.  Also, there are lots of steps, so those with balance issues or eye problems be aware that most steps do not have railings!  Inside is the extremely beautiful and full of mystery and art.  If possible, plan your visit on a Wednesday when that have a symbolic bathing of the relic -- the ceremony is breathtaking!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I was expecting more when we went here, we got crowds of pushing people and not a lot more.  I realise that it is a sacred place but it was spoilt by  pushing crowds with no regard for anyone else, especially the blind lady that was there.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: There is a flower shop outside the gates asking you to pay however much you want for the flower, quoting "500, 1000, whatever you want" - do exactly that - we paid 300LKR. Entrance you will be asked to cover arms and legs - generally the ladies have issues here. Ticketing is inside the gates (after the body/bag check). 1500LKR per adult, including World Buddhist Museum (they used to charge separately for that). You can leave your shoes at the counter next door (they'll give you a number), and pay a nominal amount (they dont state how much, we paid 100LKR for 2 pairs of shoes) when you come pick it up. Along the way, there will be people who just stop you or walk/talk with you - just politely but firmly tell them that you don't need a guide and they should leave you alone. The daily music playing lasts for hours, so no need to rush in during the morning and squeeze in with the tourists to try and take pictures so quickly - do the upper story loop then come back down and take pictures. Do look at the map of the place - there are many points of interest, and these also often have donation boxes or baskets so its easy to donate a lot of money out as you walk along (not mandatory though - my fiance is a believer so we did). The World Buddhist Museum outside the main temple, but is well worth walking in and taking a look - there are generally few visitors that make it this far in, but there are many exhibits that depict Buddhism in different countries. Interesting if you are the type to read the small print and have cultural/religious appreciation for this.

review_text: I visited here with my family and it was very hot!! I would suggest going in the earlier morning or evening. There was a lot of people but it was a mixture of tourists and locals going to pray. It was good to see the different relics and gave a good cultural experience and also was aesthetically pleasing. Children got bored at some points. The dress code is reasonably strict women must wear trousers or skirts to your ankles and shoulders could not be seen. Men had to wear long pants and shoulder covering tops. All up it was good to tick it off the list.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Unfortunately, the curiosity of the tooth relic is overshadowed by what is more a tourist trap. This was the second most overrated experience of our time in Sri Lanka (only outdone by an outrageous request to pay 1500 rupees per person to stand for FIVE MINUTES on a footbridge to observe the river we passed on our way to Kandy). Like a number of "tourist attractions" in Sri Lanka, the ticket price has just been hiked up. I has just increased from 1000 rupees to 1500 rupees. That is the price for "foreigners" though, not locals. Unfortunately, this like many other sites, discriminates heavily between visitors & locals. The temple of the tooth does not compare to the Rock Temple that myself & my fiance were fortunate to visit in Dumbulla. Interestingly enough, that site is also free to enter. I am not against some cost but, depending on what you are wanting to squeeze in to your time in Sri Lanka, this can be missed ... or, even viewed from a distance!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

My companion was almost turned away due to having slits in her maxi dress to the knee.  We had to source safety pins to close the slits before we were allowed in.
