location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: There is no doubt that this temple is beautiful, and certainly intriguing given its background! The only downside is that it is incredibly busy - so you can't walk round at a leisurely pace - lots of pushing and shoving. I would advise going on a weekday to avoid this.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Very popular tourist site, but definitely worth visiting in the evening to see the relic casket when they open the doors. You only get a couple of seconds to walk past it, but then you can stand further back and look again, and the rest of the temple is lovely too, with the story of the relic in pictures to look at

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a beautiful place to visit - the temple itself is wonderful, but I think the gardens and surrounding area also deserve a mention.  It is a very peaceful place and seems to be THE place for locals to congregate and catch up in the shade of the trees. The temple itself is very impressive and well worth a visit.  It is very humbling to be standing in front of the tooth relic; we were able to present a lotus flower as an offering (you can buy them at the front of the temple).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is just absolutely stunning! With amazing details and gorgeous statues! It is a bit crowded, but not too bad. Not so many tourists, mostly locals, so thats nice. Recommend not to go in a holiday or a weekend, as it propably is way more crowded then. As in all temples, you have to take off your shoes by the entrance, and the pavement is really hot, so I recommend bringing socks or something if you have sensitive feet. You also have to cover shoulders an knees (Also as in all temples). Note: it is pretty expensive to go in, for tourists it is 1000 rp, and to go in the museum it's another 500, but it's so worth it! Especially if you are really interested in Buddhism, then the museum is a must see! We had a great time!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I would say this was the best temple we visited on our long tour of the island. Beautifully presented, tremendous architecture, art and historic items of interest. We didn't visit during the twice daily unveiling but I think Id like to return when we return. Fascinating pictures of the destruction caused by the terrorist bombing of the Temple. Really quite a lot to see. Could spend a couple of hours slowly walking around the temple and grounds. Make sure you have socks as the ground can be really hot.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went there during the Chinese New Year holiday; the location was extremely crowded by both visitors and pilgrims. The entire complex is formed from different buildings and covers a large area. One of those buildings is the temple of the tooth where the left canine of the Buddha is kept. You cannot see the tooth itself, but only the gold casket that houses it. If you are planning to visit the place, make sure to wear lose closes (especially females visitors) cover your shoulders and legs and of course you will have to take off your shoes as in any other temple in Sri Lanka. There is a special location where you can "rent out" a place for your shoes at the front entrance; you can keep your socks on though.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Having visited a few temples on the tour was not so sure about this one, but glad we did. Only problem for two of us was the extremely hot paths out side on our bare feet (not used to this) but other two put socks on which made it easier. Is a small hose with cold water when you get back out which helps! Anyway, inside was worth the visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is amazing because it is very colourful. It is a nice experience to see so many sri lankan people coming here to honour the buddha. After the temple we went to the buddhism museum, where we learned a lot. Chilling in the garden is also very pleasant.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I was hoping that I would see the actual tooth of Buddha but it is locked away only to be brought out for one day every 5 years I think.   The palace is ok, not as impressive as some I have visited in Thailand but the history of it is interesting and well worth the visit

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The foremost Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka so you really shouldn't miss it. The morning prayers with drumming began the day we went at 9:30 AM.  The temple museums are part of the complex and are also a must to understand why this tooth is so important to Sri Lankans.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Mecca of Buddhism - this fantastic, beautiful & auspicious temple is nestled in the heart of Kandy. The spiritual home of Buddhism, due to housing the Tooth Relic of Buddah. It takes roughly 1-2 hours to see it in full, including the museum which is included as part of your entry ticket. If you can time it with the opening of the Tooth Relic room, then this will make your visit even better. However for a less-busy visit, all other times are fine. The building is visually stunning and overall the experience is excellent.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were very lucky as we visited on the day of Kandy Festival all the elephants were being prepared . We were able to pet and feed them a unique experience. The temple was beautiful to walk around and is very interesting. Wear socks as you need to remove shoes. Also take a cover for legs.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is one of the places you should visit while in Kandy. Expectedly, this place is packed with local devotees and tourists with their cameras. I still remember the guy who introduced us a good photospot asking my guy friends for a tip -- ladies normally get away with it. Be careful if you are driving (without a local driver), parking can get quite expensive if you are caught unaware of the average parking fee by the parking attendant. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A very interesting 'spiritual' experience. We queued up and got to see the relic casket, got various photos of the temple and experienced the hypnotic repetition in the music they play at the temple which is hard to get out of your head once you've listened to the same short piece for a couple of hours. It was worth the experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had been led to believe that this was going to be one of the best places to visit in Sri Lanka. Unfortunately our experience was one of disorganised chaos and a most unpleasant visit. We probably went here at the wrong time of day when the puja ceremony is taking place. There were hundreds of people all pushing and shoving to get into the temple, to get around it and then to get out. There is no crowd control whatever and we were most concerned as to what would happen if a mass evacuation of the building had to be effected. I would never wish to go through this experience ever again. I could not wait to get away from this place.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our guide was able to get us in to the temple too see the evening ceremony when the faithful queue to visit the tooth relic. It is a fascinating time to visit for anyone with an interest in the religion and culture of the island. Timing is everything so a local guide is a must.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I'm not a religious person, but I have great respect for those who are. To see the devotees at this temple makes me have admiration for a religion that is so loving, so respectful of all people and does not judge anyone for their opinions. Greatly needed in this day and age.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: As a buddhist I have visited the Temple of the Tooth so many times since my childhood and each time I feel a sense of energy that cannot be explained. I have talked to many other non buddhist visitors who shared the same view and I believe it to be the reason why so many local and foreign tourists continue to visit this most Holly temple of buddhist culture. You are required to dress respectfully when you enter this premises and if you are wearing shorts or armcut tops they offer you a suitable piece of cloth/sarong to cover yourself properly. So I recommend you wear jeans and a proper shirt/  t shirt if you choose to visit the site rather than going through unnecessary hazzle. There are vendors who sell lotus flowers and other offerings. I would recommend you take at least a few flowers to enhance your temple experience as well as a respect for Lord Buddha as well as the buddhist culture. As a buddhist I don't want to overly stress any non buddhist to visit this wonderful place filled with spiritual energy and vast history. But I will say that you are going to have an experience that you will remember for the rest of your life !

review_text: We visited at lunch time on a Saturday when it wasn't too crowded, but still so many interesting groups of visitors.  Our driver/guide explained things to us, but the story of The Tooth is well illustrated in words and pictures inside the temple. Recommended.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This houses Sri Lanka's most sacred religious relic, a tooth of the Lord Buddha.  As such, this is a place where tourists have to share with the local population.  Consequently it is very busy. The temple dates from the 16th century and is entered via two doors showing mythical beasts.  As usual, shoes must be left behind at the gate. Inside you can do little more than shuffle along at the pace of the crowd, but that's fine because you can take more in that way.  The decorations are elaborate and ornate and very impressive. The relic is housed behind gilded bars. There is a large casket and seven smaller ones, each made of gold and studded with jewels.  You have no chance of seeing the actual relic.  This is reserved for royalty etc. At about 5pm drums are played which adds to the atmosphere. In one room there are a whole series of paintings showing the history of Sri Lanka through British rule, up to independence. All in all this was a very interesting experience and because it was so crowded with locals, you have the feeling of sharing it with them.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Interesting architecture, the old temple is eye catching. All the new construction after the bombing is worth as well, museum is well organised. Down sides - overcrowded, 1000 rupees entrance fee for tourists, separate shoe rack for tourists (at least 50 rupees). We were in shorts and we had to borrow scarfs to enter the temple that our guide negotiated for us ($3 to borrow one scarf is unrealistic) so dress appropriately (long skirt / trousers).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Great to see more Sri Lankans there than tourists when we visited. Our guide took us when the door to the tooth was being opened - it is stunning (from the quick glimpse we saw). Very lively, noisy (in a good way), beautiful place definitely worth a visit. Note as it's a temple shoulders and legs must be covered - my husband just about got away with long shorts that covered his knees.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were there during Poya, which made for a very crowded experience.  If you have trouble with crowds, don't go on a full moon weekend.  We had a guide, which was so helpful!  A guide can be se used as you enter the gates.  We learned so much of Buddhist history and practice. There is so much to see and so much  beauty to behold.  Bring your caMera and plan to spend the better part of the day.

If you visit around 5 PM you will be able to experience the Evening Pooja with drummers and worshipers. If you are lucky, you will be even able to see the Tooth Relic of Lord Buddha.

review_text: Kandy is a town that has the beauty and charm and the peace is there when you are in the Town itself. The nature has bestowed the charm and blessed the land. Just north side of the lake, the golden-roofed Temple of the Sacred Tooth houses Sri Lanka’s most important Buddhist relic – a tooth of the Buddha. During puja (offerings or prayers), the heavily guarded room housing the tooth is open to devotees and tourists. However, you don’t actually see the tooth. It’s kept in a gold casket shaped like a dagoba (stupa), which contains a series of six dagoba caskets of diminishing size. The entire temple complex covers a large area and as well as the main shrine there are numerous other temples and museums within the complex. The following are some of the key sites. You could see the aerial view of the whole temple if you drive up the hill and the Temple is below the valley.. a great sight...Must visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple of the tooth stands in the middle of Kandy city and is mesmerising in its evening glow. We were blessed to be present thereon a full Moon day it witness the serene charm of the temple and surroundings. The temples history is very well documented in the pictorial format within the inner temple and is very self-explanatory. The place is clean and airy being on the banks of the charming Kandy lake. The tooth was never displayed but the whole atmosphere the drums the pipe which are played in the evening when it is worshipped is very soul stirring. If you make the mistake of going on a holiday or Sunday the local crowds are overwhelming which may touch the sensibilities of people not used to crowds but then being from India even crowds hold a charm for us. Even with crowds the place is spic and span. Usually no one is allowed on the grass but you can sit on the stairs and soak in the absolute peace around. The lake is another attraction where one can sit around in peace and hear the hymns being chanted and the drums being played. The tooth temple is a very important symbol in srilankan psyche and one has to visit it to understand why.

review_text: We went at night when there was a hive of activity. The drums bear out their rhythm and we were able to follow the history of the tooth which is one of Buddhism's most sacred relics. review_text: As the holiest place in the Buddhist faith this is an experience not to be missed. Take socks as the ground can be very hot. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We joined so many Sri Lankans who were on pilgrimage to this site and whilst it was an amazing experience we did at times feel as if we were intruding, we were assured visitors are always welcome and to see the numbers of people waiting just to get a glimpse of this historic relic was quite moving. Everyone brings flowers and fruit as a gift to the Buddha and the smell of frangipani was intoxicating. A moving experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a holy temple housing a sacred relic, believed to be a tooth of Buddha.  The tooth itself is not visible, housed inside a reliquary and that kept within an inner sanctum of the temple. I visited in the evening when the devotions were going on.  This consists of huge queues of pilgrims, ordinary Sri Lankans, dressed in white, waiting to make offerings inside the inner temple.  This was very interesting to see although in some of the smaller shrine rooms I avoided entering so as not to be intrusive of their worship (other tourists did go ahead). The temple itself isn't particularly visually stunning, in my opinion.  It's not highly decorated or especially beautiful.  There is also very loud music during the devotions, played by two drummers and a wind instrument.  I think the idea is to be hypnotic, but I really struggled with the volume and repetitive nature.  I was quite keen to leave to get away from it.  That sounds terribly philistine of me I know, but it's true!  If you find music distracting and aren't keen on loud noises, the evening may not be the best time to visit. As with all Buddhist temples you will need to remove your shoes (you may keep socks on if you wish) and leave them at the shoe check desk.  You should also ensure legs are covered below the knees, and shoulders (men and women). Overall I wasn't overawed by this temple and I found a lot of the others I visited more beautiful and moving, but perhaps if I'd visited when it was quieter I'd have had more chance to absorb the atmosphere and reflect.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

The entrance and the steps to the Holy Tooth was very crowded, the folks were really pushing us forward and in addition it was really hot! We finally enjoyed the buildings but we missed to see the reliquaries. Maybe other time would have been a better experience.

review_text: In the heart of the city of Kandy is the the famous Temple of the Tooth. Solely for it's value to Buddhism this is a not to miss. Although parts of the temple is ornate and the buildings pretty, I somehow expected more for such an important artifact. But maybe thats the point. If you are going to Kandy, this is a central part of the Buddhist experience. There is also a free audio-guide included in the tourist price – not sure if its any good. P.S. Better yet – book 6 months in advance and go to the yearly festival.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We have visited the Temple of the Tooth (Sri Dalada Maligawa) during our visit in Kandy. The temple is very big and inside it is very nice. Watch out: you cannot enter the temple with short pants!! A lot of local people come to see the event, which takes place at around 17h00.  Then you can see the relic of the tooth. Also the music is very nice.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Cost 1000 rupees a person to get in, the temple requires you to take off your shoes when walking around inside. Would recommend bringing a bag or something to carry your shoes whilst inside otherwise you can pay to leave it outside (Not sure on the cost of that). The temple had some nice rooms which tells the history of the tooth. Was a nice read. The tooth itself is kept on the 2nd floor at the back, when the time is right they open up the "window" to see the tooth, you can queue up which takes you right up to the window but you cannot take photos and don't really get any time to look as they want to keep the queue moving quickly. You get about 1 second to look unless you donate! When I first walked passed I didn't know what to look for and didn't see the tooth at all. FYI it's the gold thing right at the back of the room. There's also a guy at the window looking for donations (which in my opinion further distract you from the tooth). If you missed the chance like I did, you're just better off walking to the front and taking a long look from distance, it tends to be crowded because there are people there taking photos. Beside from the tooth the temple itself is big and you can take a look around outside,  there's an area where they have a lot of candles and incense but be warned, they have a lot of sand / small rocks on the path, so if your feet aren't used to rough terrain, then bring a pair of socks or something you don't mind ruining!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: What better way to get a greater understanding of the history of Buddhism than to visit an ancient temple, and none better than the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic! This magnificent Temple is a located in the city of Kandy and offers a glimpse into he history of Kandy, Buddhism and the sacred beliefs of the Sri Lankan people. Observing the temples golden roof glistening in the sunlight makes you appreciate the importance and significance of this beautiful location. When you enter the temple the magnitude of the temple becomes apparent! The 200 year plus wooden interior scream history with carvings and decorations. Throughout the day, offerings to the Sacred Tooth Relic are placed within the temple, creating a blanket of flowers which fragrance the whole area, the fragrances are intensified and complimented with the burning incense drifting in the air. An essential experience & Highly recommended place to visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: For many people, this temple and its "tooth" is the biggest spiritual thing in the world. I can not say this. The area is not exceptionall no amazing structures around, no paintings. Only one room is beautiful, and its the one where the paintings tells the story of how the "tooth" got into Sri Lanka. If you want to see the tooth itself you must come precisely in the morning at around 9:30 or at evening at about 18:30. At these times a processions are taking place and only at this time you can see the tooth. Normaly the tooth is concealed. If you bought your ticket and you want to go out and next time in, they will refuse you. There is one trcik to be used here and you can attend the temple withou paing. If you enter the temple and instead of going right where everybody is going you go left (where is the exit of the temple) you can skip the entrance and get inside trough exit door. Nobody is watching them. Or try saying to the ticket inspector that you need to go to the main office to get your ticcked validated. It worked for us. Take enough water with you inside. There is nothing much to watch inside, you can easily run the temple in like 1 hour or less. To sum up, for this temple I had my biggest expectations and it was the biggest  dissapointment for me.

review_text: A guide foisted himself on us at the temple gate and then proceeded to lead us around.  He was really quite rude, ordering us to be quiet when he wanted to talk and then repeatedly telling us throughout the tour how much we should tip him at the end. "1,000 or maybe 2,000 rupees," he kept saying. During the tour he failed to mention that much of the temple exterior has been restored thanks to an enormous Tamil Tigers truck bomb which exploded there in 1998.  Generally, the traffic is so appalling in Kandy that I would avoid the city altogether and go straight on up to Nureya Eliya.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: An amazing location, with some stunning architecture and history. Slightly spoilt by all the crowds, as you are overwhelmed with the number of tourists. Pushed past the actual sacred tooth, which you can't really see, in a long queue. Worth seeing.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was an amazing experience.  Our guide ensured we were there at the morning opening of the shrine containing the tooth.  Although you don't actually see the tooth just a casket.  This was obviously a very important experience to throngs of devout Buddhists!  So be prepared for a bit of a crush, but worth it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Different experience to all the other temples I have visited on my travels. Equal mix of locals and foreign travellers, what I liked is that everyone was treated equally, no special treatment for us since we were foreigners - that is how it should be! Respect for that. Bonus - we saw an elephant up close walking around the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A truly beautiful example of Sri Lanka's Bhuddist heritage, you'll not be short of opportunities to take pictures, and walk around a little of the well maintained and wonderfully presented history surrounding Bhudda and the sacred tooth. What made our visit especially enjoyable was the timing to coincide with the ceremony to view the actual casket - more photos! However, the big negative for us was the sheer number of visitors. Lots of jostling, queueing, selfie sticks and noisy tour guides with their groups. One would imagine a very early or very late visit would offer a quieter, more enveloping experience... hence only a three star review - we went around 1030 and it was already too busy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is beautifully maintained as it is a sacred site and security is quite tight. Ensure when visiting that your knees and shoulders are covered otherwise you will not be allowed to enter. Shoes must be removed but there is a shoe depot where your shoes will be looked after for a small fee. It’s very interesting walking around the temple and looking at the artwork and decoration. You can also buy lotus flowers to place before the altar of the tooth. Definitely worth visiting.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The building itself is beatiful from the inside and outside as well, but we didn't get the exprience expected. There are two different entrances, for gents and ladies, both inspected by police men. I was wearing a long skirt and also covered my shoulders with a scarf, but the lady at the entrance made me pull my skirt lower (which already covered the total length of my legs) and rolled my whole bust in the scarf. I found it interesting as I saw a local woman entering with a way shorter skirt... So tourists, be prepared to cover your whole body! After, you have to take off your shoes and hand them over to the counter and you HAVE TO pay a 'donation' (which is supposed to be facultative, but here you are enforced to do so). Then you purchase the ticket, a little overpriced for tourists, just like all other sights in Sri Lanka. We went there around 10-11AM, I don't know which would be the right time to avoid crowd, but it was very crowded. Mostly local people, who get unbearable at sacred places, thrusting like idiots, their kids crying and yelling all the time. We couldn't see anything because of the crowd, so we decided to get out as soon as possible. Inside the temple, there were also some places asking for donation (not that the entrance fee they make tourists pay wouldn't cover any donation). I liked the buliding from the outside, where it was not so crowded, but from the inside it was unenjoyable. A buddhist temlple is supposed to be peaceful and calm, this one is everything but calm. They just try to make as much money out of their beloved Buddha as possible, but you don't get the real experience of such a sacred place.

review_text: Although you can go anytime to view the temple, our guide made us be there at 5:30am. As such we were able to get into the viewing area to see the actual casket with all the devotees. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the Tooth is the centre of attraction in Kandy.Wear a white dress before addressing the god.It has a great museums depicting how the tooth arrived Kandy over the generations.We haven't seen the exact tooth but it all lies in the faith.A must visit for foreigners if you visit Kandy.The place is well maintained.We worshipped at 9AM as soon as we reached Kandy.This place is by the Kandy Lake which provides good views.The Entry fee is 1000LKR for foreigners and 500LKR for SAARC countries.You are allowed to take Pictures and videos which makes the traveller to capture memories.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was one of the highlights of our visit to Sri Lanka.  The Temple and the activities were something to behold.  The Temple was very crowded in the evening, but that was part of the experience.  Be sure to take time and read the history of the Tooth before going to the Temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It starts with the usual judgement on whether your dress offends any particular god or not. Luckily we passed the test, but the girl in front got called back for having leggings on that were slightly too see-through. Next is the process of handing over of shoes so that you can enter the temple. This involved an unruly pushing and shoving from a crowd of people desperate to hand over their money. They asked for money to get the shoes back too - nice trick. Finally inside the temple. Not much too see. You can't usually see the magic tooth itself, but you can look at the shrine that the tooth is kept in. Lots of people prayed in its direction and then put money in a box. Considering the poverty and pollution that I'd witnessed in Sri Lanka up to this point, seeing so much energy expended on an old dog's tooth left me feeling angry. Want spiritual enlightenment? Go and do something useful, don't waste your time at this money making scam.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: While the place was jammed packed with pilgrims and tourists, I felt the sanctity of the place was preserved.  Every where one could feel the devoutness of the local people who came to pray.  Entire families sit on the floor lining the back wall in front of the chamber of the tooth deep in reverence and prayer. Visiting the Temple for the evening service, with the lights all glow, was definitely one of the highlights of our eight day visit to Sri Lanka.  This is not just a tourist attraction.  This is a place deeply revered by the majority of the population in Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: As Indians, we found this temple very similar to ones found on the western coast. The music, shrines all resembled our country but for Lord Buddha replacing Hindu Gods. Although the actual tooth is not displayed, every evening around 6.30 PM, casket containing the tooth is displayed - what a majestic site. Also don't miss to watch the drummers playing in the ground floor around the same time. For westerners, this may seem crowded but the overall atmosphere is serene. Added bonus is the beautiful Kandy lake (one should visit before the temple visit, before sun sets), which is just on the right side of the Temple. Overall experience - Exciting.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This time we visited in the evening and it was packed as a service was underway. Very atmospheric - please be aware that this is a very sacred place of worship. We had an excellent guide and thoroughly enjoyed the visit - well worth it

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Strange to mix religious rituals with tourism, and I think you should be particularly interested in seeing how Sri Lankans practice their religion and perhaps consider seeing this with a guide to get the most of it. To me it was a bit random and not worth the money to explore the grounds on my own. Lots of people mainly tourists with little respect and understanding of the rituals and the sacredness of the place.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went first thing after breakfast and it wasn't really crowded. There are vendors outside where you can buy flower offerings if you wish. The temple complex itself consists of a few buildings although only a few are open to tourists. The main building housing the tooth relic itself is quite modest in size  and that’s where most of the local devotees will be queuing to get a chance to get closer to the relic. The temple and surroundings are very well maintained and clean and doesn't look old at all. The other building of interest is the New Shrine Room and Museum which has paintings depicting the history of the religion and relic. Our only unpleasant instance was when after making an offering, a monk was pressuring us to contribute more money by indicating that others were offering large denominations. I have been to many Buddhist temples across Asia but have never encountered such behaviour before.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a lovely temple situated on the side of the Kandy lake. The entrance fee is 1000 rupees (£5). To enter you must cover your back, shoulders and knees (ladies & gents) your dress will be inspected by police at the gates. You must then remove your shoes and hand them to the counter. You need to make a donation to get them back, 20 rupees (10p) will suffice. Inside the temple is the tooth relic room which the public are not permitted to see. I believe there is only 10 days a year this is open to the public. The wooden carvings around the relic room are stunning. You are not allowed to pose for pictures with your back to Buddha. This includes the shrine and relic room. I saw people doing this and they were immediately told to stop. Please respect other peoples beliefs. We hired an informative guide who spoke good English. I believe this was around 2000 rupees plus a tip at the end. You must be aware that this is a local temple for some and they come here to make their prayers and offerings. Please respect them. I felt quite bad filing in front of them whilst they were praying. It was this part that I did not like. Overall it is a lovely temple and the most sacred in Sri Lanka. Worth a visit and not expensive like some excursions.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple once while we were in Kandy. We went about 6pm and stayed for an hour. There were lots of people but it is worth going. Required clothes: Men - need pants or sorong that covers your legs. Women - need pants, dress or sorong that covers your legs. Also no dresses with 'slits' in them that come up too high on the leg. Also need to cover your shoulders. There are many parts in the temple and it is somewhat hard to understand the different areas of the temple. I suggest a guide with knowledge of the temple. It just makes the visit more entertaining and you can actually learn about the temple and history.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited here first thing in the morning. It was still busy then. Make sure you wear appropriate clothing to make the most of all the various rooms held here. Parts very ornate and all telling a story. If you fall lucky every 6 years there is a procession parading the replica relic on elephants. If not you can see its casket within a cordoned off room. 3/4 times a day the monks will have a ceremony. Worth a visit.

review_text: This is a place of worship for Buddhists and is therefore strictly not a Tourist'[s Attraction! However, most tour operators will take you there. You are very unlikely to see the Tooth Relic itself but do enjoy the temple and the surroundings. It does cost a few Dollars to get in but this is to be expected because of the throng. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Even a hard nosed agnostic has to be effected by the genuinely deep reverence by all the worshippers at this place. Whether or not one is a Buddhist, this temple oozes holiness and you come out spiritually refreshed. This is a very beautiful place, and if you happen to be there at 9.30am, there is a lot of pageantry and pomp to watch and impressive drumming to listen to.We chose not to join the line to see the tooth container being displayed, but we did make some flower offerings feeling we wanted to be part of the ceremony in a small way. This has to be one of the most significant sacred sites of the world. Don't miss the picture gallery showing the history of the tooth, or the much revered sad stuffed temple elephant in a building to the left of the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A lot is made of the importance of this temple to Bhuddists and for them it is obviously a major attraction. We found the long journey from negombo difficult and the temple a bit disappointing. It cost about £5 each to go in and there isn't much to see. You can't actually see the tooth unless you are there very early in the morning. The statues were quite small and we found the temple at Kenilaya much more interesting and full of artifacts as well as lots of local people.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Being a Kandyan myself, this is the place I love and adore the most. It is known as the highest sacred place for Buddhists. It is a residing palace for the Sacred Tooth Relic of the right jaw of Buddha. Absolutely a wonderfully beautiful and calm place. The best place for you to relax, meditate, and focus on your inner peace. The best hours to visit the Sri dalada Maligawa would be the morning and the evening. And I strongly suggest to all tourists (specially foreigners) to wear appropriate attire (that is in white) to respect the cultural customs, and behave calm and observe silence at all times as it is a religious place.

review_text: We went just before the evening offerings.  Be prepared for large crowds, hot steamy atmosphere and pushing. It's worth it. I wish I'd understood more about the ritual.  Even so, an interesting ceremony.  The faithful being tolerant of the tourist. Well worth a visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I'm not really interested in Buddhism and I think that the history of the tooth is somewhat dubious (look into it before you come), so this somewhat affects my review. Anyway, this place was on the tourist trail so decided to come and have a look. Very crowded at pooja time and you have to queue up for ages waiting for the hatch doors to open in order to file past to look through at the highly decorated pyramid structure in which the tooth is supposed to reside. One glance is all you get unless you battle with the hordes standing somewhat further away where there is one point you can see through (but not very well). Incidently, all the flowers that they sell for people to lay in front of the shrine appear to be stuffed in bin bags straight afterwards for disposal. The rest of the temple is vaguely interesting and as other people have said somewhat atmospheric. I suppose it's something you have to do in Kandy but it's a very subjective experience so don't worry if you miss it if you're not a devotee (there are actually better things to see in my opinion such as the Kandyan dancing and Helga's Folly).

review_text: Very inspirational experience to be here. Take your shoes off before you enter & learn about one of the most important Buddhist temples in the world. It's so beautiful to see Buddhists from several countries (China, Japan, Thailand, Pakistan, India, and more) come together here. There is a procession in the evenings for the tooth relic as well! Not to be missed, we learned a lot.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Sri Lanka life revolves round Buddhism and the Temple of the Tooth is a most revered location but beware that its importance can mean that it can be very busy. Located in central Kandy in a beautiful location next to Kandy Lake do not miss it but time your visit and also be aware that dress codes at the Temple are the strictest we have found anywhere in Asia so don't be caught out when you visit. Women cover bare arms and legs and men also have to make sure that their legs are covered. Do not assume that long shorts will be sufficient.

Very moving to see him in the flesh, sort of.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I visited the temple and the museums in December 2015. Being a follower of Buddhist principles I really enjoyed the visit. But one thing that really disturbed me was during the visit to the World Buddhist Museum. It is an impressive museum, nicely organised and very informative. But when I went to the Tibetan Buddhist site I was surprised and shocked to see that there was not even one photo or information about H.H. Dalai Lama. In my opinion (and I am sure that many will agree), irrespective of the different branches of Buddhism that exist today, HE is the most visible face of Buddhism in the world today. The world knows a lot about Buddhism now through his teachings than anyone else. In fact I didn't recognize any of the Buddhist monks photos that were displayed in the museum. There were so many photos of the ex-President in the museum, but not even one photo of H.H. It just gives me an impression of how Chinese money is playing its power in holiest sites of Srilankan Buddhism. It is a real pity. As ardent followers of Buddhism I expected the authorities to rise above politics in places like this which are the showcases of Srilanka to the world. It is part of their culture and it is hugely disappointing to see politics clouding their culture. I would have given 5 stars for this location. But the experience in museum doesn't deserve any stars.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I visited the temple as part of a Peregrine Sri Lanka tour and it was very helpful to have an experienced tour guide. There are strict guidelines when it comes to entering the temple complex and they are adhered to by temple staff. Sarongs or below knee length pants are required for entry by both females and males. The temple gets very busy as it is an important place of worship for Sri Lankan Buddhists. If you are feeling claustrophobic as I was, you can wander through the temple grounds and appreciate the architecture and atmosphere.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I arrived with my guide, who had a considerable knowledge of the Temple and it's surrounds. Entry to the Temple is controlled by marshals who check that what you are wearing is 'appropriate', so no shorts or dresses above the knee (male and female) and no bare shoulders. The interior is very beautiful but very busy and my only real criticism is that due to the crowds you are 'herded' through the complex a little too quickly. Certainly worth a visit and once again I witnessed first hand the value of having a guide who speaks your language well. Without this type of assistance the whole thing would have been a bit of a brightly coloured blur. With the aid of my guide the place took on a reverent splendor.

Good place to kill some hours in Kandy if you could spare them.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Everyone says it´s a "must do" when in Kandy. I say no. Allthough everything is very clean and made for you to enjoy, I do not think I did a wise choice coming here. This is a very holy place for Sri Lankan Buddhists, who comes here from all around the country to make sacrifices to what they believe is the Buddhas tooth. Even though I enjoy contributing by paying the entry fee, I did not enjoy my stay inside the temple. It was basically like I was trespassing - rudely walking in the tourist line which was constantly moving through the temple, while a even longer line of white-dressed Sri Lankan Buddhists were sitting with their offerings, waiting to give their praises to the holiest of the holy. If you really want to see temples, I would reccomend going to Anuradhapura or Dambulla, where you have temples with similar layout, but without the stepping-on-toes-of-locals part.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: You'll find this amazing Temple in the heart of Kandy right next to the lake. The Temple of the Tooth is quite literally what it says as it houses the relic of the tooth of the Buddha! You enter through the gates and walk up to the entrance of the Temple. There is an admission fee of Rs1000. The World Buddhism Museum is also located behind the Temple of the Tooth but can only be entered by going into the Temple grounds. There is also an admission fee for this Rs500. You may get hassled by locals at the gate asking what country you are from and trying to get you to pay for a tour guide. We simply declined them and this wasn't a problem. You'll also find you have to take your shoes off and there is a small fee to keep them somewhere. (I'd recommend just putting them in your bag if possible). Unfortunately the room where the relic is stored wasn't open (I think we arrived during prayer or just simply at a time when the room is closed to tourists). The inside of the Temple is beautiful though and there is so much to look at. You can exit through the back and into the grounds of the temple where you can either pay to go into the World Buddhism Museum (Which i recommend! there is a lot to see and it may be more interesting than the Temple). Remember though, this is a place where locals come to pray and it can be very crowded and at times I felt a bit rude with my camera out whilst people were praying, but there are also a lot of tourists hanging about!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the Sacred Tooth is the holiest Buddhist site in Kandy-Sri Lanka. The temple is located within the old Palace complex. The belief since ancient times that the protector of the tooth also holds the right to govern the country has made for some colorful history involving kings, wars, and a exciting tale of how the last king of India, Guhasiva, employed his daughter, Hemamala, to secretly transport the tooth to Sri Lanka in her hair. She was accompanied by her husband, Danta, both dressed as pilgrims on a long adventurous voyage filled with miraculous events attributed to the tooth, bringing them safely to Sri Lankan capital Anuradhapura. The tooth eventually made it to its present location in the mid-16th century after being transported between kings and protected by monks

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The very sacred “Temple Of Tooth” is in Kandy- the second largest city of Sri Lanka.  It believes Sri Buddha’s one canine tooth is kept inside the temple and the Buddhist’s considered it as a very sacred one.  This tooth is found from the debris of the burial sight of Sri Buddha.  For many years it was keeping in Purl –one of the south Indian cities.  The Sri Lankan king Meghavarnan stolen this tooth and brought it to Sri Lanka. According the Buddhist, the tooth is a symbol of prosperity.  So that it was keeping always close to the palaces.  Previously it was in Anuradhapura palace and shifted to many places due to the path of various kingdom and finally in Royal Palace Complex Kandy. Temple of Tooth is a very beautiful one.  The interior of the temple is much attractive with its Tamilian style of art and architecture. The pillars inside the main hall are decorated with wooden carving of elephant s head.   Most of the local worshipers were wearing white long cloths and were carrying white lotus flowers. The Buddhist pilgrims used the marble floor inside the main hall is for prayers and meditation.  The sacred tooth is kept in the 2nd floor of the temple and is kept inside a golden box which is ornate with many precious stones and diamonds.  This original box carrying the sacred tooth is the 7th box from the superficial casket.   The terrorists attacked and destroyed the main entrance of the temple 2 times and were fully restored each time. Part of the palace area was destroyed and the remaining structures were protected the archaeological department and now it act as an archaeological museum, also UNESCO considered it as a world heritage center in1998.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Had a wonderful visit to this buddhist temple which was full of history, giving us a flavour of buddhism and sri-lankan culture/history. We visited on boxing day (26th) which our tour guide told us was a popular public holiday, so the queues were incredibly long. There is no charge for the locals, but a Rs 2500 fee for tourists to see the temple; although I do believe some donations are necessary for the upkeep of the temple, it seems that about £12 per person simply for looking like a tourist is a bit of a profit-making scheme, which itself conflicts with the moralities of a buddhist temple in my opinion! Despite this, they thought I was a local somehow so let me through free of charge. It is worthwhile going on the tour as it gives you are more detailed overview of the temple and avoids the queue which can take over an hour. Also, do note that caps are not permitted as it is deemed disrespectful; and both men and women MUST cover their entire legs (i thought it would be okay for men, but this was not the case so spend Rs 400 to borrow a lunghi!)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is one of the main attractions in Kandy.  I was there on the day of a full moon, and it was a national holiday for Sri Lankans.  That meant it was extremely busy. The entrance fee for foreigners is 1000 LKR.  With that, you will be given your ticket and a DVD.  You can't enter with shoes on, but socks are OK.  If you leave your shoes with the attendant, it will cost an extra 100 LK, I think it was.  You could put your shoes or sandals in your bag, which will save you that extra cost. Once through security, I was carried along with the sea of people up the stairs and into the temple.  When I got inside, there was live music, which I assume isn't a usual occurrence.  It certainly added to the atmosphere. There is a lot of space outside, so this was the most relaxing place to be the day I was there.  People light candles and sit and pray. When you've finished and collected your shoes, go out of the entrance beside the temple and take a walk around the lake.  It's worth it if you have the time.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I spent nearly two hours here with my partner and an official guide who explained everything to us. The temple is absolutely wonderful and getting a guide really enhances the experience by explaining in depth and with excellent English the history not only of the temple but of Buddhism and the relic held within the temple. I highly, highly recommend this excursion - not only do you see the temple, but there is an ancient Hindu temple on sight as well, and a stuffed elephant who served in the annual procession for 50 years. The best bit about the temple, for me, was the fact that although there were plenty of tourists, it was not inundated and the temple was busy with people at prayer, instead of hundreds of camera flashes!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went to the temple area early afternoon 0130 pm - the locals confirmed this to be a good visiting time, not so many people there. You will have your bags roughly checked by security when you enter the whole fenced area with temples and museums, the entrance is located at the Northeastern end of the lake. You need to cover shoulders and knees before entering. You can buy flowers and smoking sticks to present to Lord Buddha both before and after the entrance to the temple area, which is neat whether you're Buddhist or not, especially if you bring kids. After a few 100 meters walk you reach the main temple of the tooth to the right. You will pay 1000 Rupees per head, that's just how it is. There are official English-speaking guides at the ticket office, one of them asked if he should guide us, price = 1000 Rupees extra, and you should definitely say yes, fully on your own you won't understand much of it all in the temple. Then take your shoes off and give them to the shoe-keeper and get a number for them. Our guide was really nice and explained everything perfectly, the temple and surroundings. The temple is truly beautiful, and filled with worshipping Buddhists and a few tourists. Stunning how the whole island's history has evolved around this little tooth - you will understand inside the temple area! Outside of the official "3-times-a-day-open-the-curtain-to-have-a-glance-at-the-shrine-with-the-tooth" times, you can still enjoy and understand most of it all. When you're finished, back at the entrance, give the 1000 Rupees to the guide plus maybe a little tip, and then go get your shoes back while you put for example 200 Rupees or so in the designated box, then you're done. Afterwards you can visit the museums in the fenced area, or go back through the main entrance and head on to downtown Kandy for a snack and some good shopping at the city center mall, main street just right to KFC.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic or Dalada Maligawa, as the locals call it, is one of most notable landmarks in Sri Lanka. Built in the 16th century, in the traditional Kandyan style sporting an octagon shaped structure at the front, it stands as one of the most venerated Buddhist shrines in the country. To reach the temple, one has to walk for at least 200~300 metres through the temple garden. There are three daily Poojas or sacred offerings to the Tooth Relic in the morning Noon and Evenings. These poojas are accompanied by traditional drum beatings. This temple may be crowded on Weekends and on local holidays and will be closed after 8 p.m. The paintings on the interior walls of the temple offer glimpses of the temple's glorious past. There is a museum which helps you to gain insights about the history of Sri Lanka and the Temple. During the month of July and August, the usually quiet streets will come out alive when a procession carrying the casket containing the Sacred Tooth Relic parades the streets of Kandy. This is generally the tourist season for this city and it’s best if you make your visit during this season. But you will have to plan your visit well in advance as all the hotels in and around the city gets fully booked in the season.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: while the outside white stone wall doesn't look all that impressive you will be amazed by the interior, You will have to remove your shoes (but can walk around in socks), be sure to have your shoulders and knees well covered or they will not let you in (don't even try). There's a 'storage' place for the shoes - divided by locals and foreigners. It's clear that you're ignored unless you have a tip in your hand if you try to retrieve your shoes when all you're ask for is to leave a donation in a box. These guys ignore that and you can scream all you want. The relic of the tooth is kept in a 2 story inner shrine fronted by 2 large elephant tusks. Another rule - you cannot take photos of yourself or anyone with this as a background. The guards will get after you. The tooth relic is removed once a year during the Esala Perahera, a 10 day torchlight parade of dancers, drummers, dignitaries and ornately decorated elephants. Probably a million plus will come to attend this. it took us 3 1/2 by bus to get here from Colombo and the traffic got more insane the closer we got to Kandy. Keep that in mind. The royal male elephant carries the reliquary ..flanked by 2 perfectly matched, smaller elephants. However, due to the serious conflicts with the Tamil Tigers the tooth relic itself has no longer been brought out during the festival (read up on the Tamil situation and don't pre-judge who is in the right or wrong; nothing is every that simple). The fear is that the Tamil Tigers will either steal and/or destroy it. The temple is joined by the Pattripuwa (Octagon) tower, built 1803, that was originally a prison but does now house a collection palm-leaf manuscripts. The King's palace is also in the temple grounds. You can easily spend an hour (or more) here since it's pretty much one of the top sights on this island.

review_text: You need a good couple of hours to explore this temple before watching the evenings procession as it is set out on a large area. At six thirty pm visitors gather to watch first of all the drummers beat out their tunes before the monks open up the temple and disappear inside. To the visitor this all looks mysterious and you are at a total loss as to know what is going on. To the wise ascend the stairs which looks down onto the inside of the temple where you can see everything. For the pilgrims they gather here and wait patiently for their turn where in single file they process past the opening holding the sacred tooth of the Buddha. The experience especially observing the ceremony is extremely interesting while down below the drummers are still beating out their tune. Explore the rest of the temple before leaving. You cannot wear shoes inside the temple so a pair of socks are useful. Because it is a religious place appropriate dress is required.

review_text: This was the first Buddhist temple that we visited on our three week tour of Sri Lanka and so far (over two weeks on - it has been the best). We visited at approximately 6.30 pm when the temple was beautifully lit and the candle lighting area was quite evocative. Once in the main hall the drummers were fascinating to watch. We then proceeded up the stairs to the area where the sacred tooth - in its golden casket is housed. We were concerned at first that our guide was queue jumping but we soon realised that there are two queues on the stairs: the slow moving one which hugs the left-hand side of the wall will take you close to the casket (but you have to keep moving - there's no lingering); and the faster moving queue takes you to an area which is about four / five metres away from the casket. However, there was a huge surge of people when we were there (literally a crush) as we later found out that they were about to close the viewing of the casket (as it's only open during offerings or prayers). Overall a very enjoyable visit but please note the 1,000 SLR entry fee for European visitors.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Sri Dalada Maligawa or the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic of Buddha is a Buddhist temple in the city of Kandy. It is located in the royal palace complex of the former Kingdom of Kandy. Since ancient times, the relic has played an important role in local politics because it is believed that whoever holds the relic holds the governance of the country. Kandy was the last capital of the Sri Lankan kings and is a World Heritage Site mainly due to the temple. The representatives of Malwatte and Asgriya sects perform rituals thrice a day. Every Wednesday the relic is bathed with herbal preparation which is said to be having healing powers. The temple said to have sustained damage from bombings by LTTE in 1998 but was fully restored each time. The brick wall which runs along the moat and Bogambara Lake is known as water wave’s wall. Holes in this wall are built to light coconut oil lamps. The main entrance gate which lies over the moat is called Mahawahalkada. At the foot of Mahawahalkada steps there is a Sandakada pahana (moonstone) which is carved in Kandyan architectural style. Elephants are carved in stone on the either sides of the entrance. Lot of beautiful paintings depicting the story of a princess smuggling Buddha‘s Tooth relic is depicted on the walls . Then we can see the Royal palace situated at the north side of the temple. The carvings of the wooden pillars which support the wooden roof are an example of wood carving of the Kandyan period and are very artistic and beautiful. The entry fee for visitors from SAARC countries of Rs.500 per head. No photography is allowed inside the sanctum. The actual chamber which the tooth relic is kept is known as the "Handun kunama".The golden canopy built in 1987 over the main shrine and the golden fence which encircles the main shrine are other notable feature. The tooth relic is encased in seven golden caskets which engraved with precious gemstone. The caskets have a shape of a Stupa. The Procession casket which is used during the Kandy Esala Perahera is also displayed in the same chamber. There is a queue to get to the main place where relic is kept and one has to carry lotus and other flowers to offer which is sold at the entrance. Kandy’s ten-day Esala Perahera is the most spectacular of Sri Lanka’s festivals, and one of the most colourful religious pageants in Asia. Its origins date back to the arrival of the Tooth Relic in Sri Lanka in the fourth century AD, during the reign of Kirti Siri Meghawanna, who decreed that the relic be carried in procession through the city once a year. This quickly developed into a major religious event with processions of jewel-encrusted elephants carrying Relic through the streets of Kandy. It takes at least 3/4 hours see the place and is a must visit place to go when one visits Kandy. We had an excellent guide who was able to explain the importance of the temple without which we could not have learned so much about this temple which is a holy shrine for buddhists

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have visited the Temple of the Tooth now many times, and always feel it a special experience. I feel blessed and serene just wandering throughout, sitting quietly in meditation at times, both within and without the temple.  Despite the extreme crowds of local and foreign visitors who stream through during the day, peace can still be found there. Personally, I prefer to visit this Temple very early in the morning, 4.30 or 5am, when usually there are rarely tourists, only the local people attending their sacred place of worship.  Only certain times are the ceremonial drums and musical instruments playing, and this is a must for your visit, whatever the time chosen. review_text: This is one of the outstanding temples in Sri Lanka, it was and is the place of spiritual uplift, the soul and heart of the power of the last Sri Lankan kingdom, and the place where Tamil bombs have caused sorrow and grief 25 years ago. You enter it through a check point that remains you on this bloody episode but behind the gates, a well preserved building for prayers welcomes you as a friend. The paintings, statues and descriptions of the life of Buddha, the journey of his tooth from India to Sri Lanka, his way from a prince to spiritual leader that has given guidance and rules for a peaceful life in respect of all mankind and beings -  you can get an exciting feeling how this believe has become what it is right now.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We arrived at The Temple Of The Tooth early morning, in time for the shrine opening, drums & procession. Packed, slightly chaotic, (to our Western sensibilities), colourful, informative, clearly an important spiritual place - and well worth the entrance fees and donations we gave. A totally memorable and enjoyable place. It really helps to read up on the Temple before going, or be accompanied by a guide - which applies to so many temples, cathedrals, museums, other attractions etc anyway, even those near where you live - there's nothing like an expert to turn a visit into an experience. We read all the information signs, which added much to our time there. Embrace what it is / don't focus on what it isn't, and you should enjoy it too.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were a group of three traveling to Sri Lanka in the first week of November 2015. Kandy was day 3 of our trip. The first to-do on our list in Kandy was The Temple of Tooth, for which we had read several positive reviews. Needless to say, we weren't disappointed. The temple is home to the sacred tooth relic (Buddha's tooth) which was   brought to the island by Princess Hemamali. The entrance fees to the temple is LKR 500, which is the most reasonable when compared to other heritage sites in Sri Lanka. For an additional LKR 500, we hired a local guide who narrated the history of the tooth relic, its significance as well as the customs related to the tooth relic. For anyone who is interested in seeing the golden casket, the ceremony at the temple is a must see.

review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is one of those must see places if you go to Kandy. It is a national treasure and plays an important role in the history and national consciousness of Sri Lanka. Most tourists get there to witness the ceremonies in the temple but one of the problems is that if you don't have someone to explain how it all ties together then the entire visit can be pretty meaningless. Read up before you go or ensure you have very good guide or you may well find yourself stunningly unimpressed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were staying in Kandy as part of a tour of the south west of Sri Lanka, and were advised that we must visit the temple of the tooth. Our guide (who was very knowledgeable) got us to the temple at the perfect time to see them open the doors to the tooth casket itself, which only happens at certain times of the day. Others had queued for a long time, so it is important to time it just right. I am not a Buddhist, but it was very moving to see everyone so overwhelmed by seeing this iconic treasure. NOTE: Ladies must have their shoulders covered, and you will need to book your footwear in (for a small charge) as shoes are not allowed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: On the second trip to Kandy and the Tooth Temple, we finally made it in time for the daily opening ceremony of the shrine itself. This is quite a spectacle and you should be there early to get a good place in the crowd. And crowds there are. The ceremony is twice a day, at around 5 a.m. (I think) and at 6:30 p.m.. There will be many pilgrims and you may not get close to the shrine itself - but the spectacle around the ceremony is definitely worth it. The temple grounds include other buildings, all listed separately here .. Just enjoy a leisurely stroll around the property, which includes a small museum on the upper floors and a beautiful outdoors area which invites for a break by the lake. As this place is so busy whenever you go, it is definitely worth visiting more than once. Plan in 2-4 hours, depending on how much time you wish to spend on leisure (other than the visit of the shrine itself). This is, after all, a place of prayer and meditation.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Not sure if I'm just getting harder to impress but this visit left me a bit flat. The temple is an old palace (I was told) and is fine, nothing spectacular, but I might just be a tough audience! Thought 1000 rupee entrance fee  was a bit steep but that seems to be the standard for things around this town. The 'donation' to get your shoes back is a bit cheeky too. In this place tourists are mixed with worshippers which at times felt a bit inappropriate, especially when taking photos. You can't see the tooth, not for another three years when it is taken out and then hidden again for another five.  So suppose, if you time it right... If you are a believer then guess it's a very important site; if you're me then it was just a drain on my days budget.

review_text: This temple is quite small (only two rooms inside and one corridor). One room is probably with altar (difficult to say without guide, there are no descriptions inside) and in the second room there is a gold Buddha with pictures telling story about Buddha's tooth that was brought to Sri Lanka in the 4th century AD. But this temple was rebuilt from king palace to the temple in the 16th century AD. If I can recommend, rather go to authentic old Dambulla Temple or visit very old and nice Gangaramaya Temple in Colombo.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth(Sri Dalada Maligawa) is a magnificent temple to Buddha with beautiful architecture, shrines of Buddha made of marble, beautiful painted murals depicting history of Buddhism, statues and paintings. Be prepared to go without shoes and wear long pants as well as covering shoulders for the ladies out of respect for the religion. Pictures of people with Buddha shrines are not permitted and should be respected.

review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is situated beside the lake which is worth walking alongside but walking up the main path to the front gives you a fantastic view . The temple is used by locals for prayer so isn't just a tourist attraction and you can purchase an offering to take in if you wish to do so. The architecture and the feeling you get inside is special and downstairs at the back there is another shrine where the story of the tooth is shown in stages on the wall.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of tooth relic is the most sacred temple in Sri Lanka . You have to come with proper dress to enter temple else you will not be given permission to enter. We have visited many a Times for 'Muruthan' pooja. Dahawal danaya / pooja (lunch) is done around 10.30am. You can view the gold casscate very closely at this time. Photographs are not allowed. Wednesday's pooja is special as the danaya(food) is served to dalada hamuduruwo (tooth relic) in gold pots. These gold pots were given to maligawa (temple) by the last king of Sri Lanka, king Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe. New born babies are brought to this Wednesday pooja to get the blessings of dalada hamuduruwo. If you are lucky , you may get chance to go to the inner room next to the chamber where the tooth relic is kept at pooja time. But this is a very rare chance as it is allowed only for people who are having the alms giving turn. There again only 16 people will get selected to enter inner room. In the 1st floor you get Natha devalaya & in ground floor of the maligawa you get dana salawa . This the place where the devotees who under took dahawal danaya (alms giving) offer the danaya (lunch) to maha sanga (monks)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Took my eight month old to Temple of Tooth Relic.Sunday is not a good day as it becomes extremely crowded. To take babies less than one year old for the poojawa the child has to be taken there  around 6.30 in the morning or 9.30.The parent has to be clad in white.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: (Visited during the ceremony starting at 6pm) From all temples we've visited during our stay this was the most touristic of them all. All tourists were gathered together and after paying an entrance fee and waiting in a line (waited for like 15/20 min) you can only see a glimpse of the room holding the relic of the tooth: everyone is guided (pushed) forward and you literally get 2,45 seconds to look into the room were a monk is asking (demanding) for a gift. It's a shame that it became this touristic whilst the building itself is beautifully decorated. You hardly get a chance to have a look around.

review_text: I have to many religious places around India and the world but what I experienced in Sri Lanka is so pure that I was automatically drawn towards the crowds thronging this beautiful temple and milling towards the tooth display. The woodwork and the main sanctum is absolutely stunning. Lots of history here. Also, this is the only temple where you'll find Buddha figurines from all Buddhist countries around the world. Each have it's own style of depicting Buddha in stone and it's really great to see them all together. Posing with the figurines for photographs is prohibited. Some tips: 1. Wear whites. i was the only one here wearing blacks and stood out like a sore thumb. Security guy double checked me :O :O 2. Please make sure to offer flowers. It's a custom here. Good to follow. 3. Desirable to have a guide to show your around as there is so much history everywhere in the temple complex. But be careful when choosing the guide. There are many fakes who'll quickly flash their IDs saying they are the official guides but then their knowledge is  questionable at best. Choose wisely.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Dalada Maligawa houses an impressive collection of artefacts and antiquities of amazing collections apart from the palace itself which pays homage to a tooth relic that belongs to Lord Buddha himself. Unless you get special privilege to catch a glimpse of the relic, we can only witness the 'Karaduwa' in which the relic is placed. You can also find museums that houses a good number of age old stuff ranging from weaponry, garments, coins, jewellery, pictures as well as the Raja Aliya (elephant) that had been treated by a taxidermist for display. The temple is worth a visit if you're in Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Poya is a festival celebrated in Sri Lanka for the full moon. We were amazed to see the number of elephants here at the temple during this time. We were in fact very luck as we didn't buy the ticket to go into Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage as it was very expensive. You will be able to see these elephants here only during festival time. It is a Buddhist festival consisting of dances and richly decorated elephants. Elephants are decorated and paraded at night. We only went during the day but saw the parade on TV at night. There are fire-dances, whip-dances, Kandian dances and various other cultural dances. The elephants are usually adorned with lavish garments. The festival ends with the traditional 'diya-kepeema'. The elephant is paraded around the city bearing the tooth of Buddha. The crowd is huge. Many thousands of people who come from far away places, would actually stay on the roadsides and wait for the parade. We were there about 11 am and it was crowded. Just make sure you take care of your belongings and keep a very close eye on children so they don't wander around. This is a beautiful place to visit. We spent almost 3 hours just walking around and watching the elephants. If you are going into the temple, please take note that footwear is not allowed. You can wear them on the temple grounds but not into the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Beautiful Buddhist Temple. Very clean. Spectacular Sri Lankan architecture. Spiritual spot for the Buddhists as it houses one of the Buddha's teeth. Could not see it though. Believe that it available for public view on special occasions only. Visit only if you appreciate visiting temples and spiritual sites.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited on a Saturday evening (I believe it may have been an especially important Saturday), and the temple was so crowded you hardly had a chance to see anything. Unfortunately, most of what I remember was being pushed by mothers and grandmothers dragging their children to pray. As with any temple, you should expect to have your shoulders covered and wear clothing that covers the knee (especially for women).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The scale of the site is impressive, it has all of the usual elements that make up a buddhist temple but on a grander scale, it is worth picking up a guide, you will inherit one at the entrance wether you like it or not, as there isn't much information in English, luckily we got one who knew his stuff so I gave him 1000 rupee. The tooth relic of the buddha is kept in a sealed container in the central chamber of the temple twice a day the door to the chamber is opened and you can file past and look inside at the vessel, this is for the truly devout as the queue can be long and you only snatch a fleeting glimpse. There are plenty of other feasts for the eyes beautiful carvings and murals in the image house and an impressive bo tree enclosure.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple is quite attractive but you can see most of it through the fence. Unless you are a devotee of the religion give it a miss it is not worth the effort.

review_text: After cremation, Buddha's tooth was  remained in the ashes and brought here. Feeling part of Buddha's physical existence gives a happy shatter to the believer. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Took the wrong decision and visited this during Pooja time (Buddhist prayer time). It was a crush to get in, but once inside the venue was great. The benefit of going at pooja time is that the tooth relic casket is on display, however the masses praying meant it was difficult to see it. It could benefit from some security intervention to get order, especially as there were children and elderly folks in the stampede.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Just north of the lake, the golden-roofed Temple of the Sacred Tooth houses Sri Lanka’s most important Buddhist relic – a tooth of the Buddha.During puja (offerings or prayers), the heavily guarded room housing the tooth is open to devotees and tourists. However, you don’t actually see the tooth. It’s kept in a gold casket shaped like a dagoba (stupa), which contains a series of six dagoba caskets of diminishing size. The entire temple complex covers a large area and as well as the main shrine there are numerous other temples and museums within the complex.

review_text: The temple is a crucial part of Buddhist history in Sri Lanka. Although it is not as dramatic as many other temples I've seen, it should be seen and respected. You really don't need a guide although having one makes the visit more educational IF you have one who really knows what he is talking about.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a must visit while in the area. The temple is interesting and large. We went at one of the times when they open the shrine of the tooth. It is only opened 3 times a day for about an hour. It gets very busy at these times as you can imagine. The locals are able to enter for free and so many come to pray and to leave gifts. You can't actually see the tooth and please don't go thinking you will. At most, you get to see the container in which the tooth is kept. It is a very sacred relic and is treated as such. The prices of admission is fair and some of the comments here about the high price are, frankly, ridiculous. It is about the equivalent of £4. There are very few places of such significance that you can visit in Europe at that price. As well as the main tooth temple you can wander the gardens and visit the Hindu temples in the grounds. There is also a museum and a monument to one of the famous working elephants. We passed a couple of pleasant hours here. Be aware that you must cover up to enter. We had sarongs at the ready. A woman in front had tied a sheet around her shoulders and she was told that a bedsheet is not a respectable thing to wear. They were also not allowing any man in shorts (even below the knee) to enter. If this is something you object to then quite simply, don't go. It is their religion and you must respect it.
