location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Next to Indian Buddhist historical place Bothgaya, the most holy shrine in the Region. Initially built by the Kings in the country and structures were made from Mud/clay. LTTE attempted to blast the temple but was protected by a brave lady policewomen by closing the gate, keeping her life to second. The temple is open for any person immaterial of his/her religion. Only problem is visitors have to dress well to enter. This not to harass visitors but to keep the respectable culture of the nation. If you plan to visit, please dress in such a way that ready to get in to a holy place. Drumming can be seen in the morning hours and evening (around 5.00 pm). The most important is to observe the respect of Buddhists to the temple among the other historical things. I am a Buddhist  & a Scientist Hence respect the religion not in blind. However, the Golden temple (India)  is the most respected place I have ever seen in the world.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Don't know how else to describe it apart from as above, it is just stunning. The ambience is so calming and it is humbling to see how many people are devoted to their religion, coming from England where is it the norm to not regularly practice your religion it makes me ponder if we are missing something back home, anyway that won't help you decide whether or not to visit. If you have a religious interest, historical interest, architectural interest then you will enjoy the visit here. There are several chambers to visit and a two storey museum also. There is a statue of a famous monk of the approach which depicting him tearing down the Union Jack flag which was once erected on the building which was interesting to see. You can buy lotus flowers inside the temple to offer to Buddha if you so wish. You also get a great little Dvd with your ticket as a momentous which is lovely. I would say you can rush it and spend an hour but I would recommend two or three hours to truly appreciate this amazing site.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A massively popular tourist attraction in Kandy and as a result the walk towards it can be a little awkward with street sellers and locals wanting to guide you in (for money surprise surprise). I made the mistake of wearing shorts that didn't quite cover my knees and as a result was denied admission as there is a very strict dress code. Problem overcome by our driver purchasing a sarong for LKR475.  Worth venturing a few streets away to buy this stuff as right next to the temple entrance the shops are rip off merchants and conman. Once inside LKR1000 for tourists, free for locals, the site is big and you get have to enter without shoes and socks so bear this in mind. See a real Buddah praying and the actions of the locals who, in turn, prey to him.   Very busy but fascinating place that gives a great experience into real life Buddhism.   Didn't find it bad inside with regards to locals hassling etc as there are police guarding the site. Would recommend a visit if in Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went on sunday when they have a mass and open the doors to the relic of the tooth. was very nice to see. it was very crowded so if you are uncomfortable with that, make sure you don't go on sunday. they ask you to remove your shoes, and it was so clean so we were so surprised how clean our feet are after the walk. they ask you to wear a scarf and look modest.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Ask someone who knows about Buddhism to explain the various shrines and rituals in this temple. It is huge and highly decorated like the major cathedrals in Europe. And it's used by devotees daily. There are large ceremonies but we went after Perahera. People were bringing flower offerings - queues of them. And the flowers on the various shrine altars were stunningly beautiful. The incense was intoxicating in an uplifting way. The drumming and horn playing added to the kaleidoscope of experiences. It is a holy place for Buddhist Sri Lankans. Be respectful when taking photos as you will want to snap everywhere because there's so much to see.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our visits to the Temple with our wonderful guide, Chandima, were a highlight of our visit to Sri Lanka. Having an opportunity to see the 'behind the scenes' preparation for the Perahera and speak to some of the participants was a joy, and we were overwhelmed by the generosity of the devotees who were visiting their Temple who treated us with such warmth and hospitality. A unique experience not to be forgotten.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: When we wanted to see the inner chamber of the Temple of Tooth where the Golden casket containing the Tooth relic is exhibited to the worshipers at the pooja or Thewawa ritual our host suggested we arrive at the Temple thirty minutes before. once we entered the Temple through the ornated entrance we heard the beating of traditional drums(dawula and tammattan) and musical sounds of the horanawa(oboe like instrument) following the blowing of the Conch shell.The aroma of the flowers and incense and the chants of the worshipers heightened the spiritual experience.We joined the small line to see the inner chamber in time.We were able to do it twice within the time permitted for viewing.To explore the Temple of the tooth,the museum you need a couple of hours.If you would like to meditate in the temple you will need more time and a different routine.small donations will help to maintain this world heritage site

review_text: This was one of the attractions I was most looking forward to and probably the biggest let down of my trip. A very early start in order to avoid crowds and to maximize the amount of ceremonies seen was only half successful. We saw all the ceremonies but the crowds were huge. It is a functioning temple and therefore was busy with worshippers. This was not an issue as I wouldn't begrudge anybody visiting their respective places of worship. I wanted to enjoy this attraction, but there were just too many negatives for me to do so.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Came as part of a tour.  Saw where worshippers leave offerings of flowers to an engraved door (leading to the special tooth which you can only see on rare occasions).  Temple is on different levels with carving and statues.  Outside you can see the bell for worshipping and also a very old open sided meeting place.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is a complex of devotion and history that is still much alive today. It is well frequented by local Buddhists as well as tourists. It was an experience to see the locals visit in reverence, silence and devotion. Outside the complex are flower stalls that sell flowers for the devotees to take to the temple. Lotus flowers, araliya forwers are abundant and a sight to see in itself. Do not miss the street to the left side of the temple complex. You have to take off your shoes to enter the temple. Although the complex is clean there is a fine gravel that is not comfortable for feet unaccustomed to walking barefoot, I would recommend wearing thick socks. The ground was also wet in areas when we visited. When you enter the temple there is a fee to pay and you are given a cd about the temple. The architecture is beautiful.. One tends to focus on the main area and move upstairs but take a moment and move to the left side of the main floor sanctuary. This is where the locals enter from. Here we could see the ritual of washing of the hands and watering the gifts of flowers as well as sprinkling of water from the fountain on the feet before entering to pray. By the entrance door for locals is another door that leads to a garden and the candle corridor. These are often missed by tourists. For me the local culture is important and gives more meaning to what the country visited is about. Enjoy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Same as everywhere , nice but not so interesting. Elephants next door were much more interesting. It was annoying that they wouldn't let foreigners enter some rooms...if foreigners don't have same rights as everyone, they shouldn't ask for such a high priced entrance fee. We were a family group of 4 without children, but I tick friends in the next paragraph, since I don't have the correct choice.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: a must visit for any traveller in kandy. especially for those interested in Buddhism. our local guide veejay eased us through the etiquette of visiting what is as much a working temple as a tourist attraction. the entrance has been lovingly restored after the tragic bombing attack in 1998 although inside is bustling it remains serene and peaceful. we were able to join the locals in paying our respects. by no means compulsory, for a very small consideration beautiful flowers are available on the way in these can be left at one of the shrines inside. Although photography is not discouraged and in fact nobody bothered us at all whilst inside, I would suggest it be carried out respectfully. fantastic atmosphere. allow an hour or two at the most. I would recommend as part of an organised tour like ours as veejay was very knowledgeable and we got so much more out of our visit due to his extensive information on the history and customs and practices.

review_text: This is our first visit to a Buddhist shrine.  Was able to see the rituals performed during our evening visit to the shrine.  Do not miss to see the tooth relic placed on the upper floor which is covered with gold ornaments.  Also visit the museum and taxidermized tusker - Raja.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: One of the sacred sites of Buddhism and a major draw to visit Kandy. Whilst not terribly old compared to the sites in the north is hugely attractive and the history surrounding the place is wonderful. The biggest crowds are always during the short occasions during the day when the Tooth depository door is opened. If you are not too fussed about seeing this, go mid afternoon when the crowds are not too great and you will get to see all the various parts without too much in the way of queuing. Do make sure you see Raja - the temple elephant declared a national treasure when he died in the late 80s and was then lovingly turned into an incredibly lifelike piece of taxidermy

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of Tooth is one of the most holy places in Sri Lanka. Amazing to see that so many Sri Lankans come to offer flowers and worship Boeddha. Families with children ,youngsters all come to pray. It can become very crowded and packed during the especially in the weekend . Best is to go very early in the morning and spent few hours wondering about.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: When in Kandy, the Temple of the Tooth is a must see. Among the devotees you get an nice impression of how the Buddha is worshipped. The complex of tempels and devala's looks amazing as well. The Shrine itself is not so very special, go here mainly because you can see the sacred place and rituals. We added the Buddhist museum to our visit and that was a must see as well. Ir turned out to be very nice to see all the different countries and how Buddism is practiced there. Well worth the 500 rupees per person.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited this temple. A spiritual place with historic events depicted on the wall on the ground floor . Also many Buddha statues from various countries. The tooth relic on the top floor is a display of dazzling gold ornaments and wealth. The arrangements to visit the temple is satisfactory.A must visit place.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Hello, My name is Bogdan and together with my girlfriend, we have visited The Temple of the Tooth in Kandy on September 2015. W have to say that is a Devine place, with lot of history behind. It is the most important Buddhist Temple in Sri Lanka and one of the most important in The World. You will need a guide inside the temple in order to be able to understand why this Temple is so important to Sri Lankan culture. The garden of the temple is very big and beautiful, inside you will find a lot of statues and paintings from the ancient civilization. Definitely a must seen in Kandy! :) Best regards, Deborah & Bogdan Romania - 17.09.2015.

review_text: I suspect every tourist in Kandy goes here. As a non-Buddhist, you need a local to explain all the things you see; not least the number of babies, who are apparently brought here to be blessed. Long queue to see the casket (outermost of 8) which house the tooth of Buddha, and you get pushed past pretty fast, not least by the rather grumpy monk on duty.  The collection of old books and scrolls is probably more interesting, and kess rushed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: What an atmospheric place. Firstly it is a place of divine worship and must be fully respected as such. Temple clothes both for men and women should be worn. Shoes being left at the kiosk outside. Follow the hoards of worshipers into the temple complex and stand back in a quiet corner and observe. The drummers beating their drums, the shrill of the pipes and the clamour of people fill the area with a rich cacophony of sound that enriches ones senses. Observe the tapestries depicting the stories of Buddha and enjoy this wonderful temple full of noise and worship.

Id stick to the cultural triangle for your Buddha fix.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited as part of tour. Our driver advised against a guide. Tourists use a different entrance to locals where feel of 1200Rs pp and security check take place. Men & women are separated and my wife had some interrogation by the guard having to demonstrate what each of her make up products in her bag were used for!  Shoes are also left with an attendant who snatched the tip from us upon return which was rather rude! Inside the temple we were given a cd upon entrance. The inside was beautifully decorated and was easy to navigate between different parts of the temple. The chamber which held the tooth relic was closed so we had a quick walk past feeling rather awkward as lots of locals were sat on the flood praying and offering flowers. The 2 floor museum was interesting and Multi lingual explanation plaques were displayed. Insightful to the Sri Lankan Buddhist history.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited as part of a sightseeing tour and therefore when a guide was introduced to us by our driver we just went with it, however I think this was a bit of a con as he rushed round in about 10-15 minutes, wasn't particularly friendly and then demanded £10 when we finished!! Personally I would have much rather been able to walk around and explore at my own pace. Putting this aside, the Temple is lovely and very interesting. Dress code must be adhered to by both women and men - shoulders and legs covered.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is probably the biggest attraction in Kandy. Its a pretty temple, usually quite crowded as it is a very touristy place. We hired a guide for 1000 LKR. I would highly recommend NOT taking a guide. The whole place is quite self explanatory. The inside domes have the story written clearly and without the guide you would have more time to randomly explore the temple. Its built quite beautifully. I am not big on visiting temples but i would say if you are in Kandy, you might as well visit this place. Its worth one go for sure :)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Make sure you visit the temple during prayer time (morning & evening - guidance from locals). It is difficult to see the tooth due to excessive crowds of foreigners & locals. It is a little expensive, but if you have gone all the way to lanka, should visit this temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Based on the tip from our guide, Khrisan Fernando from Triplanka, we went to the temple of the tooth at 6 pm since the casket containing the tooth relic is only being opened either early morning or at night. This is the strictest temple and to enter, your shoulders and knees need to be covered. You will also need to remove your shoes. Unfortunately it was a rainy night so our feet were wet as we entered the temple. There is a lot of chambers to see aside from the tooth relic. There's a museum, newly built temple containing a history of the tooth relic, multiple temples and of course the chamber where we can see the tooth relic. There were a lot of people but we were able to see everything we needed to see because our guide was very efficient. You could actually also tour around on your own. they have audio guides available. They also give you CD souvenirs. Worth visiting to learn more about their culture.

review_text: The temple is situated near a pristine lake with large fish that are used to being fed by passersby. You cannot step inside with your thighs exposed and they give you a sarong if your shorts are too hot. Inside the road to the temple is lawn lined and contains several statues of srilankan heroes and politicians. The temple itself has a moat and looks very simple on the outside - very elegant in white. Inside the ivory and gold doors hide the divine tooth relic which is opened only two-three hours a day. If you are not a religious visitor, visit the world buddhist museum in the complex which has a rich collection.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I was excited about going here, walking around checking out the culture and history,  but you get hassled by persons wanting to be your guide, even following you.  Then as you walk around,  there is alot of writing and information still not in English which makes it hard to understand - why they charge for the guide. When you go into the artifacts rooms,  it says no photography,  but the guy working there said that I could take some provided I pay him,  seemed dodgy,  and the worst part was when you are leaving,  you have had to hand in your shoes/thongs or whatever as they make you walk around bare feet,  which is ok, but they charge you 100 rupees to get your shoes back, that is disgusting and ridiculous.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This has to be on every must visit when in Sri Lanka.  We had a fascinating evening visit during puja (offerings or prayers) and it is probably the best time to go. Thousands of pilgrims come to see a small door opened every evening for an hour, behind which is Buddha's tooth. However, you don’t actually see the tooth. It’s kept in a bejewelled gold casket which evidently contains a series of six caskets of diminishing size, the last one housing the tooth relic. Because of the huge number of Buddist's attending you are all hurried through at a fast pace.  Lotus flowers can be bought for pence and we put some down as a sign of respect if not belief.  The devotees wear mainly white, the monks are in saffron robes and with the drummers drumming Make this a unique experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I used to visit this place every year. Just north of the lake, the golden-roofed Temple of the Sacred Tooth houses Sri Lanka’s most important Buddhist relic – a tooth of the Buddha. The entire temple complex covers a large area and as well as the main shrine there are numerous other temples and museums within the complex. The following are some of the key sites. Alut Maligawa Audience Hall World Buddhism Museum you can get a support of a Freelance guides & they will offer their services around the entire temple complex for around Rs 500, and free audio guides are available at the ticket office. An elevator facilitates access for travelers with disabilities.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a must see in kandy , and probably why most people visit here.  It's a fair size complex with much finery to admire , as you'd expect paying homage to Buddha and all that goes with it . For many this is a quiet place of reflection and spiritualism , not myself as I'm not bhuddist or religious but it goes without saying show respect , dress conservatively and treat it as sacred for those that do , you are after all only a visitor in another's home as it were .

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Wear something sober/respectful - white is ideal make sure shoulders covered, no shorts etc - it is a temple!!! The very best time to get here is at 6AM - and during a working day - otherwise the crowds are unbelieveable. I got a guide - an elderly guy with excellent English. He charged us Rs 500/- and spent a good hour showing us around The was the location for the Temple of Doom

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple during Perahera and were so pleased that we were spotted by a guide ahead of the 9.30am puja as he ensured that we were in the best places in the temple at the best time. Our visit also coincided with that of the new Prime Minister Ranil Wickremesinghe who was seeking blessings at the temple after his election so especially busy. The guide was an official guide and as well as the temple of the tooth took us to the adjoining Hindu Temple. He was able to answer all our questions and made the visit so much more informative than it would have been otherwise. We later took time to revisit parts at our leisure.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Went with family of 4. we were there the afternoon/early evening of the last day of Esala Perahera. The temple itself is fascinating, it has a moat and then beautiful decorated rooms. It was full of devotees praying and preparing for the big night (but not overcrowded). Next we went into the temple grounds opposite the main entrance, it was full of dancers and rummers preparing, people meandering through and lots of elephants (sometimes passing right beside us). A very serene atmosphere but also charged with anticipation. The grounds are full of small temples (buddhist and hindu) plus interesting museums and stupas. Chanting music floated about and insence wafted. Familes stopped us to take photos with us and our boys, and some passing people pointed us to interesting things or blessed the boys.  It was intensely wonderful.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited on a Saturday morning, around 9.30 and it was extremely crowded. (The weekends are when the locals attend) unlike the other Buddhist temples we visited, your clothes are actually inspected when you arrive and although my shoulders and knees were covered I was refused entry as my clothes were too tight, a sarong quickly solved this problem but I would recommend wearing loose fitting clothes for women. I don't think I have ever experienced crowds like it before, we were pushed around and shoved out the way a lot and my husband said he could feel children putting their hands in his pockets the whole time we queued, luckily our guide had warned us about pick pockets so he had nothing in his pockets for them to take! As with other Buddhist temples you have to take your shoes off, so I would take some wet wipes in your bag as our feet were so dirty by the end. All in all I would say it's worth the visit as it's quite different to all the other Buddhist temples/caves/shrines etc we saw during our time in Sri Lanka but I would try going at 6.30pm and definitely not on a Saturday!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: As we were in Kandy during Esala Perahera, there were a huge number of Sri Lankans visiting the temple complex. It's so large, though, it didn't feel too crowded at any point and it was wonderful to see true devotees and National tourists in as much awe as we were. Beautiful artworks adorn ceilings and walls and floors. The elephant 'dress-ups' for Perahera took up a third of one of the shrines and the audience hall was being put to use as a rest area for performers with sheets up to create rooms and mats on the ground. I loved that! The museum inside the temple grounds is a little dry for my taste but the photographs showing the level of destruction a truck bomb in the late 90s caused helped to provide understanding as to the level of security about town during the Perahera. A visit to Kandy has to include a visit to the Temple of the Tooth. This relic is so important to Sri Lanka that most local people we met on our way had made the journey to Kandy to see the temple and go to the associated festival, Esala Perahera. Don't miss it!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is an absolutely beautiful building both inside and outside. The architecture is amazing. The sculptures, paintings and structure itself is fascinating, as is the story behind its purpose. We went to the temple around 6pm-ish which was great as we saw the sunset, and later as it was dark, all of the candles lit around the grounds. The only problem we had was that it was VERY crowded and i did get separated from my husband and our tour guide at one point which made me very panicky. There were a lot of people around you which made me feel extremely claustrophobic and at points scared (especially when our guide told us to be aware of pickpockets) Also, it is worth noting that upon arrival to the temple you are separated into tourists and locals - different entrances for each. You are them separated again into male and female lines and have to go through security where your bags and yourself get checked (apparently a few years ago there was a bomb). You also need to dress appropriately - shoulders and legs (male and female) covered, and obviously no cleavage on display! You also have to take your shoes off and leave them at the ticket office but the floor is very clean and did not hurt our feet at all. Definitely worth a visit :)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It's a very holy place for Buddhists. The rooms are small and there are lots of worshippers... and that's why it's way too busy. If you want to 'see' the tooth, you have to wait for some time and you can't really see it, only a glimpse (half a second). We were lucky since we were able to watch the parade where you can look at it for minutes. Other places inside the temple are also crowded and people tell you to move along so there is no time to look at anything. Also as a tourist you have to pay an entrance fee of 1.000rs. The only place where we could spend a little time was the library. The small library has some very nice old books and writings. If you have the opportunity watch the parade and skip the temple. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Kandy Esala Perahera (the Esala procession of Kandy) is a fantastic and colourful festival celebrated with amazing costumes and thousands of dancers and drummers every year in Kandy. The festival is held during the full moon of July or August and you need to check every year exactly when it is. The festival's origin is ancient and is held annually to pay homage to the Sacred Tooth Relic of Lord Buddha. A unique symbol of Sri Lanka, the procession is made up of many traditional dances and lasts many many hours. Well worth a visit !!!!! However bear in mind some essential facts. If you can find a hotel room overlooking the parade then you are fine. You can take great photos and go to the toilet or even go to bed if you are tired. If however you have organised seats for the final night to view the tooth relic passing on an elephant consider how long you can hold your bladder and how long you are prepared to sit. It is entirely feasible that you could sit for as long as three hours BEFORE the festival begins and another three hours while it lasts. It is very very very long and noisy and after five hours of sitting watching endless dancing and drumming it begins to wear thin. When the festival is complete you may take 45 minutes to get back to your hotel along clogged streets and you may not see bed till 2 am. I love Beethoven and Mozart and traditional folk music but you would not get me sitting for six hours in one spot straight with limited water and toilets in very hot and humid conditions. Go for it if you love the heat, smells and thousands of people thronging the streets - it is a great experience. But don't expect to be able to move about. The only way to see the parade is from a fixed point and the police do not let you move about that much. See if you can get a high vantage point from a hotel en-route and that is the best option. Seats on the street may be great and may not be. Depends on your agent. It is a great experience - but oh sooo long !!

review_text: We went at about 5:30pm, just as it was starting to get dark. You go through a bag check at the start and then make your way past a few shrines with Hindu gods. There are chickens and a few dogs wandering around, but they pretty much ignore you. The whole area smells strongly of incense which can can make you feel a little woozy! Before you get to the entrance to the main temple, there is a kiosk to hold your shoes which costs about 50 rupees. You then go up some stairs into the temple. We had our guide with us, who picked up a couple of free discs of the tooth parade that was due to happen just after we left the country. He also advised us to wear our backpacks on our front. It was super busy, many people were happy to just push you out of the way. It was a mix of tourists and locals. It was probably busier as there was a service in progress; the drummers were drumming for 2 hours whilst the monks were in the chamber. It's a beautiful building with several rooms to see; the octagon room was cool and the huge room out the back has a series of pictures explaining the history of the tooth relic. When you emerge in the dark, the building, shrines and grounds are lit up and look stunning. Definitely worth a trip, because you just have to!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited with a tour group, but it was an incredible experience. We were told that the tooth (safely inside a golden stuppa) is shown 3 times a day. During our visit there were TONS of people, so plan ahead and get there early. It is imperative to wear "temple dress" which would include long pants (or skirt) that covers the legs as well as minimally, a short sleeve T-shirt. Your bags will be checked at the gate, so pack minimally. Our first stop was the ticket booth, then seeing some frescos showing the procession of the tooth with elephants. (I'm sure the real ceremony is remarkable). We then walked into a room where drummers started playing. This was a signal that the tooth was being taken upstairs for viewing. Again, the crowds slowly moved upstairs. There are two options for viewing the tooth, either get in line for a closer look (seemed that photos were discouraged by the monks standing by the viewing window) or stand by the offering table and get some pics from there. Sidenote- if you want to offer, there are plenty of merchants that sell offerings for about 100 rupees outside the gates. It's a beautiful sentiment whether you believe or not. There are 3 other rooms to see including the previous tooth storage room, which holds a large golden buddha. A second shows ancient ola leaf writings, and the third shows many other buddhas (gifts from around the world) and paintings that show the story of the tooth. It's an incredible site, but I think the energy in the room and the experience itself is pretty amazing too. Enjoy!

review_text: Whilst not everyone's cup of tea, to truly experience Sri Lanka a visit to the Temple of the Tooth is a must. Visiting it, and having the benefit of a guide (a must to really understand it), you can appreciate the devotion Bhuddism installs and it is a place of respect and serenity and an experience not to be missed. It is easily navigated and wasn't crowded when we were there. As others have said make sure you are respectfully dressed - for men 3/4 trousers and women shoulders covered.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was a really interesting experience to watch the locals go about their worship and to see how they all gathered in the inside. The temple itself is quite grand and has several little alcoves and other rooms to explore which are beautifully decorated. The casket itself is ornate and impressive but you get a very brief glance as you are hurried along past it to accommodate for the crowds of people (this was in low season). The vibe here is good and it was lovely to sit outside in the gardens as watch daily Sri Lankan life.  They do obviously try and over charge you for shoe care though and you are rather thoroughly searched. They are also underway admit strict about clothing - no long shorts even for men!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have something for religious places. They bring me inner peace and I just love to stroll in them. What I did not expect was my 3 yr old's reaction to this place. He absolutely loved it. A month after the trip he still talks about the Temple in Kandy. We visited late afternoon, on a week end, and it was very busy, mainly with locals doing offerings. Left our shoes at the entrance, bought flowers for offerings and off we were to visit this special place. And it truly is. The museum located at the back was very interesting as well as it shows Buddhism from all the countries were it is an important religion. It is a must do in Kandy.

review_text: It's apparently the left tooth, but as it's in a casket, which is in a casket in another casket,in a casket which is in a casket and that is in a sixth casket behind closed doors you do not see it.  The building and grounds are very nice and worth the visit. Pilgrims all around paying their respects and not too crowds. On entering you are given a mini CD which you can play to get a bit of a commentary and if you have a local sim card with Sri Lanka telecom you get free WiFi inside with commentary about the buildings etc... There is also a nice picture gallery of 20 paintings telling the history of the tooth,the last couple talk about "The Britishers" who appear not to have left too horrible an impression! Yes there are lots of guide touts and the shoe stall will charge you R25 to store your shoes after R1000 entry fee but its a lovely visit. Re the no shorts they appear to be happy to let you in if the knees are just about covered so it does not need to be long trousers

I recommend sitting outside the relic (in the upper level) and just watch people worshiping.  It's a great way to get a little more sense into Sri Lankan Buddhist culture and practice.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: My husband and I recently visited the temple whilst on tour in Sri Lanka for our honeymoon. Whilst staying in Kandy we felt that visiting this "not to be missed attraction" was a must despite having read a few reviews that said not to bother. We found it grossly overpriced at 1000 rupees per person given that we were in and out in all of about 30minutes - having visited the main temple and the taxidermied elephant. We had expected to find huge queues given what we had heard/read but arrived at about midday during a weekday and it was relatively quiet. Only problem was we were roasting due to having to wear full length sleeves and trousers in order to enter and practically burning the soles of our feet on the hot floor due to the intense midday heat. We were then extremely put out about having to pay extra on our way out to have our shoes returned to us as we were told we weren't allowed to put them in our rucksack and had to hand them in at the main desk! Tourists are definitely being ripped off! Been for the experience and to say we have done it but wouldn't be in any rush to go back on our next visit to Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was the fourth time i visited the Kandy tooth temple, and I must say I am quite sad to see the way it has become such a crowded attraction. Although it is definitely one of the must sees of the country, and i do understand the desire of us, foreigners, to visit, i am troubled by the idea that we are just crowding up a place where others go to find peace and tranquility. It is a beautiful place, but unfortunately crowded and not so magical anymore- so much to learn from but so little chance! Tourists could have limited entrance times, to be able to guve those who go for spiritual reasons the time and space they need. Im not sure how this can be fixed, but i needed to put out there the way my friends and i felt after visiting it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: There is no cost to entering the gardens around the temple which are peaceful compared to the chaos of Kandy. The entrance fee to the Temple of the Tooth is 1000SLRs and then there is the small cost to mind your shoes. We had not hired a guide because there was supposed to be a free wi-fi guide. We couldn't connect to it and there appeared to be no one around to help so we used our guide books and figured things out as much as possible on our own. When we entered the Temple there was a long line up of pilgrims waiting to view the Tooth. We lined up with them for a long time until we decided to skip the viewing and headed through the main chamber of the upper floor. It was very crowded with locals, school children and very few tourists. As we pushed and were pushed through the upper chamber, the wooden doors in front of the gold casket containing the tooth were opened. It was quite a glittering sight! We toured the rest of the Temple going through various anti-rooms and learned about how the tooth came to Kandy. The whole experience was nothing to write home about and yet I'm glad we didn't miss it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple of the tooth houses one of the most significant relics of Buddha - his tooth. The relic is central to the history of Sri Lanka, as kings during all ages have built temples to house the relic in various locations in the country. The temple is a must-visit when you stay in Kandy. You can enjoy the serenity of the setting, the various historical buildings within the temple, as well as the archeological museum which is located in the old royal palace on the grounds. Tips: - Come before one of the three daily times that the doors open of the shrine housing the relic. The ceremony starts with traditional drumbeats and trumpet, after which the doors open. The go up to the upstairs gallery (follow the crowd), stay on the left and you wil pass the upper chamber. You will not see the actual relic, but you will see from some distance its golden enclosure. - This is a sacred place and you will be expected to dress appropriately. Keep legs and shoulders covered, and preferably wear white. No hats or caps are allowed. Shoes need to be left outside, and there is a shoe minder who will look after your shoes. Also, never take your picture while having your back towards Buddha statues. - Explore the other rooms in the temple, such as the octagonal room which houses ancient religious texts, and the hall showing in pictures the story of the tooth relic. - Explore the remainder of the grounds, including the old royal palace. There is an archeological museum in the palace building, but the items in it are poorly explained. - Take water - it may be very hot

review_text: Sri Dalada Maligawa (Temple of the Tooth) is the World's most venerated religious place that many buddhist well wishers around the world wanted to visit. It's important because it's ancient traditional historical value and of course one of few places in the World that hold Lord Buddha's Noble tooth Relic.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We may have picked a wrong time or day but the place was absolutely packed with people --- school excursions, foreign tourists, local tourists, worshipers -- it was impossible to move around on our own so going with the crowd was the only option. The guide did not give any commentary at all which I found quite disappointing. The entry fee for foreigners was quite steep (an entry fee total for a family of four came as real money). Having said that -- the place is really nice as set next to the lake, the inner temple is beautiful. The magic moment came when observing the Christian, Hindu and Buddhist shrines sitting next to each other, with the Bo tree in the middle. I wish we had more time (and space) to feel and experience the place so rich with spiritual influence.

review_text: If you visit Sri Lanka, Kandy is a must, and in Kandy this sacred temple, the Temple of Tooth should be the No 1 place or even the only one to see, don’t miss it. You don't need a guide just enter the place and you will experience the serenity and feel the sacred of the place your own. For foreigners there is a counter next to the ticket counter just outside the entrance area where you should leave your shoes and don’ forget to cover your shoulders and legs. Be prepared the place is always crowded with local worshipers. The temple has a rich history and it is worth to visit the number of larger and smaller rooms inside, plus if you have time the other buildings around the Temple. The sacred tooth of Buddha is kept closed in a chamber on the upper floor and no one is allowed to enter the chamber. Local devotees just pray at the front of the chamber sitting around the closed area of the entrance of the chamber decorated with their beautiful lotus flower offerings.

review_text: I just want to share my experience with a recent visit to Sri Lanka. Our travel agent arrange for 2 different temple visits .. to Dumballa  & Tooth Relic. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Really beautiful and well maintained temple, with lots of locals visiting the place. Expect to pay more than locals to visit the temple, but it is worth it. With the same ticket, go back a second time (the same day), when the doors of the holy chamber are opened (this is upstairs!!) and you are able to see the relic of the tooth. Ask the day before at what times the doors are opened. Amazing to see how strong the locals still believe in the importance of this tooth (while British investigators suggested the tooth probably belonged to a crocodile before).

review_text: Quite a crowded temple adjacent the lake. You can take a walk around the pretty gardens right outside the main temple and click some fantastic photos of the architecture around the temple and also view the monks going about their daily activities.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This serene and sacred temple is a must visit if you are in Kandy. You don't need a guide or a regular tour. Once inside you pass through a tunnel and the original relic is placed upstairs behind a screen so you cannot actually see it. Lots of local devotees and beautiful lotus flowers. It is also worthwhile checking out the museums and buildings around the temple.

The entrance to the temple is stunning, painted with beautiful frescos.  The temple is very beautiful and busy with worshipers, making this a very interesting and lovely place to visit.

review_text: Beautiful architecture and artwork and enriching history.  Just be aware of the touts.  There are no "free guided tours" of this temple.  If approached, always ask in advance for a price or, better still, just tell these "guides", "No thank you!", and keep moving.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is worth a visit if you are in Kandy but don't make a special trip for it. The drum show is ok but not much to look at. You have to wait in a really long queue to be able to see the tooth during one of the prayer times and it's not guaranteed that you will see it either. We were lucky to catch a quick look before they closed the door. You will also need to remove your shoes here so try and take socks with you so you don't have to walk barefoot as the ground can get hot. Also instead of paying them to hold your shoes put them into your bag. This temple is quite strict with appearance so make sure your shoulders are covered and so are your knees.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is one of the most peaceful places that is located in the midst of beautiful nature. We were asked to wear white clothes to this place and be 'fully covered'. It is one of the requirements of this place. This temple is called so because of the presence of Buddha's tooth in this temple. It wasn't open to the public when we went. There are specific occasions on which it will be open to the public for viewing.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was one of the most amazing temples I have visited. I was able to attend the ceremony that started at 7 pm with trumpet players. The temple was very crowded with families and lots of foreigners. Everyone was dressed up in white for the ceremony and almost each person had a flower also. The lights are dim inside which makes the temple so comfortable to be at. It was full of pictures, drawings and statues that explained the story behind the tooth relic. I would love to visit it again for sure.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A visit to the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, which is located in the royal palace complex of the former Kingdom of Kandy, is something all travellers should do on their tour of Sri Lanka.  We were fortunate enough to have a tourist guide accompany us who was a wealth of information and explained in great detail the historical significance of this incredible site.  As we went during Sinhala and Tamil New Year the crowds were incredible but this shouldn't be an issue at other times.  The temple is breathtaking   with stunning architecture, beautiful grounds and also houses ancient manuscripts.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Unless you have a guide or know the religion, there are chances that you do.not know what really happened when you ckme out after the visit. I still have not figured out where the tooth is! Only because I did not understand the place. But a nice experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple complex has more than one building. There is a separate entrance for women and men. The dress code is strict: you must have your shoulders and legs covered. Be ready to walk without your shoes for quite some time. There are a lot of Sri Lankan pilgrims and school groups there, so the main temple is very crowded. The Buddah Tooth Relic is behind the golden door on the second floor and to see the door, we had to move slowly with a crowd. There was very little time to take pictures. Overall, with a pressure from the crowds around, there is no ample time to explore the place and to contemplate.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went to one of the ceremonies, there are three every day. It was a full on experience. Loads of locals there so not just a tourist attraction. We arrived early, as suggested in the guide book, to hear the drumming. It was powerful stuff in a confined space but wonderful. Mixed with the heady scent of incense, the heat, loads of people, sometimes tightly packed together, the spiritual feel of the place, it really was an experience not to be missed. Beautiful to see visitors and locals alike enjoying this stunning temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our visit to the temple of the tooth left me somewhat uninspired - it was a peaceful place to visit - the tea lights glistening in the evening sun looked beautiful - however having been to many a temple it felt much the same. Saying that - I'd still recommended a visit - be sure to combine it with visits to other attractions as this will not fill your day / evening - unless you take part in the prays / offerings / meditation.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is the main temple for religious people, but for me - as for tourist - it is dull place, filled with mad believers whose were waiting nearly for miracle and filled with repeating daily procedures which are boring to watch even for one time. There is nothing good to shoot with camera, lots of people are trying to reach a vessel with tooth of Budha (wich you cannot shoot with camera) and praying all the time everywhere ... there is a small museum of temple favourite elephant and that is all. Ceremony here is "funny" to see - well you will see nothing, because they will do it in room with closed silver doors and with damn lound drums around it ... that is all ... enjoy:-)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were lucky and tagged onto a group with a guide.  It really made a difference to our experience as we wouldn't have known what we were experiencing otherwise.  As it was I still missed an opportunity to go inside the golden casket as I decided to wait for my friend.  I hadn't realised it only opens once an evening for a limited time!  Seen from outside though so all was not lost.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: My family went into the temple but I went for a walk around the outside. My mum in law sat just inside the gate as she couldn't manage the walk inside. I thought it looked better from the outside. You only get a chance to see the tooth on special occasions anyway.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This place houses Buddhist most previous relic-the tooth of Buddha. It is kept in a little golden casket.  This is one of the main attractions in Sri Lanka and local people frequent the temple for religious purposes. Devotees were seen barefoot from the gate to pay respect to the holy place. There is an area to keep shoes for tourists for a small fee. Inside the temple, people offer flowers,meditate and sits for hours. There is another building that shows a lot of sitting Buddhas. A smaller building shows pictures and stories of the elephants who carried the tooth in the annual parade. These elephant were well looked after and kept in site.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Its not only a temple, but a huge area with museums and other small temples inside the premises. Its one of most frequented temples for the local people. You don't get to see the tooth relic but  overall the experience can be good. The crowd is quite a lot, so except a little bit of pushing shoving. Thankfully its manageable. The history is interesting.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A visit to this temple is amazing many levels. The elaborate detail and intricacies of the building are amazing. It is truly beautiful. Just as beautiful is the experience  of witnessing the devotees partaking in the rituals related to their faith and to this incredible relic. The drumming and trumpeting adds to the atmosphere. There are hoards of people making offerings and worshipping there so bet prepared for crowds, particularly if you arrive at the me when they open the doors to the chamber that holds the relic. A visit to Kandy wouldn't be a visit to Kandy without sing this place

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: By chance, I went to the early morning ceremony before the entrance fee booth was opened. In general, I think the Sri Lankan sites are overpriced, and so if I can find a way around paying every now and then, it feels more just. (In India, by contrast, I feel as if most entrance fees are appropriately priced.)  I would agree with some of the other reviewers -- the whole event wasn't very impressive, although I am glad I got up at the crack of dawn to see it. Bring some treats and flowers -- since very one else in line had a gift to give. The nicest thing about going then was that I was the only non-Buddhist visitor I could see in the massive throngs. A special perspective.

review_text: Okay this place has relevance attached to it in religious manner. But this place and srilankans need to learn the human rights. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have actually been to a Buddha tooth temple before, and i thought this one might be a bit of a tourist trap. Was definitely wrong. We went on a Sunday, so there many local people visiting as well, and we were really able to get a sense of the cultural significance of the temple. The temple is very big, and I was glad we had a guide to explain the significance of different parts, and to draw our attention to details we might have otherwise missed. While there were other tourists, this is clearly a place of worship and not overly touristy. Of particular interest to me were the ancient books housed there. We did not see the buddha tooth itself (i believe you need to make an appointment to do so), although we passed behind the queue of people waiting to see, and that was enough for me - it was still a very rewarding experience, part of which was seeing how culturally significant the temple is for many Sri Lankans.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple of the tooth is beautifull but I think there are less expensive alternatives. The 'ceremony' with the drums is not that impressive. Tip: take your shoes off and put them in your backpack just after enterening the gates because at the entrance of the tempel there will be a shoe 'parking lot' and you'll have to pay for it.

review_text: I visited this temple on a full moon day (also known as Poya day), and whilst it is definitely worth a visit if you are in Kandy, it becomes spectacular during Poya day. A very big temple with loads of various areas to explore, and a very spiritual place. Great atmosphere on Poya day as everyone wears white and prays around, and there are loads of different services. Many locals and families visit the temple. You can easily spend hours walking around and enjoying the atmosphere. Make sure you are dressed up decently (no shorts for women), or they will not let you in. There is an area at the entrance where you have to buy your ticket and leave your shoes (in exchange for a small donation). A must see in Kandy.

review_text: This is a most sacred place for Buddhists. The sacred tooth relic of Lord Buddha resides inside this Palace. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We made a day trip/tour to The tooth temple from Ranweli holiday village. Was a very long drive but we'll worth it. The tour guide was a very nice and knowledgeable man, and answered any questions we had. Ladies beware if your shoulders am uncovers then cover them up as I had a shawl on bit it wasn't tied properly and the lady on security literally grabbed me and tied it up but was pretty rough (but had a smile and a nice word too) lol. Good time but would recommend that if you are travelling there from Ranweli or close to there then you would be better off stating the night before in a hotel close to the temple as it is a very very long and exhausting day with all the travelling.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Worthwhile visit for both it's historical and religious reasons. There are many ceremonies held daily such as the puja. Occasionally one gets to see ceremonial elephants in the premises.

review_text: Traveled to the temple of the Tooth relic one evening, during the hours when you could see the box. Worth a visit if in the area.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We arrived at about 6pm. the next 90 mins were probably the longest time I have spent barefoot outside my house! The temple is large and beautiful but the peace you might associate with Buddhism is absent. The ceremony begins with loud drumming outside some impressive doors with various people going in and out. The main action is upstairs where, to be honest, you may well feel that you are intruding. Many people wait to progress past the tooth including tourists. For me it was a little confusing that tere should be almost a catholic reverence for a relic by a faith that I had always regarded as more cerebral. Well worth a visit

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The local guide was very excited for us to see the Temple of the Tooth. We found it very busy and claustrophobic as we waited for the tooth to appear and ended up moving further back as we felt like we were intruding in what to some people is a great honour and pilgrimage. It was interesting but less so for us as we were unfamiliar with their beliefs. You have to take your shoes off before entering the temple and there is a shoe place which you tip the staff at. I took my flip flops in my bag but got the feeling that was not the correct etiquette.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: After arriving I was told I would not be allowed in dressed the way I was (shorts ending just above my knee) and would have to rent a shaul to cover my legs for 200 rupees. This would not have been a problem however when we got in there, there were stray dogs in the gardens urinating on the statues which nobody seemed bothered about and acted as though it was normal. How my knees can be disrespectful but urinating on statues is ok I am not quite sure. They had an elephant in the garden for tourists to come and take photos with but it's back legs were chained together so tightly that it could not walk anywhere and looked like it was uncomfortable just standing (holding it's leg in the air at a funny position). We were there for one of the ceremonies and whilst it was busy, it was not so busy that you could not move aound

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a must visit place if you are coming to Kandy. The atmosphere is very calm and serene. Few advises - Make sure you were cloths longer than knee length as they wont let you in without this and you will end up buying them from vendors outside for a price; White cloths are preferred. Also, stay away from touts!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were mesmerized by this temple inside the royal palace complex; the exquisite temple sculptures, the rich history, and the immense devotion of people. This temple complex was bombed by LTTE during the civil war. Sadly, we didn't spend enough time here. We couldn't visit the Museum of World Buddhism. While we were at the temple complex, we saw all the temples. Admired the architecture, the variety of statues of Buddha, and the colorful waterlilies and lotus flowers offered to the deity. The main shrine has a canopy of golden decorations. The Temple of the Tooth Museum is also a must visit. The Kandy lake adds glamour to the entire complex! Tips: Wear appropriate clothes; ask your guide for details. Help preserve the temple monuments; don't write on them or dirty them. Keep half a day to see the temple. Beware of vendors who quote a hefty price for the worship items; if you have a guide, you can request the guide to purchase the items on your behalf. If you are driving, you may have difficult finding a parking spot especially on weekends and holidays.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Expose yourself and your children to the unique experience of seeing thousands come to worship at this magnificent Buddhist temple.  Don't pick up one of the guest lecturers unless you agree on a fair price before hand.  Do cover your shoulders (women) and wear long pants (men).  Do immerse yourself in the fervour and the spirituality of the temple.  We did 16 years ago on our honeymoon and again yesterday and I'm of the belief if you open your eyes and your heart there comes respect and mutual understanding.  What I loved most to hear from our local driver  was 'we invite  Moslems to our Buddhist festivals and they invite us to theirs'  - religious tolerance at its best!  The rest of the world should take note.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you're coming to Kandy you have to see the Temple of the Tooth. Go when there's a ceremony so you  see all the drumming and people going in to give offerings.  Ceremonies are 3 times a day, we went to the 6.30pm one. Once the doors to the casket room is open all the tourists scramble for a picture, hang around a few minutes and the scrum will clear and you can get a good view of the casket, which is very beautiful. If you wish to go inside you can, but we choose not to as we are not Buddhist. The Temple as a whole is very nice.  Once leaving the Temple and collecting your shoes don't walk by the 2 Davales nearby, they are much more peaceful. Also go to the holy tree, this is where they take water and walk around the tree 7 times and make wishes. This actually felt much more spiritual to me than the Temple of the Tooth. The whole complex is very nice and is a must see. We didn't get a guide but other people do. If you get a guide they won't take you to the Devales so make sure you don't miss them.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited the temple as it was rated as the best thing to do in Kandy. However I would advise get a guide, we didn't on a limited budget and we had no idea what was going on. Also remember boys must cover up their shoulders and legs as well as the women. They charge you a high amount to enter and museums etc you must pay again except the museum  on the elephants, which isn't translated so you can only view the pictures if you don't know the lingo. Overall it is a very beautiful building with nice grounds. The guards are very aggressive towards tourists but I felt that a religious temple shouldn't be too accommodating to tourists! After reading a few other reviews it potentially was because it was off season and there weren't many tourists there!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was a beautiful place, very ornate with lots of carvings.  We bought flowers to offer at the alters, and photos are allowed inside.  It's quite noisy for a temple and busy with lots of locals and queuing tourists.  Like all temples in Sri Lanka, shoulders and legs need to be covered so my husband and I bought Sarongs in Kandy market for £3 each to wear on top of our shorts.  You do get searched as you enter the grounds.  Shoes are left at a kiosk but you can wear socks.  A tip....before entering the actual temple, it is a tradition to wash hands and face at a water fountain to the left of the main temple door, just around the corner.  Only local guides will know this.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Kandy the capital of the Kings and the resting place of the sacred tooth of the Budda, It’s interesting to visit and see for yourself the extreme end of Buddhism, the walk around the lake will take time to enjoy or you can take a Tuk. The place you must see is the Elephant Orphanage on the way to Kandy It’s sad in a way to see these wonderful creations in such large numbers outside their natural habitat used for monitory gain, not many places in the world will you be able to see this, and at mid day they go for a swim in the river and you can sit in a restaurant and watch them It’s addictive and you will need to keep an eye on your watch. The new zoo is right next door and a must see  you need to be ready to open your wallets as all overseas visitors pay a significant entrance fee unless you have a Sri Lankan ID.  The trip can be taxing mainly due to the crazy drivers and traffic, roads have improved significantly during the past 10 years, even with all corruption associated with it, still it’s a long trip up down to Kandy in one day and I would not recommend it. The long trip over 5 days is too expensive unless you have the cash and can endure the long trip remember 20km can be equal to 60 during the day in Colombo , you can now use some of the freeways to get around like the 100km freeway to Galle. The airport is such a pleasant place to arrive at after a long trip its modern and they do not hassle you but offer you a warm welcome ,in this context I rate Perth as the worst airport in the world and if you have the wrong skin colour then you could have a long wait to get out it's as close as you can get to a Police state.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Dalada Maligawa has a historical  and architectural significance that's vital in any Sri Lankan context and is a must see to any visitor. The gold roof and the intricate carvings and drawings make this a religious place of worship second to none in Sri Lanka. We prefer to go here a bit late in the night. It becomes empty rather quickly to give you the time to explore the temple. The antiquities are amazing and you feel an aura that is unimaginable. If you do get to see the chambers where the tooth of the lord Buddha is kept it will be something to cherish. But be prepared to be rushed as the crowds are large.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple of the tooth around 6.30 pm. It was crowded and we had to wait in the queue for a long time. The evening prayers were going on. The temple looked lovely, bathed in lights and in the sound of drums resonating from the shrine below. After the long wait, we hardly had few seconds before the main shrine where the tooth of Buddha is enshrined in a gold casket. The entry fee is also steep for foreigners - LKR 700 per person.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Puja timings: 5.30-6.45am, 9.30-11am & 6.30-8pm. It doesn't make sense to come outside these times, because you'd be missing out on the action. Only during the puja, the chamber where the Tooth Relic would be opened, and also another small room where a Buddha statue is. (Halfway between the first and second floor of the main building). I would say, please reach within the first 15 minutes of the Puja, to allow the freelance guides to explain to you about the ceremonies and the history, and also allow you to get a good spot (in front of the chamber) to snap valuable pictures before the devotees start to offer the items and blocking the line of sight. You'd likely spend an hour, including witnessing the puja and taking some shots. Thenafter, you can spend some time at the museums around. Come in the morning, because that's probably when you don't see many tourists yet! :)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Obviously one of the top attractions and "must-see" sites in Sri Lanka, which houses the most important Buddhist relic--a tooth supposedly from Buddha.. My spouse and I visited this historic site on February 07, 2015 during a private two-week, 3-person tour of Sri Lanka. I am not certain if this was an auspicious, sacred day to visit, or if we just ran into bad luck. Unfortunately, from the time we entered, we encountered a chaotic and dangerous crush of religious zealots. There were few Westerners at the time we visited--but then we never saw many Westerners during our two-week tour in the country. That said, we became involved in shoving and violent pushing as people queued to get in line. No, they really never queued. I actually feared for my life as I tried to maintain my balance on the stairs. I was literally trampled and knocked aside so that I lost my balance on numerous occasions. And this was during the morning hours when fewer tourists were expected. It was disappointing to discover that we would never actually "see" this relic after all the trauma since it is kept in a golden casket, which is far removed from where one stands in the viewing line.To this day I am not certain if I saw anything other than the heads, shoulders, bodies and feet of rude people who surrounded me. I do know that MY foot suffered a severe crushing, and that one man rudely shoved me forcefully out of his way. I wish that we could have viewed more of the actual temple and architecture, but there were simply too many people to allow this. I have no idea, nor can I relate to  what travelers mean when they refer to a serene feeling of reverence. The people who surrounded the three of us from the time we entered, until we gratefully found our way out, created a terrible experience that I never care to repeat. And all of this was in the name of religion? Sorry, I don't get it.There was clearly no respect for religion--or for fellow humanity on the day we visited.

The tooth case is only visible at particular times of the day, when it can get really busy. Also, don't forget the elephant...

Pro: it was an attractive temple with a lot of sacred and historic artifacts. Also nice location beside the lake in Kandy. Cons: extremely busy. Also, having seen quite a few temples through China and Sri Lanka, we were quite underwhelmed by this one. Overall: if you are 50/50 on whether to go or not, don't go. If you decide to go, take a guide. Despite research, we were quite disappointed with our visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We really enjoyed this visit! The temple is beautiful and the whole area has places to visit! The museums are very impressive with lot of information and nice things to see! The offerings and praying are actively happening as the Buddhists come here every day and keep the tradition alive! The tooth relic is kept closed and you cant see it normally, but We were lucky to find out they do a ceremony at the evening where they open the area where the relic is, you can join the queue to have a quick look on it, Buddhists are allowed to go in for a bit longer. We felt blessed and luck to be there and felt inspired by their faith!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is the holiest place for Budhists in Sri Lanka. If you are at Kandy this is a must visit. To avoid the crowd, we visited the temple around 4pm. It typically gets crowded after 6pm .The sanctum Sanctorum where the casket containing the tooth is kept was not open at that time, but since the crowd was less we were able to spent some peaceful time in the temple. You can pick up lotus flowers at around LKR100 to offer at the temple. There is a museum inside the temple that shows the history of how the tooth reached Sri Lanka and was kept at different places over the 2500 years. There is an entry fee of LKR1000 for foreigners ( LKR 500 for SAARC country visitors). This is a sacred place and please dress appropriately and maintain silence.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Sri Dalada Maligawa (Sinhalese: ශ්‍රී දළදා මාළිගාව Tamil: ஸ்ரீ தலதா மாளிகை) or the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is a Buddhist temple in the city of Kandy, Sri Lanka. It is located in the royal palace complex of the former Kingdom of Kandy, which houses the relic of the tooth of Buddha. Since ancient times, the relic has played an important role in local politics because it is believed that whoever holds the relic holds the governance of the country. Kandy was the last capital of the Sri Lankan kings and is a UNESCO world heritage site mainly due to the temple. Monks of the two chapters of Malwatte and Asgiriya conduct daily worship in the inner chamber of the temple. Rituals are performed three times daily: at dawn, at noon and in the evenings. On Wednesdays there is a symbolic bathing of the relic with an herbal preparation made from scented water and fragrant flowers, called Nanumura Mangallaya. This holy water is believed to contain healing powers and is distributed among those present. The temple sustained damage from bombing by LTTE terrorists in 1998 but was fully restored each time.

review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is a really incredible temple.  It is filled with beautiful aspects and architecture.  Within the temple grounds there is another museum that has rooms featuring Buddhism from around the world. The countries' rooms that are represented are decorated by someone/Buddhist representatives and have a lot of great information and really show the similarities and differences of Buddhism around the world. I would suggest going and planning to exit around sunset because the sounds of the birds mixed with the view of the lake is just gorgeous.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: More than an attraction, I would consider the place as one of the holiest shrines to Buddhists. The temple houses the tooth relic of Lord Buddha which is venerated daily by large crowds. From a distance you could see the golden canopy providing shade to the relic chamber. The architecture of the temple with its typical perimeter wall, the octagon and the moat is impressive. You could hear the beating of devotional drums when you enter through the stairway. Devotees offer flowers upstairs and light lamps and incense sticks in an open air shelter downstairs. The sacred tooth relic has been venerated by many generations including the Kings who ruled the country who considered it as a symbol of power. This is a not to be missed place if you are visiting Kandy. However the place could be teaming with crowds most of the time. Also, do not forget to visit the adjoining King's Audience Hall and the ancient Palace buildings along with the taxidermied Royal Tusker.

But please make sure you have the right attire as this is a religious place of worship

review_text: This temple is actually a complex of several buildings, including the Buddhist museum. If you go a 6.30 pm you can catch a rather noisy ceremony although you wont actually see the tooth. The buildings and grounds are beautifully maintained and a lovely place to watch the sun go down.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went at 6pm knowing they have a 6.30pm ritual. It involves lots of loud drumming, and open of the golden doors. Interesting, but not breath taking. Was nice to have a look around and see a different culture. Its got a lot of history. Foreigners pay 10,000SLR entrance fee. Don't feel obliged to give offerings of flowers.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The main attraction in Kandy without a doubt is this temple. We were staying within walking distance and made our way down early in the morning only to be told we could not enter because my husband was wearing shorts! So we decided to stroll around Kandy and return later once he had changed into pants. In the evening the crowds had subsided a bit and we entered quickly. The temple was beautiful with stunning interiors and overall peaceful and serene atmosphere. People were sitting emotionally in prayer and it definitely brought a sense of calm. Worth a visit for those interested in experiencing something new or just religion in general.

review_text: this was an interesting experience, I would recommend seeing it even if there probably are other more interesting temple to visit. review_text: The fact is that it is a beautiful temple. Perfect time to visit would either be around 1 pm or 6/6:30pm if you would like to see the relic. Now if you don't really care too much for that then go during the other hours and it is extremely peaceful. Ideally, catch the Kandian folk dance performance at the cultural association next to the temple at 5pm and then head to the temple. Tip 1 - Cover yourself with a jacket if you are in a sleeveless top, no  shorts. The foreigner prices are around 2500 Rs ( appx, I think) Prices for SAARC countries - 1200 Rs. Tip 2 - You may want to carry a carry bag for your footware if you don't want to leave it in the footware stall cause you'll be hounded for a donation for leaving it there. Tip 3 - You'll find greedy guides who'll hound you. Just deal with it. Overall a gorgeous temple like all Buddhist temples.

We imagined this is what the ruins would have looked like 2000 years ago. Well worth seeing if you are in town.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is THE attraction in Kandy.  Buddha's tooth is an extremely important relic to Buddhists everywhere.  The relic resides in a closed part of the temple and is brought out in a procession (on an elephant) once a year. As you approach the entrance to the temple, you will be accosted by a guide who will try to converse with you with the typical questions:  "where are you from ... how long have you been in Sri Lanka ... is this your first trip?"  Obviously, he wants to be your guide for hire.  In this case, I would recommend a guide, since the details of the temple are very interesting and there are few if any signs or interpretive materials.  I would suggest, though, that you establish a price for the guide upfront.  I didn't ... and when we reached the end of the tour I asked him what I should pay him.  He responded that he was a Buddhist and did this for the sake of religion.  So, I gave him 500 rupees ... to which he responded:  "I'm sorry sir, but 500 rupees is very cheap."  So much for religion. Admission to the temple is 1,000 rupees ... and they do NOT take credit cards, so have cash on hand.  It is another 100 rupees to store your shoes.  You will be walking around a lot (including some stretches over gravel) so wear some socks that can take a beating. Be prepared for crowds.  This isn't just a museum, it is an active temple and there will be many school groups and others crowding into the temple ... actually making it hard to maneuver. Be aware that if you are visiting the museum attached to the temple (also very interesting) it is not at all accessible for the mobility impaired.  Stairs (steep stairs) only. One part of the museum is dedicated to photos from the truck bombing that damaged the temple in the 1980s and killed 35 people. Since there are virtually no interpretive materials in English, be sure to read a guidebook about the temple if you are going to tour it on your own. It is definitely a beautiful and fascinating attraction if you are prepared for it.
