location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I thought this would be one of the highlights of our tour but it ended up being one of my least enjoyable experiences.  Don't get me wrong - the sacred tooth ceremony and the shrine it's enclosed in, are quite interesting, but the experience itself isn't what I'd call fun. A lot of people make their way along to the temple from the hall that plays host to the 'culture show' - this is what we did and arrived about 30 mins before the ceremony started.  That gave us time to look around the lower level.   The shrine that houses the relic is quite impressive - it's quite an ornate building-within-a-building and forms the centre of the main temple area. At the appointed time, the monks arrived to open the door into the shrine - we watched that for 5mins before turning around to see that people had formed a long queue upstairs.  Our guide advised us to join this, so we did - it ended up being a shuffle around to spend a few seconds looking through a small window towards a casket that holds the relic.  I suppose it might be a spiritual thing if you're that way inclined, but if you aren't, it's basically a long queue to catch a glimpse of a box. After that, you can then shuffle around with the crowds to see other areas showing various buddhist artifacts, with loud ringing and other noises sounding throughout the whole time.  After a while, the crowds and constant noise got a bit uncomfortable so I just wanted to leave.  The guide wanted to show us around some other places within the temple area but we pretty much just zipped past those on the way out. I think if I were to go again, I'd visit the temple during a quieter time and skip the relic ceremony.  It's probably a more relaxed and interesting place to be when it's not wall-to-wall people. + The shrine building is cool + Nice atmosphere (before the events occur). - Busy as hell around event times - The bells etc start to get quite annoying.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Set in centre of Kandy this amazing Temple, that is said to house the tooth of the Buddha brought from India.  Knees must be covered, so long shorts or jeans or sarong.  No Smoking and you go bare foot once at the Temple gates (not the outer ones.  Cost to Tourist approx. 5GBP.  Twice a day there is an exposition of the Monstrance housing the Tooth.  Once in the morning and once at 6.30 pm.  Get there about 5.30 pm but it is very very, very, busy and crowded.  If you are claustrophobic this is a bad place for you; as soon as the Monstrance is exposed crowds push from both side.  I was lucky as I am tall and was in direct line to the doors opening.  Beware of pickpockets.  there are also other temples within this temple.  All very noisy but a total must to see and do.  Don't get told off and slapped like I did, by smelling the flowers, as the bouquet here is only for Buddha.  Same thing applies in the flower market.  Some of the Monks will allow you to make a flower offering, but you must use both hands and be given the flowers, DO NOT pick them up yourself.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple complex is big and full of devoted local people. As we visited on Sri Lankan new year's day, there is no way we could get close to the place where supposedly was the tooth relic. The other hall was nicer with the golden buddha  statue and a number of paintings telling the story of the tooth. It was interesting to watch how people outside were burning sticks embedded into big pots.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were lucky enough to visit on New Years Day (April 2014) and the temple was really busy creating a lovely atmosphere. We left our shoes with the attendant but it would be very wise to take socks to wear as the concrete ground was SO hot!! Families visited together, encouraging their children to place flowers at the offering table and I felt completely relaxed about taking photos of what was going on. Unfortunately, we saw no tooth.  Naively, I thought it might be available to see on this special day. Outside was the candle offering room where the Buddhists light a wick in coconut oil in a dish. Again, some lovely photographic opportunities and the smell - heavenly. A must visit in Kandy

review_text: I found the temple and its grounds very peaceful despite the large (but patient) crowd near the main shrine around 10 am.   This place allows one to reflect quietly. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is, of course, a must visit when in Kandy, but, as with all places of high worship I have mixed feelings. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are travelling through Sri Lanka, it is one of the must-go places. We were fortunate enough to visit the temple on a day when the doors were opened so that you could see the incredibly bright golden casket in which the tooth is located. It was an overwhelming experience walking in procession with Sri Lankans who had brought their new-born children and poorly relatives to the temple passing the golden casket. Be sure to wear respectful and appropriate clothing to this temple too. Hannah was frisked for cigarettes by the female security guard at the checkpoint, despite the fact she doesn't even smoke - for those of you that do, don't be surprised if they confiscate them. We recommend arriving in the morning to avoid the worst of the heat.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We have lived in Kandy and we have to say this is a must visit for any visitor to the city. It's best to avoid full moon days as a large crowd of devotees will be in the temple premises and you may not be able to leisurely  admire the frescoes, sculptures and architecture of the temple. Remember not to wear shorts or sleeveless tops as this is not allowed inside the temple, also there is a safe place to keep shoes till your visit is over. You can't wear head attire as well inside the temple. Don't forget to visit the adjoining memorial for the Raja tusker as it tells a compelling and emotional story.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Located along the lake in Kandy, this is one of the most sacred of Sri Lanka's religious sites. Its teeming with devotees who bring in lotus flowers as offerings. Very atmospheric- there are areas where incence smoke and smells wrap you, others where you are jostling with devotees and tourists and yet others that are so peaceful and quiet, that you can sit and contemplate the universe- if that is your thing. Not to miss!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I would give this a miss unless it's your absolute first time to ever see and witness Buddhist culture and traditions. Perhaps my timing was also a bit wrong as I arrived during the Buddhist new year holiday so A LOT of the locals travelled far and wide to honour the Buddha and perform their own form of worship during these special days. I timed my visit during the evening ceremony which starts at 6:30. I then trooped along with everyone else to the main shrine building which is on the second floor. I got there at 6pm to ensure I had a good spot which turned out to be pointless as the relic room is so small and many people had already parked themselves on the floor, some praying, some waiting. At first I stood right in front of the table with flowers but out of consideration for those who were actually praying, I moved to the back since I was just there to observe and atake photos. Thw crowd got thicker as the ceremony time grew closer and as the music from the trumpets started. Pilgrims garbed in all white started filing into the fenced off area right in front of the altar. Meanwhile the rest of us were packed like sardines and some pushing and shoving even ensued when the altar windrow was opened to reveal the golden casket where the tooth relic is supposed to be held. Anyone who wanted a' closer' look would have to queue from the first floor and even then you would only have less than 5 seconds to gawk at the casket before you were ushered along by the monk himself in saffron robes that was supposedly accepting the offerings from the devout worshippers. No close up photography was allowed for those in the queue. The casket itself was placed at least 5 metres away from the viewing window. Still I suppose it was still an impressive sight given how it gleamed in pure goldness made even more stunning by artfully placed lighting overhead. After that you could head down and roam through a few of the smaller halls with more Buddha artifacts where you were again ushered along quickly without really being given time to look and study the pieces. Final gripe was the shoe depository where those tending it 'demanded' I give money (uh, I thought a donation should be voluntary?). The atmosphere of the whole place was just far too touristy that it's tough to imagine it as a place to cultivate the equanimous and gentle disposition espoused by the Buddha.

review_text: The Temple of the Tooth was one of the must sees for me in Sri Lanka, one of the most revered Buddhist temples in the world. Very thought provoking. A tooth of Buddha is kept in a gold casket inside. Each day the monks check the horoscope and decide when is the most auspicious time that day for people to view the casket and is only open for viewing for 15 mins a day and no one knows when that will be until it opens. Well worth a visit even if it is a little crowded.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have been here many times, as a couple, as a family. The most scared place for Buddhist in all over the world. You are not allowed to wear shorts, short sleeved dresses, see through dresses when entering the temple. Best times of the day to go there is at "Thewawa" time. One starts at early in the morning, around 5.00-5.30, second one is around 10.00-11.00 and the last one is around 17.00-18.00. You can keep your belongings at the entrance, in parcel counter. If you are not allowed to walk there will be a mini taxi service. Don't forget to go the museum alongside the temple, There are a lot of information related to Sri Dhaladha maligawa as well as Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: When visiting Sri Lanka it's important to get a feel for the people and the island.  Visiting important religious monuments helps with this. Shoes off and no hats should be worn.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Let me first preface my review by saying that I love visiting temples, learning about culture and history, and exploring new sights. However, I must say, that this was the most lackluster experience so far in Sri Lanka (We went to almost every temple in the triangle and enjoyed it) Yes, it is historically important and yes, many people frequent the place, but unless you're a die hard religious fanatic, then I don't see the reason to visit people donating flowers and money. The cost is 1,000 and I think just entering the grounds would be sufficient. But perhaps the most disturbing part of the visit was the insane elephants swaying back and forth chained up in the courtyard. Usually when you see an elephant rocking its head back and forth, it means they've either gone mad or are distressed. Either way, it was very upsetting and it sadly exists in this part of the world (as I have seen in Thailand as well). Whether it was Kandy or seeing the elephant that put me off, I would not recommend a visit to the Temple of the Tooth (nor would I recommend Kandy).

review_text: A very spiritual  place and the guides are very knowledgeable, however my guide's insistence that I give him 2,000 LKR after I offered 1000LKR was very disconcerting. If you get the opportunity, attend one of the three ceremonial times for a realisation of just how revered the relic of the tooth is. Another troubling aspect is the treatment of the ceremonial elephant. It is out of the way behind the Christian Church but within the confines of the temple area. It is chained with no room to move, no water when I was there and rocking back and forth seemingly distressed and chewing on pieces of dry wood. Aren't Buddhists supposed to revere nature and animals?

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went to the temple in the evening because the intense heat discouraged our visit in the mid-morning- we actually turned back. I only wish we had known that we could get a free audio guide at the ticket office- there are no signs for it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple harbours a relic of the Buddha, his tooth. Perhaps he had an implant? Anyway, the temple is very important for Sri Lankan Buddhists, and twice a day there is the possibility to come close to the tooth itself. Long queues of people will slowly walk past it, flowers or incense in hand. It reminds a bit of the Mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh. The Buddha would surely object to the beatification of his tooth, as he was not in favour of worshipping objects of any kind... It was interesting, although very busy and a bit tiring.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

review_text: If you haven't seen other temples then it's well worth the visit, it's also worth visiting if you are in the area and haven't got anywhere better to see but please be aware that as with most tourist attractions in Sri Lanka the state charge foreigners exceedingly more to visit attractions than the locals. A few parts of the temple and its associated buildings are quite interesting, especially if you haven't been to a temple before. As it is close to other attractions and close to the main market it's worth rolling several sites into one overall excursion, especially if you have to endure the abysmal driving standard in the country to get there. If female, then remember to take or wear clothing to cover your shoulders and legs, otherwise you won't gain admission. Whoever you are, you will also need to enter the main temple bare footed and then pay a tip of at least 100 rupees afterwards. There's nothing to buy within the temple but if you need food or drink then there are numerous small shops as well as a small shopping arcade within a few minutes walk.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were staying at the Club Bentota Hotel in Aluthgama and visited The Sacred Temple of the Tooth Relic as part of a two day trip to Kandy. We arrived at nightfall and our first impression was how beautiful it looked lit up with the river in the background, lovely. We went through security and those who's knees were not covered were given a sarong to cover up with. It is custom when visiting Buddhist temples that both your shoulders and knees should be covered. You also hand in your shoes until you leave. There were hundreds of people bearing flowers for Buddha and heading inside the temple to pray and hoping to catch a glimpse of the golden outer casket they believe to hold Buddha's tooth. We were lucky enough to get a glimpse ourselves and considered it an honour to be allowed to share in this experience as it is only possible to get to see this relic for 15 minutes a few times a day before it is locked away again. Also many religions do not allow 'outsiders' to see inside their places of worship so we considered it a privilege. The temple is extremely beautiful with its intricate paintings and we found the history fascinating. It's wonderful that it means so much the people who visit every day and not being particularly religious ourselves found their dedication to their belief a very humbling experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were staying on the SW coast of Sri Lanka for seven days and then planned to have 2 nights in Colombo before flying home. Decided to visit Kandy on the journey to Colombo. Had completely underestimated the time it takes to travel relatively short distances in Sri Lanka. took five hours to get there and four hours to do the 115km back to Colombo. So if you plan to tour round Sri Lanka expect to spend lots of time sitting in a car. However, the 1.5 hours we spent in the Temple of the Tooth was very interesting. Our driver explained lots of interesting facts. You need to leave your shoes at the main entrance and it costs 1000 Rs each to get in (you do get a free DVD as part of the entrance fee). In places the paving slabs were very hot, we noticed some people had socks which was a great idea, so you might want to carry some socks just in case.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Without experimenting and without seeing things from a different angle you are left with what you have. I am not Buddhist, but I enjoy the religious atmosphere in the temple. People are genuinely paying their respect and hope for blessing in the temple. I believe it is fundamental need in every human. Go and experience it yourself.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I feel uncomfortable rating a holy site as a tourist attraction and do not wish to give offence. From the outside the temple complex with its lakeside location is very picturesque. However, inside is so crowded that it is impossible to see anything (if indeed there is very much to see) and it is very unpleasant being pushed along in the press of bodies in the heat. I should point out that the crowds are overwhelmingly devotees bringing flower offerings, not tourists, and that is well and good.  I have seen more interesting Buddhist temples however (generally more off the beaten track). Kandy offers more enjoyable places for the tourist (the Botanical Gardens and tea factories for example) so spend your time there. The bar of the immediately adjacent Queen's Hotel is a reasonable place to get a cold drink or pot of tea to cool off after the temple visit.

review_text: It was crowded and badly signed and overpriced. The temple of the tooth itself employs shovers, to push the crowds along, past the cask in which the tooth is stored. When you get to it, an angry monk barks at you to move on, whilst pushing a donation bowl at you. As foreigners, we'd had to pay on the way in to store our shoes, and the man in the shoe booth tried to extort an extra payment from us on the way out too. Not the most contemplative, or spiritual, buddhist temple I've been to. Don't recommend it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple houses the ancient tooth relic of Buddha. Very important to Buddhists in Sri Lanka. You need to have your legs and shoulders covered for women and legs covered for men. You have to leave your shoes and walk around in bare feet, they will look after your shoes and give you a ticket. The tooth is on show only every 5 years so you cannot see it. A guide will take you round and explain everything. Very beautiful.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We enjoyed looking round the temple of the tooth. Be aware that both men and women must have their legs covered (an enterprising local at the front entrance was doing a brisk trade in sarongs for men who turned up in shorts, myself included) and women must also cover their shoulders. We walked around for an hour or so and decided not to take any of the locals up on their numerous offers to give us a guided tour although in retrospect this could have been interesting and informative. All in all definitely worth a look, try to time your visit in conjunction with one of the services.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: a 14th century palace that is of significant importance to budhists in srilanaka. beautoiful carvings and well visited by tourists and locals. As this is like a budhist shrine, many locals come here to make their rituals. We had to change our clothing as shorts and sleevless clothing is doiscouraged. A very beaautiful setting

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was my first exposure to Buddhism and with the capable assistance of a knowledgable guide, my wife and I enjoyed the time in the Temple. Crowded?, VERY! But, the architecture and the shrines are beautiful. Our guide, a  Buddhist, was able to move us to the important areas and explained the significance of each. We arrived after dark, and as others have said, it is inspiring to see the devotion of the many peoples in attendance. Highly recommend you engage a knowledgable guide to make the most of your visit. By the way, you do have to check your shoes prior to entry. Socks recommended.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Buddhism is experienced in different kind of ways through Asia, but I prefer the temple of the tooth in Singapore instead of this one. Nonetheless it’s a must see in Kandy and overall in Sri Lanka. Honestly I liked the outside area more than the interior, because of the mystique atmosphere the Buddhist chants were creating in the evening sunlight. There is also a candle spot which overlooks the city of Kandy. We entered the temple half an hour before the evening ceremony started, so it was very crowded. To reinforce the atmosphere, 4 drummers and a flute-player dressed in traditional kandyan clothes will play (loud) music. Not only there were tourists, but also foreign (Chinese and Thai) monks with their family accompanying them. They had a standard gift packages (sold everywhere in Kandy) and lotus flowers. There was also a lot of movement in the shrine, reinforcing the question what is actually really happening in there. In my opinion you can spend an afternoon combining the temple and the nearby lake,

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Bit of a climb up steps or a windy steep path but worthit.Very crowded with lots of school parties but the children are part of the fun.You have to take off your shoes and the floor can be very hot but you can leave socks on.Watch out for the monkeys they will try ans steal hats food etc.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are not the temple thronging religious type, and if you have been to lots of temples in Asia, you can save time on your itinerary by giving this Buddha temple a miss. The waiting line to get inside was long during the evening (7pm around) and we spent a good 1-1.5hr inside the temple. Add the time required to navigate the traffic and parking around the temple. Once inside, the main Buddha statue and the ivory teeth placed around, offer a nice view.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is a UNESCO world heritage site, and for good reason. The complex, still in use as a buddhist temple, holds a very important buddhist relic, the tooth of buddha. It is said that he who owns the relic, has the power over the country. it is worshipped daily, don't miss the 12.00 ceremony. Furthermore, it has a nice museum, telling the story of the  attacks from 1998 and the history of the country. Very well preserved and more than worth visiting.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I went twice, once during the daytime to explore the Temple and the surrounding buildings and again in the evening for the 6:30 puja ceremony. If you retain your daytime ticket, you will not have to pay again for the puja ceremony.  During the day the crowds were thick, with people carrying all manner of flowers to place before the shrine.The crowds were even thicker for the evening ceremony and it was loud. There is no other way to describe it. The instruments made enough noise to give a rock concert a run for its money; I had to leave after about 15-20 minutes as my ears were hurting. But that said, it was fascinating to watch.  You can time it so you leave the Kandyan dance performance, which ends at 6 and simply walk the 5 minutes to the Temple for the evening ceremony.

review_text: Once we arrived a tour guide kind of attached himself to us. We couldn't understand a great deal of what he was telling us but still certainly worth it. He took us to all the areas of interest that we probably would have missed had we gone wondering around by ourselves.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Having seen a number of temples in my time, I would certainly not put this up with the best of them, and in many ways is similar to the free temples around Chiang Mai etc, however this has an entrance fee (about £5 DVD included)  and does have quite a good atmosphere when the tooth casket is displayed. There is music, drumming, queing, etc all for a very quick and jostled glimpse of a box. Then you can see a bit with some buddhas and some other rooms. I think the entrance fee is fair and I would recommend a visit, but it is by no means essential (a bit like Kandy in our minds).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A main attraction in Kandy. We went during the evening service and the atmosphere/music/people was incredible. Be prepared for it to be busy and put your valuables safely away but otherwise the atmosphere is lovely and a great experience to witness this Buddhist tradition and belief. The temple is beautiful, one room details the story of the Tooth, and there is a gorgeous candle room outside that looks out across Kandy, where you can light a candle and feel very humbled. You cant go to Kandy and not visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple was the main reason we came to Kandy. Make no mistake: you will  not see a tooth! It's more about catching the atmosphere and see worshippers pass by in awe. Despite this being a holy place, locals tend to behave pretty rude, in particular towards foreigners.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a religious/cultural site in the heart of Kandy town. The entire town of Kandy is built around this memorial site. There are beautiful flower stalls lining the street outside the monument with brilliantly hued lotus flowers. You can't enter in shorts or tank tops so dress appropriately

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A long held dream realised ... Being in the presence of this relic of the Buddha. It felt like I had to fight to maintain my place in the slowly moving queue of pilgrims to file past the relic and leave my floral offering. I was amazed at the pushing and shoving ... To get where exactly? It was also quite difficult to find a space to spend time quietly contemplating the relic. Maybe I am too stuck in my Western ways with my western expectations. The temple complex is very interesting ... The shrine a place of mystery, opening and closing a couple of times during the day. Check the times.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth, surrounding gardens and buildings are magnificent. The only problem was (hypocrital of me) the tourist side of things. People are in the temple wanting to pray...all the while tourists brushing past, taking photographs, queuing everywhere. Although it was a great place to see, tourist numbers should be restricted and buddhists should be able to come to what should be a tranquil place...not somewhere that is like a busy market. On the otherhand, the culture here is priceless and our guide gave us a great insight about his religion, from the heart (and mind!).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Chance to see a lot of great history I am just not to keen on walking in as a spectator while people are actively praying.  And when I went they were lots of people there to actually pray.  So I spent more time in the museum than in the main area

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I visited this temple in 2014.The temple of truth is 2600 years old.One of the best temple having a beautiful exterior and interior architecture.We can  see some beautiful paintings inside the temple.A divine place.If we are in Kandy ........ A best temple to visit as a tourist.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited the temple at about 6pm, straight after the nearby cultural show at 5pm. Obviously can't compare with other times of day, but I thought this was a great time to visit. As it was nearly dark when we arrived I at first thought we had missed the opportunity for good photos, which perhaps we did, but in return we experienced the temple at a very atmospheric time. After the initial queue to be searched (males and females line up separately, but ended up just being a quick bag search), we wandered with our guide. There was a lot of people, but also a lot of local people and I just found the atmosphere quite enjoyable at this time of evening. In relation to the tooth, we lined up just before 7pm and waited in line for no more than 10 minutes for what really was a quick rush past to see the casket, which is quite impressive, but it is more the Whole experience and excitement of it that I found intriguing, and then I had had enough of the crowd!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was a lovely lovely place to visit. It felt so serene and peaceful. There was hardly any noice chatter etc other than then chants. It was not terribly packed on the day we had gone although still a lot of people milling about. It was very clean and well organised. A must visit if you are in the area. The Lotus flower colours and arrangements were just awesome. You can do the visit in about 1-2 hrs but if you can, stay there longer and take in the atmosphere.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went to this temple on 25th Feb. The temple's  surroundings were serene,clean & beautiful .The  devotees were orderly and  allowed us to pray in  peace .I  cannot say this about temples in India. On the whole a divine experience which I have not felt in many places.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We arrived at a busy time and to see the Tooth Relic there were two options - queue for ages to get into the room with the relic or walk past the outside of the room. Our group took option 2. It was busier than the tube at rush hour - avoid if you are claustrophobic.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple in the evening at time of offering in the middle of February, high season in SL. It could have been a nice visit, but it was completely ruined by loads of tourists pushing around, using flashes and ipads to shoot pictures... I have visited hundreds of temples, and I am looking for quiet, peaceful place to contemplete and switch for a moment from the busy life. This temple, although very beautiful, is just a opposite of it. I feel very sorry for all the pilgrims, that they have to suffer from these crowds of undelicate people. I should have known better from the previous reviews, but I wanted to give it a try ...

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: An afternoon visit on a weekend was really a jam packed experience, the tourists pushed more than the locals who appeared to view the tourists as weird visitors from another world, which perhaps we were. Library worth a visit, and the view over the Temple from the library windows spectacular.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Clearly a highlight of not only Kandy but Sri Lanka.  Not sure what some people on here were expecting, but here is an honest review. Pro's - You are getting to see a real Buddhist ceremony subject to crowds (the Buddhists paying respects and tourist taking pictures). You are paying a small price for the opportunity to see and look around a genuine Buddhist 'mecca' (entry fee of 1000Rs).  Guides will provide you with a cheap (500Rs) overview of the site and traditions.  The area is generally clean and well presented, people at the site are helpful. Con's - ladies and gents you must cover to below the knee and over the shoulders,  so longer shorts and no vests, it can get warm so take water.  Also no shoes, so pack socks which can be warn if you have sensitive soles.  Wear flipflops to the site and carry with you inside a bag otherwise pay for storage  at the site entrance.  Other tourists believing that their 'picture' is more important than the ceremony going on, all nations having a total lack of respect for the locals and visiting Buddhists.  Crowds, if you dont do well with them avoid the ceremony times, the locals are okay, but again the tourists from all over and all ages bring an attitude and no patience. Id highly recommend a visit, it was an interesting relatively cheap outing for a morning, 3 hours tops and your done.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The set up of the temple is amazing and there's an instantly relaxed and calming vibe around the whole place.  Go for one of the ceremony times (3 in the day) when they open the door to the casket housing the tooth relic and you can walk past and see it. I found a guide inside who was amazing, only cost 500R and was highly knowledgeable and told me exactly where to go and stand etc for the ceremony which was truly valuable. A great place to learn some history.

review_text: An experience of walking through a temple barefoot, through pathways and up and down stairs. Very busy on the day I visited as it was a public holiday, so check first, as you don't see the tooth very easily because of the crowds. It is a fascinating story about the budha.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our guide brought us here at 5pm to experience the daily offering ceremony. Hundreds of devoted people give thanks to the Buddha and give their offerings, mainly flowers. fruit and vegetables. or, some give a gift pack of a monks essentials. (robe, bag, thread. needle and flip flops/ The tooth relic is kept behind gold doors, in a gold tabernacle type container, which can only be seen during the ceremony It was one of the best experiences of our tour of Sri Lanka and I am very happy that our guide changed our itinerary so we could experience it. The drummers, who play for the hour that the golden doors are open add to the atmosphere .  If you are going to Kandy don.t miss it.

review_text: It was first temple I felt the soul of the place. People are coming for preying and blessing not only for visiting. Beautiful. Very interesting international museum of buddism. Be aware of "guides" who want to earn money as everywhere in Sri Lanka. At 10.30 is the blessing ceremony.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple along with the lake, are very beautiful. But since this is a religious place, it gets very crowded on auspicious days, and we landed there on one of such days. Try to dress in white if possible when you visit the temple and if you are a foreigner take your time to explore the temple as the entry is expensive. Overall the temple is clean and serene and good place to relax your mind

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: First impression - Nice and clean temple - The offering are kept neatly, premises are clean, well-lit. Footwear kept organized. But quite crowded and be careful of the guides - I think quite expensive and have half knowledge. Our group of 30+ people went around 6:30 p.m. We got 1 guide who explained some bits going inside, then we were made to stand in a queue going up the stairs to the floor where the tooth relic is kept inside a golden dome. So, as such one can't see the tooth itself. There are actually 2 queues - 1 which goes from outside where the flowers are offered and other very close to the chamber where dome is kept. We realized later that we were in the outer queue and saw the relic from some distance. Also, people who have gone in the inner queue come in between our line of vision and the dome chamber. In the queue too, people keep pushing or joining in between. In all this, the door of the chamber closed around 7 p.m. and half of us were not able to even get a glimpse. The guide then again wrongly told us the door would open only after 1/2 an hour. But we waited, then somebody told us that it actually shuts and opens in intervals of 10 minutes between 6 and 8 p.m. So, then finally we went in the inner queue and got a good glimpse of the tooth relic. So, if you really religious, have enough patience or haven't had the cultural experience or if you just are curious about the place like me, then surely visit and enjoy. The tooth itself is displayed only once in 5-6 years or so, though they have a yearly procession of the tooth relic in dome.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Being a public holiday, the temple was bursting with worshippers which created a wonderful atmosphere. It has a fascinating history, struck by terrorist bombing on two occasions and rebuilt each time. There are wonderful stone carvings, wall paintings, gold, ivory and various gem stones in abundance and of course the tooth relic. Well worth a visit.

review_text: Temple of the Tooth. As everyone else described. Busy, felt intrusive when there were genuine worshippers there. No camera charge unless you wanted to buy a video permit. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: probably because i have seen a lot of temples during my past 8 years in Asia (i live in China): this temple is supposed to be THE temple in sri lanka, unfortunately i have to admit that relatively this is not interesting at all for people who are simply interested in cultures, architectures and religions. If you're pious it's a different case.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was the top of my wifes "to do" list in Kandy. We went on a saturday morning. Entrance was R1000 each and straight away we were in a conga line of worshippers. No dancing, just pushing. The line snaked from the entrance to the area with the tooth relic. Variety was added by the Aunties and Grandma's pushing and shoving their way to the front and stepping on toes as if they had a divine right to the front of the queue. Once in the viewing area you are rushed past a small viewing area by staff and if lucky catch a brief ( 5 seconds?) glimpse of the shrine. No photos. You end up on the far side of the shrine and I tried to get a better look from the back of the crowd ( height advantage). You will find yourself treading on worshippers kneeling randomly and obliviously to everything else. Again a longer glimpse but it is tricky to remain in place due to crowd dynamics.Certainly no chance of a photo. Once out of the chamber the pace slackened and I was able to relax and enjoy the rest of the temples and museums. I felt a bit deflated by the first part and would not bother again. However my wife loved it so that is priceless. We passed it on Sunday morning on the way elsewhere and the crowds were horrendous. TOP TIP: Go early on a weekday.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A default visit for any traveller visiting kandy town. A sprawling complex housing one of the most revered buddhist relics. Take time off to visit the museum of world buddhism located just behind the main shrine, and several small devlayas located within the complex. The Entrance fee is 500SLR for SAARC nationals and 1000SLR for nationals of other countries.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Go in the evening when they take the relic out and people come in to meditate and give offerings. You will be searched before entering and men and women have to dress modestly. It's a bit of a scene when the relic first comes out, but if you wander around the other rooms of the temple and come back toward the end of the frenzy you can see the relic without having to stand in the long line. Give yourself at least 90 minutes or more to soak it all in.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Legend and the belief is that molar tooth of The Buddha was brought from India and enshrined in this Temple .  Temple of Tooh Relic is deeply revered by the  majority Buddhist  population of Sri Lanka . It is a major religious pilgrim center of all the followers of Buddhist faith not only from Sri Lanka but from all over the World . Visiting this place and offering prayers on Full Moon Day is of special significance . Due to these reasons there is large crowd on almost all the days but particularly the crowd becomes very large and difficult to manage of full moon days. The Temple and the surrounding buildings are very well kept . The statues , stone carvings on pillars and door arches  and murals on the interior walls are beautiful and therefore deserved to be a tourist attraction . If you are deeply religious Buddhist person do brave the crowds and the long queues and  visit the shrine where the crown containing the tooth is displayed . If you are a normal tourist visit the complete complex with out getting in the queue and the crowds . Happy viewing .

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Better than expected, and rather beautiful.  Interesting history and gives you a snapshot of part of the beating heart of Sri Lanka.  We felt privileged to visit and were extremely conscious of not disturbing many of the devout waiting to pay homage to the tooth. Tip: Make sure you have your knees and shoulders covered, and be as respectful as possible. Also, you must take off your shoes, and some pathways are a bit stoney so if you have poor feet, beware.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Some aspects of this temple was really nice such as the wooden treasury building and the shrine which shows the life of Prince Siddhartha. They open the doors for the tooth casket 3 times a day but the queue is horrendous! The smell of the temple is lovely with all the jasmine and lotus - but do not smell them as it's unlucky! Also wear long sleeves and trousers to enter. We took a guided tour and he was quite good showing everything about the temple (much of which can be read in a guide book) albeit he was rushing a bit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Unfortunately our visit was too short but a helpful official guide called Kandy(!) told us a lot about the temple and the Buddhist philosophy.  For Buddhists it is equivalent to Jerusalem or Mecca, but it seemed to be much more peaceful than either of those.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple campus which is said to house the tooth Relic of the Buddha stands in splendid isolation in the busy part of Kandy. The temple premises has the look of a manicured garden, with a beautiful man-made lake next to it. But, alas, we cannot see the tooth relic. It is housed in the first floor of the temple in a beautifully ornamented casket. This is said to have been brought from India by Princess Hema Mala in the 4th Century AD. Until the early 19th century, this temple was not completed as shrine for the tooth relic, by the last Kandian King Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe.  Even during the annual festival which falls due in August every year, the casket is taken in procession on elephant.  None in the present generation actually seems to have seen the tooth relic, except perhaps the head of the monastery attached to this temple, who is also the supreme head of Buddhist churches in Sri Lanka.  Nevertheless, the temple is beautifully ornamented with lots of gems, gold and other precious materials. Take care not to turn your back to Buddha's idol and pose for photographs. That is considered extremely offensive by the Sri Lankan Buddhists.  There is a beautiful museum attached to this temple which must be seen. Photography is permitted everywhere except the museum.

review_text: A very important site for Buddhists in Sri Lanka where the sacred relic of Buddha's tooth, rescued from his cremated body and transported in secret from India is housed.  This means that the Temple is likely to be busy with both tourists, pilgrims and monks from other countries so there could be long queues to see the golden casket that houses the tooth and the sacred library.  On the upper floors there are artefacts and belonging of the various rulers of Kandy over the centuries.  Take time out to visit this area.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Tooth temple is very significant for Buddhist primarily but for all it has museum, once in a year perehera (a local temple specific festival) and the story about tooth of Buddha taken there after his demise. The parts of body of Buddha wherever it is secretly kept has all big establishment e.g.hair in Shwe Dagon Pagoda of Myanmar. Both are spectacular. For Hindus, tooth of Mahakali (Bhagawati) was shed in a place called Vijaypur, Dharan ofEastern Nepal is visited by most of the Hindus  - has lot of religious significance and the hill where this temple is located has other temple of particular spiritual significance called Budhasubba (temple in the name of equivalent to sage) and Pindeswor Dham of Lord Shiva, who visited there with Goddess Parbati and shed tears after being so happy and those turned into Rudraksha trees. Rudraksha are again very sacred for Hindus. So, here I wanted to highlight few similarities across religions and their significance,

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

Recommend you go at prayer time (we went at 10.30) and you get a feel for what the temple means to the locals and see the religious activities. review_text: My wife & I visited the Temple of the Tooth on Poya Day in January.  The place was heaving with Pilgrims which added to the atmosphere and the religious fervour. Even allowing for the heavy numbers of worshippers, pilgrims, monks and tourists, my wife and I both were able to make our way to the very front to see the casket that contains the relic. A Must Do!  I Recoomend a Visit particularly if you are able to visit on a Poya Day

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are a foreigner and come to Kandy and go without visiting the Dalada Maligawa it is like going to Egypt and not seeing the Pyramids ! Be warned that you need to 'cover your legs' and 'body' - so no shorts and low cut dresses, tops are allowed.  Best to go in Jeans and T Shirt... The architecture is awesome - though nothing compared to the magnificent stupas in Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa.  Also, be warned that it is absolutely a hive of activity during the weekends - specially on Sundays - when it gets packed with the 'faithful'.  Right throughout the day you will have visitors coming in - and probably the best time to go is in the morning around six to see the customary drumming and poojas taking place... Don't forget to see the museum dedicated to a faithful tusker !

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Discount can be availed if you are a resident of SAARC country, so please carry your passport with you. Located in the heart of the city beside the Kandy lake, this is a beautiful place. Remember, this is a TEMPLE. So go there to PRAY, not gossip or just click pictures... We saw a few people clicking pictures with the shrine in the background, when there is a board which specifically says that "Do not take photograph of yourself with the shrine in the background". So please DONT do that, because there must be some reason behind it. We didn't get into the reason; but its obvious that when it is specifically instructed, refrain from it. I think the images of the temple should be captured in your mind, not in the camera! Also, if you are buying flowers to offer , please don't smell them - its wrong to do so. It is very peaceful inside. They offer the view of the shrine from a small window at specific time in the morning and evening. Do enquire the landlord of the place of your stay for the timings. We got to see the shrine in the evening time(around 1800 hrs), since we had been there in the evening. There`s  a Vishnu temple and a Naath temple in the premises as well, so do make sure you explore all the aspects of the premises. Unfortunately we couldn`t because it was raining heavily. So pray with sincerity, and discipline yourself- you will be satisfied when you leave the temple.. :)

review_text: Temple of Tooth is Kandy is a "must-see" if you're in that area. Former royal palace, the complex boasts a very formidable architecture and history. Definitely can be a very pleasurable experience as long as you don't get scammed by "guides". There are few advices from our mistakes: we were conned to believe that having a government licensed guide is mandatory. It is not. You can enter premises without any guide, as long as you're properly attired and follow rules (they are written in English in each hall). You'll have to remove your shoes and socks to enter the palace grounds. If you decided to get a guide, agree on the fee and length of the tour beforehand. We didn't and ended up listening all kind of stories about him, his family and monetary problems for over 3 hours, unable to break free from his clutches. When they say "You pay me after as much as you feel I deserve" - it's a huge trap, because at the end you will be pressed to give exorbitant amount you did not even dreamed to pay, so all the "pay if you're happy" is just a way to lure you to hire the guy.

I also feel that charging money for the temple is not right in form of a ticket. Anyways its one of the major Buddha destinations in Srilanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

I admired all the Kandyan motifs, paintings and arts within the temple, caught a quick glimpse of the casket holding the buddha's tooth (you can't see it) I took in the whole place leisurely, allowing myself ample time to appreciate everything, it was a wonderful experience. This is a must-see place when in Kandy.

review_text: The temple of the sacred tooth relic or the Dalada maligawa has to be the greatest Buddhist shrine in Sri lanka. Since Kandy was the capital of ancient Sri lanka from 1592 to 1815, reigned by many great Kings. The temple opined as the heart of the Kandy city. The sacred tooth relic was received to Sri lanka about 16 centuries ago. The other tooth relic is believed to be placed in the Somawthi Dagoba. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I'm sure it had great history, but we felt like a herd of cattle getting ushered through to get a glimpse of the casket for all of 0.5 seconds. Even this minor glimpse was distracted by a monk pointing to a bowl wanting donations. It felt a little like vatican city where you the cash machines rolling with the sound of notes being counted. The building however was beautiful and intricate. All in all, if you don't have much time in Kandy, I would personally go and explore the city rather than see another temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The site is interesting- temple or group of temples perched on a hilltop with a steep climb yet worth the effort. There are several rooms of worship and of religious significance, with some interesting mix between Buddhist and Hindu rituals in at least one. The most interesting aspect I found was also the devotion of the people to the times of prayer and the very smily and happy faces of people entering and leaving the site.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I find it really interesting to see how other religions are played out and the ceremony of the Tooth was one of those times. As another reviewer said it is a little crazy for the amount of people in a small space but our guide was very clever judging the queues. The guide also bought us flowers to offer to The Tooth Relic and we were taken by a monk up to an alter were we received a blessing ( this cost of course! ) My husband and I are Church of England but we found it quite moving. Definitely worth a visit

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: There are temples all over Sri Lanka and Bhuddist monks wandering about everywhere with their laptops! This temple has massive significance to the Sri Lankan people and our guide was keen to take us there for a service of the relic. It cost 1000 roupees to enter (around £5 each) and 300 roupees to hold your shoes. We were curious about the relic and were keen to see what has attracted so many people. When I say it was like being in a sardine tin, I'm not exaggerating! We couldn't move once we got in and the queues were like waiting for a lady Gaga concert. We got a picture of the relic, just before the end of the service, but as we're not Buddhists, it didn't have the relevance for us. I'm glad we went, it was quite interesting, but it's a place you only want to be once.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This beautiful temple located on the shores of the Kandy Lake has great spiritual value for Buddhists from all over the world. It was truly a spiritual experience to witness the late ceremony when the sacred urn was displayed. Please check the timings for the daily rituals when the urn is displayed to the public. Be prepared to wait in a queue and get jostled to get a view of it. There are a lot of interesting Buddhist artifacts on display in the various chambers in the temple.  You will need to plan for atleast 2 hours if you wish to see the exhibits in all the  chambers in the temple. You are filled with peace and tranquility when you visit this temple. I was really saddened to see throngs of tourists jostling to get photo opportunities in the temple, thereby hampering local devotees who are there to express their faith and donate offerings.  The temple authorities should impose a ban on photography within the temple premises.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our driver rearranged our visit time to early morning to take us when there was a ceremony taking place, this was NOT a good idea because the place was crowded and a crush. You don't see the tooth which is inside a series of cases, rather like those Russian mother dolls. There are some small doors, about 2 feet square that are opened for about 15 minutes during the service and you look through and in the distance glimpse the outermost case that is said to contain the tooth. There was a massive queue of people waiting to glimpse this and our driver/guide whipped us away almost as soon as the doors opened. I almost fell in the crush because there were people sat on the floor with the legs outstretched. My wife and I are Christians, as such I reccomend visiting any other religious site when there is no activity taking place so you have time to appreciate the building and the wider context. I was somewhat disgruntled to find that we had to pay an entry fee because our holiday package was expensive. Generally Sri Lanka has two prices, one for foreign tourists and one for local people, we felt that the price were we charged was similar to what one would pay for a top attraction in Europe.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Take a small bag to carry your shoes and wear long pants. Get a guide in order to really understand all you will see in the temple. Be prepared for crowds but don't worry as everyone is very very calm and easy going. The architecture is beautiful and the ceremonies are fascinating. Must see in Kandy.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went there on a ceremony day, the day the Budhha was supposed to have attained enlightenment. And the people celebrated by offering a million lotus flowers. So many people flocked here all day to merely play their respect and offer the flower they carried. Truly, an experience we happened to by chance

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

Although, the temple has some historical significance it wont appear to be a tourist attraction if you arent well aware of Buddhism. It is indeed a place for sanctity and peace and if you are a very religious person, the place is apt for you.

review_text: What an exciting city Kandy is! Taking a peaceful, uneventful road toward it, one can hardly imagine the excitement that awaits one in this city.  Entering it you get a feel of a great experience awaiting you.  Taking the hairpin bends you know its a hilly town with a pleasantly cold weather that will dissipate the heat of the trip on the road. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Located in the city of Kandy, this site houses a relic of the tooth of Buddha. Since ancient times, the relic has played an important role in local politics where the country’s belief lied that whoever controls the relic has the right to rule the country. Kandy was the last capital of the Sri Lankan kings and a UNESCO world heritage site. It is located on top of the hill by the lake. Since it is a temple, dress accordingly; women with covered shoulders and both genders with no legs showing. The building embodies a magnificent architecture complete with moat. We arrived here after watching the Kandyan Cultural Dance which is located next door, the festive lights and the huge crowd made it a night to punctuate with a  and great sleep. The length of time depends how much you want to spend inside watching all the activities and touring the entire area.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Here is the disappointing summary of my visit of the tooth temple: (1) the price is 1,000 rupee per person (2) waiting lines to see the golden Dagoba (houses the tooth of buddha) can be quite long (one hour or more). (3) one can not see the tooth only the Dagoba that houses it. This takes about 2-3 Seconds as the personnel will motivate you to move on. The temple is quite commerialized and the entrance fee is high compared to the experience that you get ( I thought of a rip-off). I would not recommend it for Non-Buddist and would not go again. If you go: (1) Go when there is a puja (ceremony) if you want it loud and cultural. (2) You can only get a view of the Dagoba during a puja. (3) to see the Dagoba: Do not stand in the waiting line and go directly to the shrine that houses the Dagoba. (Follow the entrance sign in the temple). The door of the shrine will be opened during the ceremony (Puja) and you get a good view of the Dagoba which is the same the people in the waiting line get. (4) take your shoes in a bag with you to save a few rupees. (5) You will not be able to get behind the door of the shrine as this is restricted for respected buddists. (6) read about the temple and it's purpose before you enter it as rhis will help to understand the procedure.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is a magnificent sight to be sure and as a national treasure and magnificent monument it is worth seeing - but surely it goes against the very principals of Buddhism to revere a body part - even if it is the Buddha's tooth? To enshrine it in a solid golden, jewel encrusted shrine, patrolled by guards with walkie-talkies and then pray to it? Buddha taught the elimination of thirst is the way to enlightenment - thirst for EVERYTHING - including riches, praise and reverence - he said 'do not revere me, I am just a man' so why a golden temple to hold a tooth? But definitely you should go and see it - just so long as you realist that THIS IS NOT THE MESSAGE OF BUDDHISM - it is a tourist attraction.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a once in a lifetime site, if you aren't lucky enough to go several times. A beautiful Buddhist temple complex with a moat, incredible vistas, carved stone and work, incense and flowers. The reverence of worshippers visiting the site that houses the tooth of the Bhudda in an ornate golden casket was very moving. Entire families were relishing the environment, new babies brought for blessings, and many absorbed in prayer. The dignity of the monks was awe inspiring. Officials gently and quietly managed the crowds and kept the line in front of the casket moving briskly. Everything was clear, orderly, and controlled. Everything in the temple is invested with meaning and significance and it is worth taking your time to appreciate the detail. There is a museum in the complex, worth seeing - but read up before you go to appreciate what you are looking at because it is poorly curated, to put it mildly.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of Tooth Relic is a very sacred temple for Buddhists. It also holds historical value for even the non-Buddhists as it served as a political and architectural landmark in the Sri Lankan history. It is a must-see place if you go to Kandy! Dress code should be given importance to, as short dresses/trousers are not allowed due to religious reasons. Also, make sure you go within the times that the compartment which holds the sacred tooth relic is open to the public (it closes sometime between 10am and 11am in the morning and again in the evening). Another must-see item there is the museum for tusker Raja.

review_text: This temple had a great story that was explained to us as our tour guide took us through. review_text: This is a must visit site when in Kandy....There is an entry fee to enter the temple & vendors selling flowers for offerings in the temple Being from a SAARC country the entry fee was much less as compared to the one for the other countries Fantastic views & sitting in a corner gave real peace Great views outside also....Dont Miss :) Visited in Oct 2010

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: As we passed the garden of the temple, I saw the statue of the monk Wariyapola Sri Mangala who took down the Union Jack and raised the Sinhalese lion flag before the convention that handed over the control of the Kandyan kingdom to the British in 1815. There is an entry fee of SLR 500 for my entrance ticket. After taking off my soft shoe, I entered the temple We went to see the treasury and a large Buddha statue in front of it. We then went to a hall which housed another large Buddha statue. From the guide I could gather that readings were made from the Dhammapad and mainly from the Tripitaka. I went to the section containing the stuffed temple elephant Raja – the Maligawa Tusker, the guide led us to the place. On the way the devotees were burning incense on a terrace. The room had the stuffed elephant which was much loved and had served the temple for more than 50 years. He was caught in the jungles and trained here. He was declared a national treasure by the then Sri Lankan president – Jaywardene. With time to spare we headed for the museum situated in 1st and 2nd floor. It has an array of gilded and bejeweled reliquaries and gifts to the temple. There were statues of past head priests of the temple. It also has pictures of the damages caused by a bomb attack in 1988. I then went to witness the religious ceremony that was about to tske place. There are 3 ceremonies each day at 6 am, 10.00 am and at 6pm. Only during these times when the ceremonies are on is the chamber containing the Golden Casket containing the Holy Tooth opened and the visitors and worshippers can see the casket. To reach the chamber where the holy relique is kept, we had to climb a series of stairs. There were a lot of foreigners and devotees and worshippers. There were two lines. One close to the casket from where a good view can be obtained but no photography is allowed. In the other line which is behind the first row, the visitors can take pictures. Soon the temple drums started beating signifying that the ceremony was about to begin. A little later the chamber was opened and our line started moving. I entered the chamber and had a look at the Golden Casket. After this, I went and joined the crowd behind and after getting a good position, started taking some pictures. I was thankful that I had the opportunity to see the holy casket. On the way out, I saw the temple drummers beating the drums near the Treasury and a group of tourists and devotees had gathered to watch the drummers.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A great place to visit. This is the most venerable place for the Buddhists, as it gives shelter to the tooth relic of Lord Buddha. It is interesting to see the series of pictures relating the story of the tooth relic which came from India after the cremation of Lord Buddha about 2600 years ago. One should not miss the pictures of destruction caused by the LTTE terrorist attack on the temple in 1996. Other interesting item to see is the museum dedicated for the tusker named Raja who served carrying the tooth relic in Kandy perehara for nearly 45 years. It is an eye opener to see the devotion of Lankan people for the sacred place.

After being there as long as you wish you can then look at what is left of the royal palace grounds which are adjacent to the temple.. "

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I can't imagine anyone would visit Kandy and miss the Temple of the Tooth, but whatever you do, don't miss a visit here.  I was here for the morning puja and was very moved by the devotion shown by the faithful.  The temple itself is a fine piece of architecture and a quick turn around the Raja Tusker museum not to be missed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This temple is 100% worth checking out. One of the highlights in Kandy. The colors, paintings, history. Buddha's tooth is in this temple hence the name. There is also a very old painting made of sand that is quite special. And there is a separate room outside with an embalmed royal elephant (his name was Raja) who served in the Peraheras for 50 years. Don't miss it!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I had heard so much about the significance and travels of the Buddha's tooth relic that seeing the temple where it is presently housed was a must. The temple building is interesting from a historical perspective but what caught my attention was the devotion of the many pilgrims and the groups of enthusiastic young school children led by their somewhat harried teachers.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Security is tighter at this temple due to an attack in the 1990s during the civil war. However, it is definitely a must visit for Buddhists and visitors. The entire complex is full of ornate tiling works, granite beams and woodwork. The temple has 2 levels - the top wooden floor housing the sacred tooth. The door to the sacred tooth casket is opened 3x per day at 5.30 am, 9.30am and 6.30 pm. If you want to witness the casket then go to the temple around these times but it will be busier with more locals/devotees. The entrance fee was LKR 1000 but worth it. As with most Sri Lanka heritage sites, it is beautifully preserved and serene.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It's a wonderful Buddha temple. The architecture is great and so is the history behind the temple. It has stood through time and the turmoils of the local riots in Srilanka. Parts destroyed during the times of terror have been reconstructed well. I unfortunately happened to visit on a Sunday and it was crowded with a lot of locals offering their prayers. The long queues and the ushers who ask to move along real fast on reaching The Buddha, reminded me of the wait at Tirupathi temples in India. If you want to go see this temple slowly for its beauty and peace, go on a weekday. If you want to experience the method of worship of the Srilankans, the blue lotus offering to The Buddha, then you could visit on a weekend. The entrance is about $ 10 for non Srilankans. As in other temples in India, you would need to leave your foot wear outside. It can be deposited at a counter for free, but a small tip is ideal. There is also a dress code at the temple -shorts and sleeveless t shirts are considered disrespectful and hence not allowed. My hotel in Kandy was kind enough to inform me of this in advance and I think most hotels are...but just in case they forget, I thought It would be better to mention it here. Of course you don't get to see the tooth of The Buddha. It's enclosed in a casket and is only taken out once in 5 yrs for the public.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Must-see attraction in Kandy, mainly because of the significance of the temple to the local people. Throngs of locals visit the temple daily to pray and make offerings. Tourists had to pay to enter, but still a great experience to experience the local culture, history and religion. View of the temple is great and mystical during the evening puja. Come after the cultural dance which is just nearby.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is the home of Buddhism in Sri Lanka.  Its golden roof can be seen glittering from many vantage points around Kandy, and is always a sight to behold.  We were lucky enough to visit at the time of the Perahara, when the Temple was lit up with tiny lights.  It was a breathtaking sight, especially as the sun went down.  The elephants taking part in the Perahara were grazing on the lawns outside, and later we got to watch the lead tusker being dressed for the event  Highly recommended at any time of year, but especially beautiful during the Perahara.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Loved the ceromony and the flowers but most of all a living, working temple.  We were lucky to arrive as the tooth ceremony took place, a little dramatic perhaps but clearly the locals making their offerings gave it an authentic atmosphere.  Some of the side rooms are truly wonderfull.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Would have preferred to soak up the atmosphere of Kandy.  Temple of tooth is sacred to buddhists but not much to see. We took lotus flowers and had a quick tour.  The door to the tooth container was closed and I felt voyeruistic amongst the many sri lankans who had come to pray.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are in Kandy you really have to do this, our guide Roshan ( supplied by Kuoni and would recommend ) explained a lot about Buddhism so we had an understanding of what was involved. We went in the evening and it was extremely busy, people shoulder to shoulder queueing to see everything. Consequently it was very hot and at times uncomfortable, also having left your shoes behind to enter you get your feet trodden on occasionally. The temple itself is very interesting and quite beautiful, many artefacts etc are contained within and it really is well worth a look. The problem we had was that it is a real temple and lots of people are trying to worship in there amongst the chaos of tourists and kids running around and I couldn't help feel like we were intruding on something personal. Our visit was a bit frantic and rushed in places and I found lacked something because of this, but would still recommend it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: the entry fee is a little steep, even after we got the special India discount but that should not take away the serenity of this temple. The inner sanctum is very serene and calming as well as has the complete story of the temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A brilliant and comprehensive precis of what the religion is all about  - very dramatic, particularly as we went just before it closed so it wasn't so packed that you couldn't take it in. It was also dark so even more spectacular by the lake.  Thanks to Jai our brilliant driver/guide

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the temple as part of a whirlwind tour of Kandy, as we were only there for a quick overnight. Fortunately we met up with a wonderful driver when we arrived at the train station (send me a private message for his contact info). If we had tried to figure this out ourselves we wouldn't have had nearly as great an experience. He took us to the temple after going to see the dance show. He hooked us up with the right tour guide at the temple, who in turn showed us the ropes, including where to stand to see the crypt open to reveal the coffin with the tooth relic. It is really amazing that this ceremony has been going on for so long and is clearly still so powerful. It is worth being there during the daily ceremony, but would be overwhelming if you didn't have a guide to help you with everything from admission to providing historical information to negotiating the crowds to getting your shoes quickly when you leave.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was a good cultural experience observing the locals go through the ceremony. I planned to visit this one due to its religious importance so I didn't have much expectations. review_text: It is worth a visit, but it's only okay. Get a guide to understand things, otherwise most of it will go over your head. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Kandy is a disappointment: dirty, scruffy, noisy and lacking tourist infrastructure. We visited the Temple for the regular evening "puja". Read the guide books first because you will not be able to do so in the Temple due to the press of people. I took no photos as I consider it disrespectful in such a holy place. It was dark for our visit and the monsoon had arrived. The whole thing was atmospheric with the trumpets, drums, incense, candles and myriads of devotees.  A great mystical experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Went just the day before the 2013 escala perahera festival in August, knowing that the temple would be impossibly crowded and jammed with devotees during the annual event. Arrived at the temple in time for the 6.30pm puja. Didn't read about the unofficial guides touting foreigners. We only had a driver with us throughout our trip in SL. I decided to engage one guide with an "official tag" hanging on his neck - didn't see exactly what it wrote. Didn't know if he charges for the service - should have asked him, but I was so looking forward to the temple. It turned out to be the best decision I had ever made on a trip and it worth every cent of the sum paid for his service (for all 4 persons) Language wise, he didn't speak very good English, only managed to catch some facts about the temple. There were very loud music leading to the starting of the puja, we could not hear him well. However our guide was very precise about what will happen at what time for the evening puja and we managed to cover essential areas of the temple within the time gaps before the puja started and he led us to the tooth viewing area despite a strong crowd. He ensured that all of us took a centre stage view of the tooth, he managed to do this because he led us walked anti clockwise direction of the second floor - he had to do it otherwise it would be at least an hour wait for the viewing of the tooth. Post that, he cleared the way for us to exit the second floor by getting people who were occupying space by sitting on the floor, to stand up, freeing some walking space for us and for the rest of the visitors at the second floor. That act eased the human traffic immediately and we were able to exit the crowded area quickly. I wasn't sure if he is really an official guide from the temple. However, no one stop him from doing what locals usually dun do like walking anti clockwise direction around the temple. Clearly, the local devotees were all listening to his instructions to clear the way for us, all done in a gentle manner, no shouting or anger. We wouldn't have covered all of the puja event if not for the guide. We would have quietly queued for at least an hour for tooth viewing, missing out on other parts of the temple. Musuems in the temple had closed for the day and it would have been a boring visit to the world famous temple if it is not for him. We later found out that our driver is non buddhist and he would probably be clueless about the temple puja event and likely not able to provide the service that our temple guide did. I didn't remember our temple guide name unfortunately but he made our trip to the temple memorable for us in years to come.

review_text: One of the key temples in Sri Lanka and in the Buddhist world. Among a few tourists, locals come for prayers in families and in groups, giving this place a unique sense of real spirituality. It is actually bigger than its looks on the outside - the gardens are quite big so it is worth taking 2 hours at least to stroll around and feel the place.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Kandy is one of the sacred cities in the world.The sacred tooth relic of Buddha is the most venerated object of worship for Buddhists.The temple buildings are not magnificent.White red roofs and they cluster around the Kandy lake. The glittering Esala Perahara is one of the best events of this which you should see. The best scenery of here is when the night comes the shadow of Sri Dalada Maligawa which is nicely lighted with large number of bulbs with the gold roof can be seen through the Kandy lake.Here you won't be able to entered in to the temple without covering your knees.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Be sure you cover your knees both males and females otherwise you are not allowed in and have to purchase a sarong from the guards brother at an great expense! The temple was amazing though and the history behind the tooth fscinating

review_text: Visited the temple during the service , and joined in , the atmosphere pierced through me , and I made offerings. The sound of the drums and being surrounded by worshiping Buddhists was a real life experience.
