review_text: Was really looking forward to visiting the Temple of the Tooth but to be honest I found it to be over hyped and not a lot. Maybe it is because I am not a very religious man but what I saw there I had seen many times in other temples/sacred places around the world. We went on a Sunday and you could hadly move what with all the people there and we were constantly being pushed along in a crowd of other visitors. Added to this did not think much of Kandy so all in all not a great trip, especially as it took up a whole day due to the usual slowness of going anywhere in Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were in and out before we knew, and crowds of people were being yelled at by some temple staff to move faster. This was perhaps because we went on the day of "thai pongal" which is a festival. But I didn't see anything spectacular or mind-boggling while in there. And the price of 500 rupees to enter a temple does not make sense at any level. I stayed in Kandy to visit this temple, and later on felt that I need to have been straight to my next destination in Sri Lanka as this visit wasn't up to the expectations. And the fee of Rupees 500 applies if you're a citizen of one of the SAARC countries. It will be double that rate if you're from some other country, and the locals get to enter at no cost. I feel that this is completely unjustified, at least given the fact that this is supposed to be a place of worship. Never again.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is good historic temple and maintained well but i did not get peace of mind , which comes to you generally being in temple. The paintings at the entry and inside the temple is mesmerizing. The Stone carvings on the pillars were beautiful and you will see lotus carved in gold at the ceiling . But It was very crowded and people will stare at you like anything. I don't want to disappoint you but it was way below my expectations.The place where tooth was kept was so much noisy and crowded, so 'll not get time/place to prey. It is situated beside Kandy lake and its good to have walk around lake in evening as sun shines to you through water.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We spent an hour and a half here a few weeks ago. The location is nice and central to Kandy and cant be missed as Kandy is quite a small city by European standards. Dont forget to wear long shorts past your knee otherwise you will have to buy a sarong al a Beckham to wear while you are inside. The temple is a nice building, but the main thing to see is the relic. You cannot actually see the tooth, but you can see one of the seven gold containers that it is in. There are many people praying at its location and a line of peopl ewalking past the relic in close formation, so you will only get 30 seconds maximum to take a look and a photo.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was interesting to see the Buddhist pilgrims, en masse, bringing babies here to be blessed. However, the whole thing just reminded me of how much wealth organized religion sucks from the poor believers. This was highlighted by the large lunch served to a group of monks on a platform while the pilgrims watched. But for Buddhists this is a very special place indeed.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This was our second visit to the Temple of the Tooth - our first was ten years ago - and the 9.30am poya has not changed at all. The Temple of the Tooth is  very sacred, and there is nothing more silencing, than to be drawn into what this place means than to stand beside a monk. Upstairs new mothers waited for the ceremony to end to move forward with their babies to be blessed. The ceremony is a mix of sound (trumpets, drums) and smell ( incense) and drama (walking around th e temple three times, going in and out of the central room with offerings etc.) most tourists go to to the evening ceremony but the morning is equally as powerful an experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the tooth or more commonly known amongst the local Sri Lankans as Dalada Maligawa is believed to house a tooth of the Lord Buddha. It is a beautiful temple with ornate decor and historical paintings and murals mostly relating to Kandy Era. The 'poojawa' takes place three times a day and you will notice a very long queue waiting to offer flowers. The Tooth is not visible but can see the chamber it is housed during the poojawa times. The temple is full of history and there is a museum in the premises which is well worth visiting. If you get on to the tower you can see the beautiful surroundings and it overlooks the Kandy Lake. The garden outside is well kept and can walk around and there are mini temples you  can visit. There is a entrance fee for tourists but not expensive and if you are in Kandy this is well worth a visit. The only set back is there is no wheel chair access to the temple. This may be because you are not expected to sit on chairs within the premises as all the prayers are said sitting down on the floor. Please note to be dressed appropriately when you are visiting the temple. i.e. No shorts,minis or sleeveless tops

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: To be fair we went in the middle of a torrential rain storm which clouded our views somewhat. It is interesting and a 'must do' in Kandy so we weren't sorry we went but a bit like cathedrals in Europe once you've seen a number ..... The paintings on the entrance corridor and the shrine are spectacular. One point to note is the place has lots of monkeys, like many temples, and these ones smell!! They also wee and poo on the floor where you are walking in bare feet - delightful!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: A real temple housing centuries of history! A must-see!! It was really crowded, a mixture of cultures and expectations... what i liked the most was that in the crowds though a lot, tourists were a minority compared with nationals. Wasn't able to see the tooth itself, got just a glimpse to the chamber in which it rests but no way to get near. There was a looooooong line waiting with flowers offerings, clothes for the monks, etc, etc. I strongly recommend to go with a well prepared guide- able to open the mysteries of the temple and its contents without hesitating after your questions.

review_text: My main reason for coming to Kandy was to visit this temple. Located near the Kandy lake, the best time to visit is either in the morning or late evening, when it is all lit up. There is no entry fee, but there are flower sellers outside & I gladly bought some to offer inside. The main shrine where flowers are offered is upstairs, and it can get quite busy at ceremony time. I took my time wandering around & taking note of all the beautiful architecture. This temple was apparently attacked several times by terrorists at the height of the terrorism problem in Sri Lanka, and each time it was reconstructed. This is one of the most holy shrines for Buddhists. One point to keep in consideration is to dress modestly..this is after all a temple.;) There is a sign outside the temple requesting that & most visitors seem to adhere to that;) Beautiful temple & worth an hour of your time if you are in Kandy or passing through;)

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the Tooth also known as Sri Dalanda Maligawa (in Sinhalese, Sri Lankan Local Language), is the most precious place for Buddhists in all around the world. Temple of the Tooth one of the very few places where you can find Lord Buddha's Tooth Relics. This is a very ancient place and you should never miss this place if you visit Kandy. Please make sure you wear proper cloths when you are visiting since this is a very sacred place. You will get amazed by the feeling you will get and the atmosphere inside. It will be great if you can visit in the evening since the entire palace will be brightened up by lights... There are some official tour guides inside who can provide you valuable information about the palace.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: One of the best Buddha temple we got to visit on our trip. We were right on time for the ceremony and it was divine everywhere. The temple is usually crowded as it is the most sacred place in Kandy. Locals are allowed to get closer to the shrine. Tourists should keep in mind that it is a sacred temple. please do not wear shorts, slippers are not allowed, do not go drunk, please give all the due respect just like how you would give to the God you believe. do not pose in front of Buddha. We loved the place.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Definitely worth a stop for anyone who likes temples. The shrine housing the tooth is ornate and interesting to study. You can watch monkeys playing on the temple while you walk the grounds. There is also a free audio tour included so get the player at the entrance. The cd is actually in the ticket packet they issue you at the gate. Be sure to keep the packet and the receipt because the guards will collect the register receipt and tear off the ticket in the packet before letting you in. You will also need to check your shoes. A donation for that service is not required but is strongly suggested by the men working the counter.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I read so much about this temple. It was nice worth the trip. The new chamber they created in the back has a good story about the temple being made and where the tooth came from. Without reading it I may have not enjoyed the experience as much as I did. Try to avoid the evening prayer time. You have to wait in long queues and the time you get in front of the tooth shrine is barely few seconds with hoards of people waiting behind you. We went at 6:00 pm so avoid it during the evening times as well. Try going during the day. Overall nice atmosphere and worth the trip.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This really seemed like a genuine working temple when we visited. We purchased flowers like everyone else seemed to be doing and then joined the procession through the temple and were treated with great enthusiasm by the local worshippers - it was so interesting to feel part of the ceremony. It would have been nice if there were more info provided especially as they do charge a fair bit to enter - even a photocopy info sheet would be nice.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It's one of the most sacred places in Sri Lanka. The temple is unfortunately not in its original condition (due to the terrorist attack); nevertheless, it's beautiful, and the exhibitions inside are worth taking a longer look. Also, the scenery around the temple is beautiful, in particular at dusk.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This place is amazing - we had a guide who helped us to negotiate the packed queuing crowds to see the inner sanctum and then on to tour the complex. Wonderful art on the walls and standing statues - great stories about what the building has seen and still means and as a final sentimental treat, a visit to an exhibition explaining the life of probably the most famous of the temple elephants, Rajah. Don't miss this if you are in Kandi - do go with someone who knows about it all and can tell you all its stories.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Just a little background knowledge will make your visit more interesting. The tooth temple is an absolute must and forearmed with a few facts, an enigmatic and fascinating destination awaits you. The tooth was brought to Anuradhapura by princess Hemamali and after some adventures eventually ended up in Kandy. It is important to realize that possession of the tooth signifies the right to rule. Don't think of the tooth as a bit of nonsense, it has been carbon dated and it's journey chronicled. A great way and convenient way is to visit the Kandy cultural show and visit the temple after, which is almost next door. You will pass through security and then on to a ticket booth where you must leave your shoes. At around 6.30 the small doors to the main shrine will be opened for the viewing of the casket of the tooth. You must get in the left hand queue if you want to get real close. The smart alecs who rush pass one the right side will see little. Try not to be overwhelmed by the number of visitors and observe the many groups of villagers who have travelled from all over Sri Lanka to pay homage. The manic drummers add to the overall atmosphere. The actual temple is part of the grounds of the royal palace so the king could keep an eye on his power token. After take a tuk tuk to the Almost Chilled cafe for a nice meal with a view. Enjoy, Pedroofpobla

review_text: If you are religious, it is a great place to visit and see the tooth relic...and visit the vel bodhiya if you can as well. (I missed that the last time I came here.) You can partake of the 'kiri pooja' at 5am if you are an early riser..not sure if that happens everyday or just on Saturdays. If you are not religious....The architecture and craftsmanship in this old palace that is now the temple of the tooth relic, is just simply gorgeous. review_text: It's the most important Buddhist temple, nice to see, but I was not impressed. There's a museum on site with lots of Buddhist jewellery, different tools and objects and history of the temple and the tooth, and that was more interesting for me then the actual tooth relic.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the Sacred tooth relic of the Buddha ($7.7 pp).  This is the most important relic and temple in Sri Lanka to Buddha followers (nice Buddha temple, but the tooth relic is in a pagoda kept in a locked room so you don't see it.).  Overall just OK for a 1/2 hour stop.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Beautiful buildings, one room more impressive than the other. They open the actual relic around 6.30 in the evening apparently but we were there before, to avoid being caught in the crowds. Tells the story of the Buddha whose tooth is kept in the temple, and the history of the buildings itself. Behind it is the museum of International Buddhism, which is also worth a visit. A must-do in Kandy!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The sacred tooth of the Buddha is housed here, and at any given point the place is always crowded with locals and tourists alike .. if you are into buddhism and practising this place will be of great value to you .. The grounds are green with a lovely view of the temple in the distance .. Admittedly you might just enjoying sitting outside watching crowds of people going past to pay respects .. The inner is quite dark adding to the sacred and religious atmosphere, while people pray and occasionally chanting .. 2 floors of a museum with photos to one side depicts various stages of history but beware the staff here .. One guy rudely came up yelling NO PHOTOS ALLOWED before my guide told him I was a tourist wherein he timidly apologised and walked away .. Look up towards the ceiling for some artificats as well The tooth relic itself is placed at another end of the building which is really crowded going up and even more crowded as people seat themselves praying at the relic so you need to move fast keeping going with the flow of people .. You wont really get a close look and if taking a photo hold it above your head to get a good shot if you can zoom in enough .. Just outside is another small museum with a few ancients paintings and stone structures .. Am not sure what the importance of this really is, but its only another few mins additional Keep in mind dress code, no shorts, slippers or sleeveless .. you will have to check in your footwear at the entrance anyway and go in barefoot but your clothing will probably get you stopped at the door and proper attire will be rented out .. Anything for a buck .. Once you are outside the typical tourist venders are loafing around .. Have an ice cream its pretty delicious and needed after the hot crowded interior Definitely worth the look though, to understand the level of loyalty to religion and local belief

review_text: We engaged a guide once inside. If you are Australian and seen the Peter Kuruvita cooking show where he goes to Kandy's temple of the tooth well you may be in for a different experience.  When the tooth relic is to be shown (three times a day) there is much praying and a huge amount of noise.  Crowds gather in to see the relic and it is not the calm as it was on the show (obviously not one of these times). A trip to Kandy is incomplete without visiting the temple so go and be happy.  Because as our guide says "if you are happy, I am happy"

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple of tooth is a good visit and it is better done when the open the doors of the temple where the tooth is kept which is generally in the morning. However the rush can get a little daunting as devotees flock to catch a sight of the holy tooth, be prepared for it.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a tip worth passing along: We enjoyed lunch in Kandy before visiting the temple. My husband enjoyed a cold beer to wash down his deviled fish. As we were going through security for the temple, the guard got quite aggressive in frisking my husband, really patting him down!  Then, he made my husband open his mouth and breathe on him only to turn him away as he could detect beer on his breath.  Seriously, my husband was perfectly sober and we were a family all together.  It was quite humiliating though we had a good laugh after the fact.  When we mentioned this incident to the owner of our B&B, he found it preposterous. Regardless, be certain to pop a breath mint if you enjoyed a cold brew before your visit.  You never know if an overzealous guard may want to make an example out of you! We returned to the temple the following day and enjoyed the visit.  Be sure to see the tusker museum as well as the old royal palace.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were taken here by our guide on our whistle-stop tour of southern Sri Lanka and I am so glad we didn't miss it. Despite it being so busy, there was order and no-one was pushing and shoving - everyone was waiting their turn to make their offerings.  It was a magical and spiritual place, highly ornate, serene and very beautiful.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went to Kandy by train, sitting in a reserved seat in the observation car. Train ride itself was exciting enjoying the panoramic views of the country side and the mountains views of the hill country. Express train is punctual, cheap and take only 2 hours. We have heard so much of the Sri Dalada Maligawa and it's historic importance to the rulers of the country. Whole temple complex sits magnificiently by the shores of the Kandy Lake displaying it's magnificient architecture. There is a Pooja time early in the morning and then again in the evening, These times are very crowded but worth the experience of watching the colourful drummers and dancers performing though the drumming noise may linger in your ears for some time. Devotees gather around the replica of the tooth on display ( acual tooth is open to display only once a year) and thet make offerings. If you wish to see the beautiful statues and paintings it is best to pick another visit during the day. Visit gives you a calmness and respect for the splendour of the palace temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: After visiting the Tooth Relic for morning puja I cannot see why this attraction is rated so highly. We stood down below and watched a silver door open to let the cleaners in, and "listened" (could you avoid it?) to a small band playing and banging drums. The tour groups then seemed to form a long line to file in front of a small window for a brief view of a large obscenely ornate casket that allegedly contains a tooth. Then we joined more queues to file through two other chambers. The octagonal room is of interest for all the old books - but you can't stop walking long enough to have a good view. I like visiting temples, and normally find Buddhist shrines calm and meditative places. The Tooth temple is neither of these things, nor is it particularly old. As to the claim that it is central to the Buddhist tradition I would question that - as I could not see any Buddhist values in the relic worship that goes on.  Add to that there is the issue of the price of admission for foreigners....all seems decidedly commercial to me. So unless you believe in the powers of relics like old teeth - I'd walk round the outside and find a quiet cave temple elsewhere to discover the true depth of Buddhism.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The most sacred temple of Buddhists in Sri lanka is this temple which holds the tooth relic of Lord Buddha. The majority population in Sri lanka follows Buddhism and this temple is their most sacred temple. It is believed from ancient times that always the kind of the nation who govern the country had access to the tooth relic, had its blessings and he or she carefully looked after it with all security measures taken to safe guard it. Even during the periods of colonization by the Englishmen, priority had been given for the security of sacred temple. It has got a long history since the 17th century . Its architecture, its carvings, the museum attached to it and its cultural events such as rituals and the Asala perahera the annual pageant are all connected to it. The special rituals conducted as homage to the tooth relic of lord Buddha, persons connected to these rituals are all taking a unique manner. Any person visiting Kandy should visit the temple without fail to get an idea of the above details.

review_text: When you arrive you have to remove and leave your shoes. Bear in mind you'll be shoeless until you come back to get them after you've toured everything (could be an hour or more). Lots of pilgrims (this site is one of the most sacred to Buddhists worldwide) and if you don't want to get that close you can stand in the back and still see the golden casket. review_text: Cost: Rs1300. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a beautiful temple and is a must visit place if you are in and around Kandy. There is a lot of history associated with place and the place has been well restored after the bombing by terrorist. It is a great cultural experience and takes you back in history. The place is very clean and has been maintained very well and the amount charged for tourist for entering the premises is well justified. The temple is right at the centre of Kandy city and hence, it is very easily accessible and you do not have to travel for a long to visit the temple. This place also holds ancient Buddhist scriptures and it was fascinating to be able to see them and was great learning experience.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Its currently LKR1000 rupees for tourists. This may seem expensive for a religious site, but I assure you its a fraction of the entry fees you will be asked to pay elsewhere! If you don't like crowds, avoid the prayer times when the temple is really full. We went mid afternoon. The downside is that the prayer times can be the most interesting, with music and chanting, so it depends - crowds and music vs no crowds but maybe less of an overall experience. And you do NOT have to make donations of either money or flowers. Its purely voluntary (and anyway the temple itself does not benefit from the sale of the flowers, they are independent vendors for the most part). Tell anyone pressuring you to give that you already paid your entry fee! I would recommend a guide, although you can find your way around alone.  It does not surprise me, however, that I see some people felt ripped off, since I gather the quality of guiding is not always good, and always ask the price in advance. Our guide was really helpful in contextualising the story of how the Buddha's tooth was rescued from the crematorial ashes and smuggled to Sri Lanka for safekeeping in the hair of the princess! All in all, recommended.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It was one of the main sights to visit in kandy, I was looking forward to going there, my husband and I went to see the cultural show, and then the temple of tooth after, once we got there, it was dark, and the lights were amazing, the building looked really nice, the colors and paintings were interesting, however, we had to take off our shoes and walk inside, which I didn't mind, up until we left the place from an exit door, where we had to walk on sand and pebbles and broken things, I didn't feel comfortable, and was not used to this, so it was a bi painful for me, ( note, that it only occurs when u leave the building). They had a very loud drumming going on inside, which bothered my husband and I, only because we had a headache from the cultural show we were in right before our visit to the temple of tooth, It is amazing, how everyone gathers at that time, waiting for that moment where their monk opens the doors to the tooth, and everyone starts their prayers, giving out flowers and money, It's interesting to learn more about the culture, and how they believe it brings them rain if they shake the tooth in a dry season ( 3-4 months of no rain).

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Right in the middle of Kandy it is hard to miss the Temple of the Tooth.  They have done a great job of restoring it after the terrorist attack and the grounds around it are beautiful.  The Temple itself is a little smaller than I expected but no less interesting of a cultural experience.  A really cool side area is the preserved elephant that was a HUGE tusker, very cool old pictures.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited the Temple of the Tooth in September and I have to admit it was one of the highlights of our visit to Sri Lanka. The history of this temple is truly amazing and is very interesting. I could of walked around it all day. The details in the carvings and Budhas are worth the entrance fee alone. I would advise people to take socks with them though as you hand your shoes in and the grounds are quite big and the floor was very hot. We were lucky enough to have a guide as part of our tour who had amazing knowledge of the traditions and of what to do or not do i.e no photos posing in front of Budha as it is very disrespectful. (feel free to take photos of everything else). Not to be missed!!

review_text: I'm not going to lie I found it strange visiting a temple, watching the tour guides tour, snapping photo's of this that and the other, whilst surrounded by buddhists praying and chanting and going about their faithful practices. I was lead by a stranger into one particular temple where people were praying to a reclining buddha and a collection was being taken and, honestly this made me feel uncomfortable. I can't pretend to pray to a god or buddha I don't believe in, and I can't give money to support the religion either. So I froze like an idiot and very wuietly slipped out. The very nice helpful guy that lead me there just looked offended and walked off. And I can't blame him really if he's buddhist! This is an active place of worship and I felt utterly intrusive and invasive traipsing through with my camera. In addition to this the tie-dye wrap-around skirt I was made to wear (there's a no-knees rule) added no-end to me uncomfortable feeling but was taken with a healthy dose of humour! And no - you don't get to see THOSE photos! All in all it was a beautiful site the temple was staggeringly ornate and beautifully decorated! Just maybe try to find a quiet time to visit!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple tooth in kandy very good attraction for locals and tourists. This is very much sacred place for Buddhist people. According to history, the tooth was taken from the Buddha as he lay on his funeral pyre. It was smuggled to Sri Lanka in 313 AD, hidden in the hair of Princess Hemamali who fled the Hindu armies besieging her father's kingdom in India. It immediately became an object of great reverence and was enshrined in a series of nested jeweled reliquaries. The tooth was brought out for special occasions and paraded on the backs of elephants, which are sacred to the Buddha. Where it survived numerous attempts to capture and destroy it. When the capital was moved to Kandy, the tooth was taken to the new city and placed in temples built to honor it. The temple was originally built under Kandyan kings between 1687 and 1707, but later severely damaged during the 18th-century colonial wars against the Portugese and Dutch. After the wars, the original wooden structures were restored in stone. In January 1998 Hindu Tamil separatists bombed the temple, damaging its facade and roof. Restoration began immediately afterward. Courtesy of daladamaligawa

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Foreign tourists are vastly outnumbered here by locals (or non-local Sri Lankans) crowding in to get a quick sight of the reliquary.  The experience of jostling with the worshippers is the most memorable part of the experience. In terms of the actual sights on display, it's a bit overpriced for foreigners at R1000 (about US$7.50), which of course is far more than the locals pay.  Compared to other sights in Sri Lanka, the temple isn't particularly impressive--people come for the Buddha relic.  The ticket also gets you in the temple museum, which has lots of artifacts from the last few hundred years, most of which were offerings to the Buddha, some from distinguished supplicants. A bit of warning--they take the dress code seriously.  You'll be turned away at the entrance to the grounds (nowhere near the temple) with bare shoulders or knees, unlike many other sights in Sri Lanka which are not nearly so strict.  You might also be frisked on entrance to the grounds (I was, my wife wasn't).  Don't forget to pick up the free audioguide with your ticket -- I would tell you how it was, but I *did* forget!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is considered the most sacred buddhist temple in Sri Lanka. Visit in the morning (before 9am) as there is a daily ceremony at 9:30 where offerings of food are brought in. Also, every Wed, the ceremony includes bathing the relic (water is poured over a mirror reflecting the relic). People line up to get some of the water as it is considred blessed. It gets very crowded but worth the visit at that time. A lot of the ceremony is on the ground floor but on the first floor, a window to the room where the relic is held is opened for people to catch a glimpse of the casket in which the relic is held.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had already seen several Buddist sites but the experience of The Temple of the Tooth really does reinforce the importance of this faith to the Sri Lankan people. We arrived in time to witness the "rush hour" of devotees before the tooth casket was closed from view and, thanks to our guide, could fully appreciate the importance of this place. The building is interesting and it is a very pleasant setting in the centre of Kandy. If you are in Kandy this is a must-see attraction.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is surrounded by enclosures full of tethered elephants which form the bulk (oops) of the annual Perahara parade; a spectacular and enjoyable festival through the streets of Kandy in July/August. The tooth in question purports to be one of the Buddha's as rescued from his ashes by a devotee. The inner tooth temple itself is a beautifully decorated structure with some very attractive decorative woodwork and painting. Inside you may catch a glimpse also of the mahouts repairing their elephant adornments with soldering irons & a bit of electrical skill! Seperate buildings in the enclosure house a museum and the stuffed form of Raja - one of the favoured & famous old elephants.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Visited the temple during Perahera (religious elephant procession period) so the temple was very busy. About 15 elephants were being kept in yards adjacent to the Temple. I am told that this is the most important temple for Buddhists in Sri Lanka as they believe that the "Tooth" is from Buddha's jaw, so all his words and philosophy has passed it. As with all Temples hats and shoes must be removed and appropriate clothing worn. There is a stall before entering the Temple where foreigners can store their shoes for a small donation. The temple was bombed by the Tamil Tigers so there is a level of police security. The visit was worthwhile and there are several rooms to visit. Visitor numbers are high as many followers will be there. Mornings are less busy than the afternoon.

review_text: Ticket priced at LKR1000. This temple is the major attraction in Kandy but I personally view the place not worth visiting. At the entrance strongly guarded with security guards. We placed the lotus flowers that we brought but the temple priest, not happy with us not putting money in the pot, started to chase us away. We noted that those putting money were  allowed to view a little longer than those who DID NOT. Then, we went out of the temple with an heavy heart. There the shoe rack fella gave us our shoes and at the same time SCOLDED US for not giving him tips. TIPS we pay for good service.  Then what the TICKET is for? Better save the money for a nice Ayurveda massage.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Whole of Sri Lanka is amazing. From Negombo, just north of Colombo, to Yala National Park and from Colombo to the east. Negombo Lagoon by boat is something to do when you want to cool down. Kandy had other attractions for me other than the Temple of the Tooth, namely cricket. The Temple is a must, but get yourself a good guide. Take a day to go to The Sigiriya Rock Fortress, have a good head for heights and get there early in the day to avoid the heat. Wear good walking shoe's, a lot of climbing to do.Take another couple of day's to see the 12th century Capital of Polonnaruwa, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The statues of the Buddha are worth the trip alone. Another few day's to visit Yala National Park, taking in Galle on the way. If you are lucky as my partner Ola and I were, you may see the rare Sri Lankan Leopard. If you go to Sri Lanka take your life in your hands a take a tuk tuk ride somewhere, just for the experience. Somewhere to have a drink and bite to eat in Colombo is The Cricket Club Cafe. If you can get to Negombo, a must for food is a newish place Ola and I found, TUSKERS. It is owned and run by a jolly Belgian and his Sri Lankan wife. She train in Paris, so with her and his background you get Sri Lankan /Western food in large portions at very reasonable prices. All-in-all an amazing place with wonderful people.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you are planning a trip to Kandy from a resort area, there are some things you need to be aware of. Firstly, although Buddhists hold all life to be sacred, this does not include yours. We took 6 minibus rides & I have not recovered 2 weeks later. The roads are poor but that does not excuse suicidal behaviour by your driver & most other road users. Our worst experience of many was to have the driver put his vehicle through a gap that was too small & ending up in the mud at the side of the road. Brakes, gears, accelerator and steering seem to be operated more or less at random. What drivers do not seem to appreciate is that all their antics such as overtaking in a non-existant middle lane will save only a few seconds, while giving you a seriously bad time. Start as you mean to go on & tell the driver what you expect. You are paying enough money to be delivered safe & sound. The actual Temple is loud, hot & chaotic. All part of the charm, you may feel. My wife was fairly upset by having begging bowls literally thrust under her nose at every turn, despite having paid a hefty entrance fee. They even ransom your shoes! You may be lucky & see the container in which the tooth is kept. Or maybe not, it appears to be at the whim of the monk in charge. The building itself is very interesting, being beautifully decorated & of course you are surrounded by history going back some 2,300 years. I forgot to mention, they will make you put on all the clothes you possess, despite the 30+ hot. I couldn't help but notice that no-one stops the locals from going in suitably dressed. Give the Pinawalla elephant detention centre a miss unless you actively dislike animals. It is distressing in too many ways.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited this temple an hour before the ceremony and waited for the ceremony after a guided visit of the temple.  This temple has an amazing history and the guided tour was great. IMO, this is #1 of the places to visit in Sri Lanka. It was an amazing experience of visiting this holy place. We hired a tour guide Rs.500.The guide also explained the history of the arrival of the tooth to this location and about every painting, building and the relics in the temple. Also, the postures of the Buddha. each posture had a meaning.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Do visit only on a full moon day, known as Poya day in Sri Lanka, and you would thank me for it. Though Temple of Tooth, obviously, is famous for the "Tooth Relic of Buddha" enclosed in a casket, the entire experience could be something great if you get to witness the "Perahera". We  reached the temple on a full moon day around 5 pm. There was some rush to get inside and see the casket. Not understanding why this is happening, we came out of the main temple building. On our way out, we saw an Elephant completely decorated and ready to carry a replica of the casket! Wow! we thought and walked outside the temple complex. Little did we know that an amazing treat was awaiting outside. More Elephants joined the procession, known as Perahera, and dancers joined in too! To our surprise we were standing right next to the performing crowd and it was great to witness the Perahera from such close quarters!! Awesome place to visit in the evening and check out the decorations in the night!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We don't see this many people together at home unless it's a concert or rugby game. I can't say how much this added to my new love affair with Sri Lanka. I was totally immersed in the culture, warmth and love during this magical visit. The heady heat, the throng of the music, the murmuring of the people as they line up with gifts, flowers and young and old to get an opportunity to view the tooth. To just 'be' in the moment and value and respect the culture of others. I have grown as a person and realize that I have more than I need. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: There is a great deal to recommend Sri Lanka and Kandy is one of its nicer towns. However, the Temple of the Tooth did not rate as highy on the Sri Lanka hit parade as we expected and any of the ancient sites further north offer more in terms of art and architecture. The main problem for us was the crowding. As some other posters have noted, there are always long queues and you never get more than a glimpse of the star attraction, the tooth. It is like going out to the airport to see a famous rock star and all you get is one brief glimpse before they step off into a taxi and are whisked away. This place might be one of the most famous Buddhist pilgrimage sites, but it has just too much of a show biz feel to it these days and you will wish it was a more restful experience.

review_text: Went here during Vesak - had a brilliant guide Dinesh Duminda (adroit999@gmail.com) who took us around the Temple and explained everything to us. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Now a buddist temple this was originally a palace built by a king of Kandy. It is impressive on either count. To get the best out of a visit hire a local guide who can tell you about the history of the place in far more detail than you can get just by walking around on your own. The guide who approached us was friendly and helpfull, not too pushy and when asked how much his service was said "between 1000-3000 SLR, it's up to you" We thought he was very good and were happy to give him 2500 SLR. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The best time to visit the temple is at the night ritual. The entry tax included also a CD about Kandy and the Temple; very nice introduction in the world of Lord Budha. The outside simplicity of the buildings which form the temple is exceeded by the beautiful interiors decorated with inlaid woods,ivory and lacquer. The guide explained me in datail the life of Lord Budha and the history of the temple. I was impressed by the discipline of the faithful standing in line to get a glimpse at the shrine;all dressed in immaculate white, in perfect silence, offering flowers ... A dignified celebration which emanate a great peace. A lesson of respect and simplicity which invites you to meditation. I was impressed also by the library of the temple. Definitely a place you should visit in Sri Lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I arrived in the morning shortly after it opened.  I was immediately accosted by two wannabe tour guides, but managed to shake them of and proceed to purchase my ticket, then deposit my shoes at the rack (more on that later).  Inside is quite interesting.  You make your way upstairs to see the actual tooth relic, housed in an interesting wooden temple/shrine.  Then you make your way past the courtyard to several statues of the Buddha, and accompanying depictions of how the tooth relic came to be.  Finally, you can visit a museum that is honestly, kind of a let down.  There are a few interesting artifacts, but the lack of overall structure/plan to the museum (it's more like haphazardly arranged items), and the extreme focus on the bombing that took place there kind of makes the museum worth your time only if you have an extra 20-30 minutes to kill. So the actual tooth relic chamber itself is very ordinary - you simply shuffle past, maybe take a photo, and move on.  At the exit, I went to retrieve my shoes, only to be accosted for the tip.  I pointed to the sign (see photo), but the attendant was insistent on getting some sort of tip.  That experience itself, pegged the attraction down 2 notches for me.  After days in Sri Lanka, I had lost all my patience for touts and scams - yes I get it - the economy etc etc etc - but I have visited dozens of countries, and have never had to feel the aggressiveness of guys asking for money more so than in South Asia.  Needless to say, I slipped the guy a small amount of change, which seemed to annoy him since he wanted a heftier tip.  Oh well...

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This is a large temple complex with several different sections. Some were closed off during our visit, so we did not see everything. There is a ceremony performed a couple of times a day, where food offerings are brought to a central sealed room and taken inside to (I think) be consumed by senior monks. We waited about 30minutes for this, but were seriously underwhelmed by the "pomp" attached to it. We then joined a tide of humanity as it swept us all upstairs to pass by a small window opening into a room in which (I think) the sacred relic of Buddha's tooth is held. This was quite an interesting experience, with all the local devotees carrying offerings (mainly of beautiful flowers). However avoid if claustrophobic as it is very congested - I saw one local faint. Most disappointingly, as you come level with the window into the relic room you have no time to peer inside before the tide moves you on again. It must surely be even more frustrating for the worshippers. If you intend going I would recommend that you do some reading first, so that you have a better understanding of the different sections, and of the symbolism, if you want to get the most out of it. Note also that they are particularly strict about clothing here (arms, shoulders, upper legs covered). There is a stall where western vistors remove and leave their shoes.

review_text: On any given day, perhaps after a few days by the beach, why not go on a trip and visit The Temple of the Tooth in Kandy. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth in Kandy is really amazing. Upon entrance, you would see the temple structure showing the "Buddhist Architecture"...inside you will be amazed with the Buddhist painting on the walls and ceiling.... the entire temple has a distinct ambiance... allowing you to appreciate Buddhist culture and religion (way of life). location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were here the day after the full moon day in February so every man and his dog were visiting.  It was super crowded but it just added to the atmosphere.  A lot of what was going on was beyond us but it was such a special place and amazing people watching to be had!  Everyone deep in meditation, praying and generally just being happy to be there.  The smells of flowers and incense, the noise from chanting and drums and the hustle and bustle of everyone trying to get a peek at the tooth - immense.  When we went past the tooth, we both had goosebumps, the place has an electric aura about it.  I will never forget it and would recommend.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple is magnificent, as is the museum but what I really want to draw to your attention is the train journey. One of the great travel bargains. The train leaves Colombo Fort Station at 0700 and arrives in Kandy at about 0940. The carriage/car you want is the 'Expo' carriage and today's was spotless, comfortable and easy. It serves a snack breakfast that was fine, it has free wireless, can and should be booked and paid for online, and I recommend you print 2 copies of the ticket as you have to hand them in at each end, super clean lavatories and the whole return trip costs R2000 which at the exchange rate is £10.00. Oh, and it has two plug sockets per pair of seats that take the UK 3 pin plug... The return journey leaves Kandy at 1500 and arrives back at about 1740. The views and scenery are great - well worth the train ride alone - but Kandy and environs is a lovely town and the temple magnificent. It costs R1000 for a foreigner to get in - for which as a ticket you get a mini DVD - you have to leave your shoes (free but I left. R50 tip) and there is dress code that requires shoulders to be covered and will not accept skimpy dresses and shorts and tops. Not surprising for such a sacred place. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Thanks to our excellent guide, we visited the Temple of the Tooth very early in the morning (6AM) on a special holiday (full-moon).  The experience was beyond memorable.  Because of the sacred nature of the site coinciding with the full-moon holiday, many, many Sri Lankan's were there.  They were almost all dressed entirely in white, carrying beautiful flower offerings, in reverent prayer throughout the site.  For many Sri Lankans, this Tooth Relic Temple is a pilgrimage site.  We were fortunate to be able to witness the opening of the door to the small room that houses the Tooth Relic casket.  It was incredibly moving.  The entire Audience Hall was amazing and well worth your time.  Also worth your time is a visit to the Raja Tusker Museum (on site), devoted to Sri Lanka's most famous elephant. You might want to consider bringing an old pair of socks to wear as you visit this site.  The site is large, and unless your feet are used to walking barefoot, you'll appreciate the padding!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have to admit, I am not a fan of Buddhist temples, the garish colors, the endless identical Buddha statues are not my thing. This temple, however is easier on the eyes. Built in typical Kandyan style (no idea why it's calledd that, when earlier capital cities have the same architecture), it is worth visiting. As this is one of the most sacred sites of Buddhism (as I was told), expect really large crowds. Especially if you want to see the golden box that houses the sacred tooth (or its replica if you beleive some) - you'll have to stand in a long line.

review_text: The building and the monastery were really impressive in terms of architecture and serene from inside. review_text: We arrived at the Dalada Sri Maligawa in the early afternoon after driving for about 4 hours from Colombo. Security is still kinda tight even though the war with LLTE has been over. The story is the Buddha's tooth is secured in layer and layer of small pagodas which are encrusted with various precious gem stones, and it is stored in a bullet proof vault. There was a lot of devotees at the time we visited the temple, praying and paying respect to the tooth. A nice, quiet, serene place to visit.

One should also go to the top of the hill to enjoy the view of Kandy and to see the Temple from top.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had a mediocre tour guide. I have no idea how to find an excellent one. It'd be better with a better tour guide. It's just there. It's big. It's a big deal. But it's not one of those places that just fills you with awe. Sometimes, I walk into other people's cultural treasures and I can just feel the pulse and excitement and am awestruck by them. For example, the Taj Mahal, the Sistine Chapel, the palace in Bangkok, the temples in Siem Reap, Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, the ruins at Petra are all just as awesome as they are cracked up to be. This one is not. The people are kind and interested in you because you are foreign. It's just...not awesome. So, if you're in Kandy, obviously, you have to do this. If you aren't, don't sweat it; you aren't missing out. Dambulla, Sigiriya, the beaches are all far, far, far more interesting.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were told by our driver that the temple gets busy during weekends and full moons, so being a Thursday morning we didn't expect the temple to be so crowded. The tooth itself is apparently a very important budhist relic so it was packed out. There was quite a bit of pushing and shoving just to get to a massive queue in order to see the chamber holding a box which houses the tooth (you don't actually get to see the tooth). You can see the relic from a distance without queueing up and because it would have taken at least a few hours  to get through, we didnt bother. We watched as people were ushered past the doorway to get a brief glimpse of the chamber before being moved along and it was quite hot, stuffy and chaotic. It was not really the kind of peaceful temple experience we had in mind, felt more like a busy market place. The temple and grounds are pleasant, and strolling the grounds you can see a few elephants owned by the temple which was nice. The temple itself also had some very beautiful architectural details as well which are worth taking a closer look at.

Our 1st hustler in Sri Lanka.

review_text: The temple is very beautiful and it is visible that care is taken to maintain it and the surrounding grounds - being one of the most sacred Buddhist places in SL. There is a steep entrance fee for visitors which I personally do not think is worth it. Having already been to Anuradhapura, Sigiriya and Dambulla the temple itself was a disappointment. If this is your first experience with a Buddhist temple in SL then you may appreciate it more. Try to visit the temple during the morning or evening puja. Keep in mind that evenings can get very crowded during the puja time. The temple is located right at the lake and is a 15 minute walk from the bus/train station.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: It is not much different from other temples I've visited in Sri Lanka, the main difference is the steep entry fee for tourists (though you can avoid them when you have a residency visa). You can walk around the temple premises, which are very nice and avoid actually going into the temple and save yourself some money. Also be very careful if you should take a guide. Some of them only speak rudimentary English and sometimes tell you uninformed nonsense. You're better off with a good book.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is a spot that everyone will ask you to go in Kandy and its worth obliging. It’s a regal looking building from the outside and on the inside the design is splendid. It’s a brilliance mix of colours and one walks through the arched passageway into the main temple. Unfortunately when we went the sanctum was closed but nevertheless, the rest of the temple was open for us to see. It’s not a place that one should ideally like to see in a short visit. A couple of hours will always be worth it and well spent. There’s a lamp lighting room inside the temple and lamps are sold as one enters the temple. The lamps come in cardboard boxes complete with wicks and also oil to light the lamps.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: MAJESTIC AND TRANQUIL....WE WERE IN THE RIGHT PLACE AT THE RIGHT TIME!!! a medium sized crowd, very orderly and pious,no pushing touching or jostling... beautiful golden edifice and inner sanctums..superb carvings and an insane amount of ivory tusks in the temple and prayer halls.  Nice view of the Kandy lake as well. No entry to where the tooth is kept....one can only guess. fragrant offerings of lotus,jasmine , incense and fruits can be bought and made.We paid an entrance fee...AND AS IT IS IN MOST RELIGIOUS PLACES IN ASIA..no footwear allowed inside the premises..lucky for us the sun played hide and seek. lots of well cared for temple elephants.Spent about 2 hours here. Photos are allowed,

review_text: My husband and his cousin , who are from Bhutan and I went in the evening to have a blessing from the tooth relic.  We waited for quite a long time, but was very fortunate to see inside where the casket is that holds the relic of the Buddha's tooth. Very well worth the wait and felt a very blessed and strong energy from the place. If you are a Buddhist and plan to go to Sri Lanka , really go to see the Tooth Temple . it is a very special place.  The only problem with going to some of these places is you feel you get ripped off by the selling of tickets and money greediness.  It was quite sad to see that. All over the Buddhist places of Kandy, Pollanaruwa, Dambulla, Srgiriya, and Anuradhapura , you get chased by people trying to sell you things and anything you try to buy is way overpriced.  In fact all of Sri Lanka is way over priced for hotels and food.  Be aware that it is a very expensive place. But it is beautiful.

review_text: When we got out of our cars, my father hired a tour guide for us and my friend and I proceeded to enter the temple. We were allowed to take picture inside as long as we weren't posing in them. Raja, the stuffed elephant, who lived at the temple for over half a centry is preserved and displayed with many pictures from the annual Perahera where it carried the scared tooth relic. I think this place is a must to visit when visiting Kandy. [--]

review_text: I am not a great fan of temples and churches, but I have to admit that I really enjoyed this visit. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We arrived just in time for the drummers to start the devotion time,when the flowers are offered up to Buddah. This was a spectacle to behold and very interesting. We had a guide whoo spoke good english who clearly explained the history and beliefs involved. The Temple was very cool and a place of peace. A very interesting place to visit and very worth getting a good guide to show you the place and explain its history. You need to cover your shoulders and legs,shorts not acceptable.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of the Tooth is an important temple for Buddhists as is houses the world’s only, genuine remain of the Buddha.  It is easy to pick up a guide outside the entrance.  Alternatively, there is an audio tour available.  Shoes must be removed before entering any temple but some temples allow socks to be worn, which helps with the heat of the sun-baked ground.  It is considered deeply offensive to turn your back to Buddha, a natural position when having your photo taken!  Generally, it is appreciated if shoulders are covered in temples (some temples insist)

review_text: feel happy to reach the temple and make my wish. main attraction the tooth is in 1st floor. To view the tooth case.(you can't see content because it is covered in precious gifts and necklaces) it is locked behind closed door!  However, the door is open and close and open.... so don't immediately jump behind the queue, wait to take photos from the front of the door , after that you can join the long queue and view it in up front. Do prepare some donations..which is somehow expected by the few burly unfriendly guard? didn't see the monk when I did the turn, only saw the monk when taking the photo in the centre altar. personnally, I don't agree with the way the tooth box is kept behind closed door and I end up feeling they make money to let people see it closed up... :( that is not what buddha would have wanted. tips; flower need to be bought from outside the temple. Pass the gate and walk into the park to the building.. Get Entrance ticket, before main entrance need to remove shoe, as in all buddhist temple. So don't wear branded shoes to visit the temple!! ha ha. of course some temple has the shoe deposit counter which in this temple has 2 section, local and foreigner, no explanation why.  I bring along my small shoe bag and kept my shoes to carry along. I advice bring a lot of socks which to put on when walk around the temple.. you will know why when you step on hot sun burnt floor!! certain temple area is walking on rocks and sand in the cultural triangle ruins. overall. had a good religous experience for me.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is one of those "can't miss" sites while you're in Sri Lanka.  Its a site of such historical importance that you can feel the energy of the place while you're inside.  Beautiful architecture, paintings, stonework, and statues make this place incredibly memorable. If you're going, make sure you explore the whole grounds and not just the main temple.  There's much to see!  Also, you have to make sure you arrive when the window to see the Sacred Tooth Relic is open.  Even though you'll only get to walk by the window for a passing few seconds, you know you've seen something very special historically and spiritually.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The entire city of Kandy is fascinating. Places to visit in Kandy and its surrounding areas are: 1  Elephant Orphanage 2  The Botanical Gardens 3  The statue of Buddha atop the hill 4  The Kandy Lake 5  The Temple of the tooth The temple of the tooth is the prime attraction for a lot of visitors. The white structure with the stupas is a very peaceful place. A good time to visit is early in the morning, as the devotees visit the temple to gain blessings for the day before they go to the work places. Men and women with lovely white flowers in their hands make a bee-line to bow before the statue of Buddha. The silence itself as people pray in their hearts is a marvel to be experienced. Ask around for the timings to see the relic - Buddha's tooth. A word of caution about the proper attire for the Temple visit - Shorts are not allowed for both men & women.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth is an absolute must when travelling to Sri Lanka. It's one of the most sacred places in the world for buddhists. Our driver insisted that we'd go in the evening because then it's less crowded and you get (a little) more time to see the shrine. Apparently you can hire an audioguide (I saw the numbers indicated) but there is little information in the temple so to non-buddhist a lot of the objects and especially the rituals seems a bit strange. Whenever the shrine is on display there are drummers that fill the whole temple with loud music. Not really a relaxing visit when the jetlag starts to kick in...

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This cost us 2000 Rs for the two of us and it was not worth the money. The building is not that impressive and when you are inside there is very little to see. The tooth itself is locked away, but you can see a photograph of it! The same picture was in the lobby of our hotel. It's nice to see the locals praying in the temple, but we felt we were just getting in the way. If you want to see some impressive sites go to Sigiriya and Dambulla. I would highly recommend them!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We attended a service at the Temple of the Tooth on a Sunday evening in October 2011.  A local guide accompanied us, and explained the Temple, and the proceedings, to us throughout. It was a really beautiful experience, and quite spiritually uplifting.  We are very glad that we had the opportunity to witness this, and would love to return to see the Esala Perahera festival.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We missed the viewing time by 15mins and consequently missed seeing the library, the casket in which the tooth rests, and a shrine, all of which are open to the public at 3 times during the day. review_text: Temple is not so ancient like other Srilankn temple but is fascinating. Impressive building and strutcure, with a lot of gold and murble. location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Temple of tooth relic is located in Kandy, long a center of the Buddhist faith, the stunning 17th-century Temple of the Tooth (Sri Dalada Maligawa) is believed to house the left upper canine tooth of the Lord Buddha himself. This precious relic attracts white-clad pilgrims, bearing lotus blossoms and frangipani, every day. One full day is good enough to cover the entire Kandy, below places you can cover in one go:- 1) Temple of tooth relic temple (3 hours) 2) Kandy gemstone market (1 hr) 3) Cultural Dance (2 hours) 4) ayurveda messages (1 hrs) open till 10 pm, but you need to good negotiate well

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: On my recent visit to Kandy I got the opportunity to visit this amazing buddhist temple in the heart of the city. I went to the temple in the evening time for the prayers and it was a nice experience to be here. Was impressed by the massive structure and the setup. The statues and chambers in this temple were so well maintained. I did avoid the guides outside waiting to prey on you and was on my own that gave me time to enjoy each minute of my time here. I felt blessed. As it was prayer time and many people had come to worship, I could not get very close to the chamber where the sacred buddha relic, "the Buddha tooth" is kept but that was fine with me. I highly recommend a visit to this temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Impressive buildings and the historical significance of the temple both ancient and modern facts. Enlightening as one appreciates many of the images one sees of Sri Lanka and on various artifacts and arts such as batik cloth. Need a guide or a good guide book to explain details. Guide tends to rush the tour (not saying anything new here am I?) Lots of locals especially ner the time of openng the various sanctuaries.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We were taken to the Temple by our Sri Lanaka tour guide William, from Lanka Holidays he showed us around and explained the history to us. It is a lovely temple and the story of the Buddahs tooth is fascinating. It is good to have someone with you to tell you the all about this lovely temple. We recommend William and you can contact him for all your tours in Sri Lanka on [--]

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple of the tooth was a beautiful and fascinating place to visit, and given that it is also a working temple with people worshipping with toursits all around is very humbling. Please remember that this is a sacred place and as such your legs past the knees and shoulders should be covered. You have to go in barefoot, there is a little hut on the left before you enter where your shoes are looked after for a 25 rupee fee. Everywhere you look there is beautiful artwork-make sure that you look up ! The history of the temple of the tooth is told through a series of paintings in a beautifull anteroom decorated at ceiling hight with golden elephants The actual tooth is not seen as it is kept in a series of caskets the largest being bigger than a house , beautifully and ornately decorated. The history and beauty of this place is fscinating and a must see on your visit to sri lanka.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The Temple of the Tooth, or Sri Dalada Maligawa, is one of the most majestic and holy buildings of Sri Lanka. This temple is located on the north side of the Kandy Lake. It houses Sri Lanka’s most important relic the sacred tooth of the Buddha. How this tooth reached Kandy is a long story in itself. The gilded roof of the relic chamber attracts all the tourists as soon as they enter Kandy. Every year the Esala Perahera , which is the biggest festival of Sri Lanka, begins from this temple. You should dress in decent clothes that cover shoulders and legs and wear shoes that you can take off easily. Do not wear caps inside the temple. You have to take off your shoes outside the temple and pay a fee for their safekeeping. The temple is open 24/7. It is generally extremely crowded at all times but there is a huge crush at Pooja times. So try to avoid these 3 hours, 5:30-6:30 am, 9:30-10:30 am and 6:30-7:30 pm if you want to see everything. Tourists try to enter at Pooja  time because the relic chamber is open for worshippers at this time, but they don get to see the actual relic, all they see is the chamber and a gold chest. The Temple security is very tight. There is an entrance fee of LKR. 50 for locals, LKR. 100 for SAARC residents and LKR.500 for other foreign nationals.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I honestly thought Kandy was a bust compared to other areas of Sri Lanka. The Temple of the Tooth was the major draw and it was really just a place of worship for Buddhists.  Rip off entry fees, too, plus they even charge you a fee to hold onto your shoes!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: This Temple was well worth a visit, but I was dumbfounded by the two-tiered pricing, where a local/Sri Lankan pays 50 rupees, and "foreigners" pay 1,100 rupees. 20 x as much? It leaves you a bit shocked and appalled, however we needed to escape the horror that is the polluted hassled streets of Kandy, so we paid-up. It was amazing to look at inside, and as it was during the Perahera festivities, very busy, but well worth a visit, just a shame about the pricing.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Our driver brought us here just as it was getting dark and the Temple of the Tooth was gearing up for a big religious ceremony that night.  Forgive my ignorance of Buddhism, but that won't detract from what I want to say here.  We parked our car up and went straight into the Temple.... I was overwhelmed - completely overwhelmed.  That night was a heady mix of incredible architecture, lights, smells, people, music and a well-orchestrated religious ceremony that starts low-key and builds up as the night goes on.  This, dear reader, is what I went to Asia for.   Forget your tourist trap fake massages, worthless gems and screen printed batiks.....this was pukka happening, and I was there. I love anything ancient, so I was like a kid in a sweet shop at the Temple of the Tooth.  Its a temple in a temple - the original temple has had a much bigger temple complex built on top of it.  Its all impressive, but the extremely well preserved ancient temple is so stunning. Now, on to why I felt so uncomfortable being there.  I am torn between two ways of thinking here - one the one hand, I want to see and experience the Temple of the Tooth and all the spectacle that goes with it.  On the other hand though - I felt so sorry for the genuine Buddhist devotees that were there in their faith and who could hardly access the place for camera-toting tourists.  We shouldn't ever forget that its their faith and their temple - and a very important and sacred temple too. Like so many other tourists, I help clog the place up for the long suffering Buddhist faithful.  I took my place in a very slow moving queue to see, er, something.  I don't to this day know what I was actually in the queue for, but I saw a long line and joined it.  This is nothing but cultural greed at the expense of the true devotee, and we'd do well to remember that as tourists we are welcome guests but also mere onlookers to someone else's culture and beliefs. I did what I consider the Right Thing and quit the queue, giving my place over to a group of grateful locals who presumably will understand what they're looking at once they get to the front.  In return for giving up my place in the line, according to my Sri Lankan driver and guide, in the next life I'll be coming back as something further up the evolutionary chain than a cockroach.  Thats the theory anyway.....

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I feel the temple may be a victim of its own sucess. It is a fantastic temple - we have visited many temples across SE Asia and in terms of religious importance and ceremony this is one of the big hitters.  The building is very imposing from the outside, although more of a Castle than a temple.  Its pricey for a religious site - we understand it has to make money but it seems quite a steep charge. We visited at one of the times when the tooth is scheduled to be able to be viewed.  Our guide recommended this.  However the temple was absolutley packed.  There is a ceremony before the tooth is to be available for viewing - which consists of banging of drums and some kind of bugle playing.  There were some older folks to whom the crowd, heat and noise appeared to be too much.  The unseemly rugby scrum of a crows pushing around the temple virtually wipes out any spirituality.  We manages a glimpse of the container of the tooth which was, granted, gorgeous. However just outside Monks and Devotees light candles in the grounds - we left the crowds and stumbled upon this and it made up for the hullabaloo inside.  Very spiritual and more akin to the religious reverence we were far more accustoed to in temples.  We ventured back inside after the masses had returned to the coaches and given some quiet reflective time the temple does indeed have real spiritual charm. To summarise the building is awesome, just avoid peak times and explore a bit away from the main rooms and it's very rewarding.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went on Feb. 25th 2011 to visit the SRI Dalada Maligawa, knone as Temple of the  Buddha's Tooth and we've been lucky to watch at official cerimony which is daily held to offer foods and beverage to the relic. It is a amazing cerimony where the selected families are offering something as devotion the the relic placed at the second floor. As we entered there is some paint on the celing and the wall representing the festival of kandy back in XVI centrury and then you walk into to the patio at the grand floor where you can see the temple main door made up wood and covered by silver design. There are musicians that are playing with local drums and trumphet, a sweet music during all the event and other people dressing old costume carrying out, gifts and food. Watching around you'll see asthoninshing basement stones, representing elephants heads and the roof is complete in solid wood (tek); second floor is plenty of people praying and singing, in a kind of queing to go and see the small "golden core" where the Buddha's Tooth is inside but non visible. Then also the smell of caracteristic incense candles and spyce parfums will give a sensation of extraordinary feeling to stay in there. In the middle there is a children box for protecting them and their parents from the wave of visitors and tourist walking around to catchup picture or simple to watch inside and say ... I was there as well. Behind the temple there is a museum where you can watch at many Buddha statues offered by several country and a dezoen of picture representing Buddha life; at higher floor you can see also many tools back some centuries, costimes, maps, paper with first written caratters, pens and so on; attractive. Really oustanding visits absolutly NOT to MISS if you go to Kandy.

review_text: The Temple of the Tooth, or Sri Dalada Maligawa (Maligawa) in Sinhalese, is the most venerated Buddhist site in Sri Lanka and is said to house a tooth relic of the Lord Buddha. The original structure of today’s Maligawa was built by King Vira Narendra Sinha in the early 1700′s and has since had several additions by subsequent kings. I have documented my visit, including photography and history of the "Maligawa" on my blog: www.discovering-serendipity.com
