review_text: went to the temple of tooth late evening. was super crowded. was advised to go in the morning but could not do so. was beautiful and well lit and drummers playing. got to see a glimpse of the casket after waiting in the queue for almost 20 mins for just 5 seconds!! saw all the different areas and even the area which has the story explained in detail was nice and informative. helps if u have a guide or local person to explain the details and intricacies of the things else u would miss it. definitely worth a visit if u go to kandy

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We went on a thursday morning and it was very crowded with tourists and worshippers.  It was a good experience, my first time in a buddhist temple.  There was music by the drummers, it added to the spiritualness of the experience.  We also walked around the gardens of the temple.  Worth the visit.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: From the outside this doesn't look like a very impressive building, but once you are inside there is so much to see it is overwhelming! The carvings, ceilings, statues, decorations, floral offerings and general colourfulness of the people all contribute to a great experience here. Definitely a must!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We visited here in the early evening and it was manic! The volume of tourists and worshippers made this a very close encounter but somehow this did not put me off. It may have distracted me from being able to take in and understand all you are seeing but somehow seeing the temple during a busy prayer time actually added to the experience. You dont get much time to see the casket of the tooth relic - blink and you will miss it, but it is worth queing for as you listen to the music playing below and the cocophony of noise around you.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: I have been reading a book about Buddha and so I thought it would be really interesting to experience this, but I found it really quite a strange evening.  We rushed from the cultural evening we'd had, walked through 2 different security screening rooms where my boobs were blatantly grabbed and squeezed by one of the women!  I don't know what she was thinking I had hidden in my bra.  We then rushed to drop off our shoes, rushed into the temple, rushed up the stairs and there was loud chanting so we couldn't hear our guide tell us anything about what we were seeing, everything seemed excessively over decorated, gold leaf here and there, statues, shrines, just really over the top in decoration and expense having been spent on the building and interior.  We then queued to be whizzed and pushed past a tiny window, we moved so fast I couldn't even take in what we were supposed to see, then we rushed out of there into another room with another statue, down into a room with more statues and some interesting painted hangings which explained about the tooth relic.  I found that my understanding of what Buddhism had been about was clearly off the mark, as I had thought that it would have been a far more modest and less flash place, not an ornate tourist circus. I think if you are staying in Kandy it is one of the must do things...or so people say...but for me I found it like being pushed into a herd of sheep and then pushed, poked and prodded all the way around until we finally got outside and could catch our breath.  Not an experience I'd like to repeat and disappointing that my ideas of Buddhism were so out of line with seeing it being practiced.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: If you don't see Kandy or the Temple of the Tooth while you're in Sri Lanka its like going to pub without having a drink, why bother going if you're not going to see the most famous part? The Temple is quite impressive and the archutecture is beautiful. You go around bear foot which is really unique and sets the scene for you (a useful hint would be to take a rucksack and some light footwear - just take off your shoes and put them in your rucksack, if you don't you have to give them to these people who when you go back to get them expect a tip. We did this as everyone's gotta make a living, but seemed abit silly to me!) but the general myth of the tooth relic is a little deceiving as you don't actually get to see the tooth relic unless you go at specific times where you get 15 seconds to walk past it and you're frowned upon if you take pictures. You're basically going to a place of worship. Of course the legend of the Tooth isn't clear (not to be a geek about things lol) and there is rumours that the tooth at the temple is only a replicer so if you're looking to see something equivalent to the holy grail, you'll be dissapointed. However the Temple is well worth the visit with everything being very stunning and generally nice to have a look around. Please remember not to take a picture with your back to a buddah as they take that very seriously as it is a sign of disrespect. Would I go back to the Temple? Probably not. Once you've seen it you've seen it and thats that, but like I said, it's one of the most famous tourist attractions in Sri Lanka and you'd be a fool not to visit it, even just to say you've been there.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: usually i'm not that much interested in sights, but the temple of buddhas tooth you have to visit. after having entered the location i just sat down on the floor to feel the energy there. it's wonderful - go there and feel it. the only thing that made me sad was the information about the bomb attack that happened there - so do not forget to inform yourself about the history as well! visit it!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: The temple houses the most important Buddhist relic - a tooth of the Buddha. It is said that the tooth was snatched from the flames of the Buddha's funeral pyre and smuggled to Sri Lanka in the hair of a princess. It was first taken to Anuradhapura, and moved through the country on waves of history before it ended in Kandy. The tooth shrine receives many worshippers and tourists. During pujas the heavily guarded room housing the tooth is open to devotees and tourists.  The tooth is kept in a gold casket shaped like a dagoba.  You don't actually see the tooth.  Remember to wear clothes covering your legs and shoulders and remove your shoes.  You have to pay an admission fee.  You are allowed the use of a still/video camera.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Located in the heart of Kandy, this is definitely a 'must see' while in the area.  I would recommend attending the cultural show in the evenings and go during the scheduled celebrations.  It is believed that the tooth relic of Lord Buddha. The exterior of the temple buildingsa re not magnificant or elaborately decorated, but are still a magnificent sight to see. The interior is righly carved and decorated with gold, ivory, and various woods. The tooth relic is housed in a golden casket shrine enveloped with large elephant tusts and sits on a solid gold lutus flower. Others rooms int he temple include the story of Buddha, pali written on palm leaves, and other historical information.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Unless you have a burning desire to stand in a long queue and be rushed past a tiny window through which, 25 feet away, you can see a small golden urn for less than 10 seconds, I'd give it a miss, particularly at the price now being charged for entry. Given that one of the central beliefs of Buddhists is that all are born equal and should be treated as such, to see the seperate queue of Japanese tourists waiting to enter the relic room itself from which all others are banned was frankly shocking.  This is no longer a place of worship for an ancient religion, but a schmaltzy, over priced tourist trap.  Avoid it and visit a real, local temple.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Kandy (in Singhalese Maha Nuwara means Great City) Kandy the city that is surrounded with beautiful mountains, old buildings & countryside, a sacred lake in the middle of the city, Kandy is also home of the temple of the Buddha’s tooth relic & also prides in Great annual festival (Perehera) that attracts thousands once a year in the months of July or August. It was the Capital of the last Sinhalese kingdom after enduring the Portuguese and Dutch, Kandy somehow fell into the hands of English in 1815. Kandy is a historically rich city. Kandy is used by many travelers as a base to explore ancient cities & hill country. Many travelers arrive straight from Air port to Kandy to organize there tours all around the island. Things to see: •Temple of the Tooth Temple of the tooth holds Sri Lanka’s most important historical object, a sacred tooth of the Buddha. The story goes that this tooth has been taken from Buddha’s Cremation in 543 BC. Then the tooth was smuggled into Sri Lanka in the 4th Centaury AD. The temple was said to have been built in 16th Century. Don’t miss the Udamale (upper storey)-which keeps the relic, Sanctuary, Audience hall and back of the temple is the museum. • Kandy Lake It was built in 1807 by the last king who ruled Kandy. It was known to be the place where queens bathed. The island in the Centre was used as the king’s harem. •Udawathekelle Sanctuary It was known as the “prohibited forests” during the period of the kings of Kandy, It’s Very cool and Pleasant forest; it’s shaded with lots of big trees. There are plenty of monkeys and birds to be seen. Recommended to travel with Guide and not alone. •Kandyan Dancers Every evening there is a Kandyan Dance show (also known as cultural show) and it’s a sight not to miss. The Dance was done during the king’s times as an entertaining show for the kings. However its popularity reduced when the British took over, but now it’s revived and taken on for the stage. The Kandyan Music & the Dresses all are a beauty to watch. •Embekke Is located in a beautiful countryside and popular silver, brass & copper village called Embekke. The temple is built in the 14th Centaury and has a sanctuary, Drummers hall & Dancing hall. The Carvings Include double Headed Eagles, Wrestling men, Dancing women & Swans. •Lankathilake Temple Located on the top of panhalgala.  A Monk has told the king that he had an unusual vision and the king felt he should make a temple there and so it was built. The temple is built in the 14th Centaury. It has a Buddha image, Kandy period Paintings, Elephant figures & Rock face writings. •Gadaladeniya Temple Built on a rocky edge and covered with small rock pools. The temple dates back to Lankathilake temple and the Embekke devala. You could find inscriptions on a rock which dates back to 1345 AD. There’s a stupa & Bodhi tree here. Peradeniya Botanical Gardens It was the 14th century Queens Pleasure gardens, and then became the home of a Prince in the 18th Century.  In 1821 it was changed into Botanical gardens. It’s surrounded from 3 sides by the longest river in Sri Lanka Called “Mahaweli”. The Garden boasts Orchids, and many specializing streets are to be found. Among them you should watch out for the Double coconut Street (each Coconut is around 8 Kg to 20 Kg), Royal Palms Street, and Cannon balls Avenue. Most Names of the plants given on a board next to the plant and you would find around 4000 labeled types.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: Beautifu Place, Kandy. Once you get down from the Vehicle, you at once feel the difference from all the other cities and towns of Sri Lanka. The Temple of the Tooth was really a wonderfil experience. And as I learnt later on, I was really lucky to get a good Driver/Guide in Bandara contactable through writing to cananil@yahoo.com Some of the other Tourists Visiting the place seemed to be rushing out in a hurry and I found out later on that their Guides did not know enough to explain about the Temple of The Tooth, which is actually a part of the Kandy King's Palace. Bandara Explained to me not only about the History of the place itself, but pointed out all the beautiful and old paintings, and the meanings of all of them, and when I thought it was finished, there I am taken to a Museum, and it was like I was experiencing all of that History myself. I really must say that the wood carvings at the place are absolutely superb. And there are still some wood carving places around Kandy, where you can still find the fine work being done in small factories. And don't forget the famous Ceylon Tea, better to buy at a Factory, it is really fresh there. Bye for now!

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: for buddist`s this is one of their most sacred(probably the most sacred)temple in the world.visitors are welcome and even as  a non-buddhist as long as you follow  some basic ettiquette your visit   should be enjoyable. we had a guide for our trips around kandy but he told us that guided walks for groups(there were 6 of us) around the temple are not allowed(discouraged?) but he dropped us off by the lake and gave us a rough outline of what to do and where to go. firstly the correct attire should be worn.legs should be covered,so long trousers for men and ladies skirts should come well below the knee(although a sarong wrapped over shorts is acceptable for both)and no bare shoulders. security is tight as the temple has been subject to a number of attacks-most recently by the tamil tigers(ltte) in 1998-so be prepared for a bodysearch and scrutiny of large bags etc.best bet is to travel light.next remove shoes at the shoe collection point after security(a small gratuity when you pick them up will not go amiss). the best time to go to the temple is in the evening during the `auspicious time` when the casket holding the tooth is exposed(i think it is at 7 pm) if you there at this time head left up the stairs from the main area and join the line of waiting  people.the casket is viewed through a series of doors and you will have only a few moments to view it. towards the back of the temple a room houses the story of the tooth and a number of statues-worth a visit. when we were there in 2007 there was no problem with taking photographs and using a camcorder,however it is reguarded as extremely bad manners to be photographed with you back to a statue of the buddha(but you can stand in profile) so please act with respect and enjoy.buddhist`s are normally very easygoing but i saw a security guard go absolutely ballistic with a spanish teenage girl who had wrapped her shawl haphazardly round her neck and under her arm exposing both shoulders- so be warned.

location_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
review_text: We had a wonderful holiday in Sri Lanka with our trip guide, but amongst all the very beautiful places we went the tooth temple has to be one of the highlights of the trip. It was enlightening and very special to see the temple, we had a guide around the temple who was very good in telling us all the history and what goes on in the temple. My son who is only 5 years old also enjoyed it and was very interested so in my books it was more than worth the visit. I would advise anyone who is planning to take a trip to Sri Lanka to go visit the temple it will be so worthwhile.
